news.body: Brian Thomas Jr. (shoulder) is questionable to return for the Jacksonville Jaguars against the Cleveland Browns.
news.impact: Thomas Jr. suffered the apparent shoulder injury in the second quarter of the Week 1 contest, hauling in all three of his targets for 40 yards prior to exiting.

news.head: Brian Thomas Jr. (shoulder) without injury designation for Sunday
news.body: Brian Thomas Jr. (shoulder) is without an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Cleveland Browns.
news.impact: The young wideout's shoulder injury is no longer an issue and he carries no injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Browns. He won't be limited at all, but it remains to be seen how big of a role he will play in Jacksonville's offense in 2026.

news.head: Brian Thomas Jr. (shoulder) practicing in full
news.body: Brian Thomas Jr. (shoulder) has been practicing in full this week.
news.impact: Thomas has been limited by a shoulder injury recently, but he was back to full practice activity on Tuesday. The third-year wideout should be good to go for Week 1.

news.head: TreVeyon Henderson returning to practice on Monday
news.body: TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) is returning to practice on Monday.
news.impact: Henderson missed the Patriots game against Seattle on Wednesday, but is hopefully going to make his return to the field for Week 2. Should he play, it will be interesting to see how things are divvied up between him and Rhamondre Stevenson. Stevenson wasn't particularly efficient at first glance, but looking deeper, he had to do a lot of work after contact, so his box score might not be as bad as thought.

news.head: TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) ruled out for Week 1
news.body: TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) has been ruled out for Week 1 for the New England Patriots against the Seattle Seahawks according to Ari Meirov.
news.impact: Henderson will miss the season opener after being unable to practice to begin the week for head coach Mike Vrabel. Rhamondre Stevenson will see as many touches as he can handle against a strong Seattle front seven Wednesday night.

news.head: TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) officially misses practice Monday
news.body: TreVeyon Henderson missed practice again on Monday.
news.impact: Henderson continues to trend towards missing Wednesday’s season opener.

news.head: TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) not seen practicing Monday
news.body: TreVeyon Henderson was not seen practicing on Monday.
news.impact: Henderson continues to trend towards likely being sidelined for Wednesday’s season opener. Rhamondre Stevenson should open the season in a workhorse role.

news.head: Ja'Marr Chase very quiet to open season
news.body: Ja'Marr Chase caught 2-of-4 targets for 12 yards in the Bengals 33-27 win over the Buccaneers.
news.impact: It was a Week 1 to forget for Chase fantasy managers to say the least. There shouldn't be too much of concern after one week, though he draws an even tougher matchup in Week 2 against the Texans.

news.head: Ja’Marr Chase (knee) cleared for Week 1
news.body: Ja’Marr Chase (knee) has been cleared to play in Week 1 for the Cincinnati Bengals against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers according to Kelsey Conway.

news.head: Ja'Marr Chase (knee) logs full practice Thursday
news.body: Ja'Marr Chase (knee) logged another full practice session on Thursday.
news.impact: As expected, Chase was able to log yet another full practice session on Thursday. He is trending towards being a full go for the season opener on Sunday, assuming there are no unforeseen setbacks between now and then. He will be a top-tier fantasy option if active in Week 1 and beyond.

news.head: Ja'Marr Chase (knee) practices in full Wednesday
news.body: Ja'Marr Chase (knee) practiced in a full capacity on Wednesday.
news.impact: Chase was able to log a full practice session on Wednesday and is considered close to full health, if not already fully healthy heading into Week 1. He should be a full go against the Buccaneers and projects to be an elite fantasy option in the season opener and beyond.

news.head: Matthew Stafford quiet in loss to Niners
news.body: Matthew Stafford completed 15-of-25 passes for 155 yards and a pick in the Rams' 27-7 blowout loss to the 49ers. He also ran twice for a loss of a yard.
news.impact: Stafford was not in his best form on Thursday, missing throws and looking a little rusty. It's a rough start for a team that was deemed Super Bowl-bound, but he will look to get back on track next week.

news.head: Matthew Stafford expected to have reps managed in training camp
news.body: The Rams are expected to limit the reps for Matthew Stafford in training camp.
news.impact: Stafford’s degenerative back issue cost him almost all of training camp last year, and he went on to have an MVP season. He is expected to have load managment once again throughout training camp as he enters another season.

news.head: Matthew Stafford agrees to one-year, $55 million extension
news.body: Matthew Stafford has agreed to a one-year, $55 million extension with the Rams. He is now under contract for LA for the next two seasons.
news.impact: The Rams are in a Super Bowl window, so this is hardly a surprising move. Stafford will give them the boost they need off of an MVP season to help them continue to compete for the next two years. As for Ty Simpson, it looks like he will be on the Jordan Love trajectory where we will need to wait at least two years to really get a shot as a starter.

news.head: Matthew Stafford, Rams deep in contract extension talks
news.body: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports that Matthew Stafford and the Rams are “deep” in contract extension talks.
news.impact: Rapoport added that the Rams believe there is a “real chance” Stafford plays beyond the 2026 season. This comes the day after they invested the No. 13 overall pick on Ty Simpson. It appears he is likely to be sitting multiple years behind Stafford.

news.head: Malik Nabers hauls in six passes Sunday
news.body: Malik Nabers hauled in 6-of-9 targets for 69 yards in Sunday night's 28-20 win over the Dallas Cowboys.
news.impact: Sunday night marked Nabers' first game back after being off the field for nearly a year due to a serious knee injury. He looked pretty good in his first game back, totaling 69 yards and leading the team in targets en route to a big win over the Cowboys. Fantasy managers should be optimistic that he will return to full form in the near future, assuming he suffers no further setbacks.

news.head: Malik Nabers (knee) active for Week 1
news.body: Malik Nabers (knee) is officially active for Week 1 for the New York Giants against the Dallas Cowboys according to Mike Garafolo.

news.head: Malik Nabers (knee) game-time decision for Week 1
news.body: Malik Nabers (knee) will be a game-time decision for the Week 1 contest between the New York Giants against the Dallas Cowboys Sunday night according to Adam Schefter.
news.impact: Nabers continues to work back from a severe knee injury suffered during the 2025-26 season and could potentially leave head coach John Harbaugh without his top pass-catching option in a key Week 1 divisional matchup. Fantasy managers will need to have another option ready to plug into lineups whether it be in one of the earlier kickoff windows Sunday or an available option in the Monday night contest between the Kansas City Chiefs and Denver Broncos.

news.head: Malik Nabers (knee) officially questionable Sunday
news.body: Malik Nabers is listed as questionable for Sunday’s game against the Cowboys.
news.impact: The reports all week have suggested Nabers is expected to be good to go for Sunday's season opener. He should be on the favorable side of questionable going into the weekend.

news.head: Alec Pierce suffers hand/wrist bruise, expected to be fine
news.body: Colts head coach Shane Steichen said Alec Pierce’s left hand/wrist is fine.
news.impact: Pierce said he is dealing with a bruise. His status will need to be monitored in practice this week.

news.head: Alec Pierce leads pass-catchers in Week 1 loss
news.body: Alec Pierce hauled in four of his team-leading six targets for 61 yards in the Colts' 41-23 loss to the Ravens in Week 1.
news.impact: Pierce was impactful for head coach Shane Steichen while operating on a snap count, leading the Colts in targets and receiving yards in a losing effort. The wideout remains an impactful pass-catching option ahead of a tough Week 2 matchup against the Kansas City Chiefs.

news.head: Alec Pierce (heel) on snap count for Week 1
news.body: Alec Pierce (heel) will operate on a snap count in Week 1 for the Indianapolis Colts against the Baltimore Ravens according to Mike Garafolo.
news.impact: Pierce is in line for 20-60 plays according to Garafolo as the wideout continues to work back towards full health after a late start to his preseason activities for the Colts. Tight end Tyler Warren alongside wideouts Keenan Allen and Josh Downs will likely see increased targets from quarterback Daniel Jones against the Ravens Sunday.

news.head: Alec Pierce (heel) off injury report Sunday
news.body: Alec Pierce is off the injury report for Sunday's game against the Ravens.
news.impact: Pierce is not expected to face a snap count. He is fresh off his contract extension this offseason.

news.head: Omarion Hampton finds the end zone in Week 1 loss
news.body: Omarion Hampton rushed for 43 yards and a touchdown on 12 carries in Sunday's 26-14 loss to the Cardinals.
news.impact: A first-round pick in 2025, Hampton carried quite a bit of hype coming into his second NFL season, as did the Chargers' offense as a whole. At least some of that hype immediately died down after a disappointing season debut against a suspect Arizona defense, but it is only one game under new OC Mike McDaniel. Hampton found the end zone on an eight-yard run in the opening quarter, and this Chargers' attack will find its footing at some point. The Raiders are up next.

news.head: Omarion Hampton (ankle) will not practice Wednesday
news.body: Omarion Hampton is not practicing on Wednesday.
news.impact: Hampton is “working through it” and “doing everything he can” to get the ankle better that sidelined him in Week 18. He should still play in the Wild Card round against the Patriots, but it is possible he's still fighting through the injury.

news.head: Omarion Hampton (ankle) ruled out for Week 18
news.body: Omarion Hampton has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Broncos.
news.impact: Hampton will be one of several starters sitting for the Chargers. Kimani Vidal could lead the backfield if he is cleared.

news.head: Omarion Hampton (ankle) misses practice Thursday
news.body: Omarion Hampton did not practice on Thursday.
news.impact: Hampton is likely to sit the regular season finale on Sunday. Kimani Vidal could open the game as the lead back, but it remains unclear how long he may play.

news.head: Michael Pittman Jr. goes for 58 yards in Week 1
news.body: Michael Pittman Jr. caught all three of his targets for 58 yards in a 20-13 win over the Falcons in Week 1.
news.impact: Pittman led the Steelers in receiving despite only seeing three targets. It was a slightly concerning Pittsburgh debut for the veteran, as DK Metcalf easily dominated in the target category, drawing 10. Pittman will be a fantasy flex option heading into Week 2 against the Patriots but should be on the bench if there are better starting options available.

news.head: Michael Pittman Jr. (hamstring) good to go for Sunday
news.body: Michael Pittman Jr. (hamstring) is good to go for Sunday's game against the Atlanta Falcons.
news.impact: Pittman is now fully recovered from the hamstring injury he was dealing with earlier and is set to be a full go against the Falcons on Sunday. He shouldn't be started in most league formats but remains an intriguing player to watch and evaluate in his first game as a member of his new team.

news.head: Michael Pittman Jr. (hamstring) practices Monday
news.body: Michael Pittman Jr. practiced on Monday.
news.impact: Pittman missed time during training camp with a hamstring injury. He remains on track to be good to go for Sunday's season opener against the Falcons.

news.head: Michael Pittman Jr. will be available Week 1
news.body: Steelers GM Omar Khan announced WR Michael Pittman Jr. will be available for Week 1.
news.impact: Pittman has been dealing with a hamstring injury, but will still suit up in Week 1. He slots in as a low-end flex play in his Steelers debut against the Falcons.

news.head: Jameson Williams sees nine targets in Week 1 win
news.body: Jameson Williams caught four of his nine targets for 45 yards in the Lions' 31-30 win over the New Orleans Saints in Week 1.
news.impact: Williams would have offered even more of an explosive impact if not for a couple of deep throw drops on passes from quarterback Jared Goff. The wideout remains a high-impact, explosive pass-catching option for fantasy managers ahead of a Week 2 road contest against the Buffalo Bills.

news.head: Jameson Williams (shoulder) returns to practice
news.body: Jameson Williams resumed practicing on Wednesday.
news.impact: Williams missed the Lions’ last two practices. He made his way back on Wednesday.

news.head: Jameson Williams catches six passes in Week 18
news.body: Jameson Williams hauled in six passes for 74 yards during Detroit's 19-16 win over Chicago in the final game of the year.
news.impact: It was the sixth time this season that Williams caught at least six balls in a game. The third-year wideout continues to improve production as he established career-highs in receptions (65) and receiving yards (1,117) while tying a career-best with seven receiving touchdowns.

news.head: Jameson Williams sees three targets in Week 17 loss
news.body: Jameson Williams hauled in two of his three targets for 37 yards in the Lions' 23-10 Week 17 loss to the Vikings.
news.impact: Williams was one of many underperforming options in the Detroit offense, finishing with less than five receptions and nine targets for the first time in his last five games. The speedy wideout remains one of quarterback Jared Goff's primary pass-catching options, with a Week 18 contest against the Chicago Bears up next.

news.head: MarShawn Lloyd sees 13 carries Sunday
news.body: MarShawn Lloyd ran for 37 yards on 13 carries in the Packers 39-22 loss against the Vikings. He did not catch his lone target.
news.impact: Lloyd was the lead back in the Packers backfield without Josh Jacobs. He was very inefficient as he averaged less than three yards per carry. He'll be a flex play next week against the Jets.

news.head: MarShawn Lloyd will play in preseason
news.body: Packers OC Adam Stenavich confirmed that MarShawn Lloyd will play in the preseason.
news.impact: Stenavich said every day Lloyd is able to practice, he gets more confident his injury issues are fully behind him. He is competing the backup role in the Packers backfield.

news.head: MarShawn Lloyd to be ramped up in training camp
news.body: MarShawn Lloyd is expected to be ramped up early in training camp.
news.impact: Packers coach Matt LaFleur said Lloyd doesn't necessarily have a rep count in camp, but learning from past the plan is to "gradually" ramp him up for season. He'll compete for the backup role in training camp.

news.head: MarShawn Lloyd receives second-team reps Tuesday
news.body: MarShawn Lloyd received reps with the second-team in practice on Tuesday.
news.impact: Josh Jacobs was back with the team taking first-team reps at practice on Tuesday. Lloyd was back after he was absent last week.

news.head: Chase Brown finds the end zone Sunday
news.body: Chase Brown ran for 56 yards and a touchdown on 16 carries in the Bengals 33-27 win over the Buccaneers. He also caught 5-of-6 targets for 22 yards receiving.
news.impact: Brown did not have the most efficient afternoon, but it still got the job done for fantasy managers. He draws a tougher matchup in Week 2 against the Texans.

news.head: Chase Brown, Bengals in talks on extension
news.body: The Bengals and RB Chase Brown are reportedly in talks on an extension.
news.impact: Brown finished the season strong this past year after a rough first half. He is entering the final year of his rookie contract next season, which would make sense for both sides.

news.head: Chase Brown catches touchdown in loss
news.body: Chase Brown ran 13 times for 72 yards and caught four of six targets for 18 yards and a touchdown in the Bengals' 20-18 loss to the Browns.
news.impact: Brown closed the 2025 season with a nice fantasy day, totaling 90 scrimmage yards and a score. He struggled early on this season but rounded into form as time went on, and should be a low-end RB1, high-end RB2 for 2026.

news.head: Chase Brown (illness) returns to practice
news.body: Chase Brown (illness) was back at practice on Friday.
news.impact: Brown missed the previous two days of practice due to being under the weather, but the Bengals lead ball carrier returned Friday. He should be ready to roll for Sunday's seas finale against the Browns.

news.head: Tyler Warren finds end zone in Week 1 loss
news.body: Tyler Warren hauled in three of his five targets for 13 yards and one touchdown in a 41-23 Week 1 loss to the Baltimore Ravens.
news.impact: Warren was mostly bottled up by a stiff Baltimore defense, averaging 4.3 yards per reception in the Week 1 loss. The tight end remains a primary pass-catching offense for head coach Shane Steichen ahead of a Week 2 contest against the Kansas City Chiefs.

news.head: Tyler Warren (groin) practices Tuesday
news.body: Tyler Warren was able to practice on Tuesday.
news.impact: Warren has been working his way back from a minor groin issue. He should be good to go for Week 1 next week.

news.head: Tyler Warren (groin) not practicing Wednesday
news.body: Tyler Warren did not practice on Wednesday.
news.impact: Warren remains likely to miss practice all of this week as he recovers from a groin injury. His status for Week 1 is not in danger yet if he can return to practice by next week.

news.head: Tyler Warren (groin) may miss practice this week
news.body: Tyler Warren (groin) may be sidelined at practice all week.
news.impact: Indianapolis' star tight end is in the process of recovering from a groin injury right now. It's possible that he will be sidelined at practice all week, but he is still expected to be a full go for Week 1, so fantasy managers shouldn't read too much into his status at this point.

news.head: Josh Jacobs has court appearance date moved up
news.body: Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs had his initial court appearance moved up to Sept. 10 from Nov. 17 regarding Jacobs' misdemeanor charges.
news.impact: Jacobs was charged with battery and criminal destruction of property and is scheduled to appear at the Brown County courthouse on Sept. 10, multiple days before Green Bay's season opener against Minnesota. It is unclear how this will affect his return timeline; Jacobs is currently on the commissioner's exempt list, with a potential suspension looming.

news.head: Josh Jacobs expected to play for Packers in 2026 per GM
news.body: Packers GM Brian Gutekunst said he expected Josh Jacobs to play for the team in 2026.
news.impact: Gutekunst said he wants to let the process play out when asked if there’s a scenario in which the Packers release Jacobs. He was placed on the Commissioners Exempt List on Sunday. This will remain a situation to monitor.

news.head: Josh Jacobs placed on commissioner of exempt list
news.body: Josh Jacobs has been placed on the commissioner exempt list by the National Football League according to Tom Pelissero.
news.impact: Jacobs is now ineligible to practice or play for the Packers while the league continues their investigation into alleged improper behavior while being charged with two misdemeanors related to his conduct earlier in the week. If the running back is forced to sit out for any period of the regular season, MarShawn Lloyd will be in line to receive the majority of backfield work while the recently acquired Kaleb Johnson gets up to speed on the offensive playbook with Week 1 approaching.

news.head: Josh Jacobs charged with two misdemeanors stemming from May incident
news.body: Josh Jacobs has been charged with two misdemeanors following an incident in May. His initial court date is set for mid-November. The NFL is conducting its own investigation, and a suspension could soon follow.
news.impact: It's important to remember that the NFL has the ability to either suspend Jacobs at the start of the season or wait until the legal process is over. If they wait, then Jacobs will likely not face suspension until next year. If not, we could be looking at a potential 6-8 game absence, though that is more of an educated guess at this point. For anyone taking Jacobs in drafts right now, Marshawn Lloyd is a must-have handcuff and is a great target for Zero-RB builds.

news.head: Dak Prescott underwhelming in loss Sunday
news.body: Dak Prescott completed 22-of-34 passing attempts for 175 yards, two touchdowns, and one interception in Sunday night's 28-20 loss to the New York Giants.
news.impact: Prescott didn't deliver a great performance on Sunday night. He was held to under 200 passing yards against the Giants and lost one turnover in Dallas' loss to their divisional rival. He will have a good opportunity to bounce back next week against the Commanders, but this is not the type of performance fantasy managers wanted to see out of him in the season opener.

news.head: Dak Prescott, Cowboys starters will not play in preseason
news.body: Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer said he won’t play starters in the preseason.
news.impact: Schottenheimer said he broke up all players into four groups for preseason playing time. The A group plays zero snaps, B+ group plays 10-15 snaps, B- group plays 20-25 snaps and the C group plays unlimited snaps. We'll get our first look at Dak Prescott and the Cowboys starters in Week 1 against the Giants.

news.head: Dak Prescott (knee) limited in practice Tuesday
news.body: Dak Prescott was limited in practice during minicamp on Tuesday.
news.impact: Prescott took four reps in team drills when he would normally would’ve had eight. It does not appear to be anything serious that he is dealing with after he was expected to be limited.

news.head: Dak Prescott has contract restructured by Cowboys
news.body: The Cowboys restructured the contract of Dak Prescott.
news.impact: Prescott, Tyler Smith and CeeDee Lamb all had their contracts restructured to help create a significant amount of capital space for the Cowboys. They are now under the cap heading into free agency.

news.head: DJ Moore goes for 100 yards in win over Houston
news.body: DJ Moore caught 5 of 8 targets for 100 yards and a touchdown in the Bills’ 36-31 win over the Texans.
news.impact: Moore looked good and re-invigorated in this game, showing off some of his old self against a Houston defense that didn’t look like its normal self. His touchdown was a bit fluky, as the defensive back solely made a play on the ball and failed do to so, leaving no one around Moore while he walked in for a score. But, fantasy managers won’t be complaining. Next up for DJ are the Detroit Lions, who just allowed big days for Chris Olave and Devaughn Vele on Sunday.

news.head: DJ Moore avoids serious ankle injury Saturday
news.body: Bills coach Joe Brady said DJ Moore was “good to go” after suffering an ankle injury in Saturday’s preseason game against the Panthers.
news.impact: Moore appeared to have his ankle rolled up on after a catch and run. He hauled in 3-of-4 targets for 61 yards in his first official game with the Bills and Josh Allen.

news.head: DJ Moore will play in preseason opener
news.body: Bills HC Joe Brady said starters will play against the Panthers in the preseason opener.
news.impact: Moore has seemingly had an excellent camp. The WR will now have the opportunity to showcase it against his former team in the preseason alongside Josh Allen and the starters.

news.head: DJ Moore admits to 'growing pains' in Buffalo, confident it will be better
news.body: Bills WR DJ Moore admitted to "growing pains" in Buffalo early on, but he remains confident "it's gonna be perfect later."
news.impact: "I mean, it's gonna be perfect later on, but right now it's still growing pains," Moore said earlier in the week during OTAs. He was traded to Buffalo this offseason after three years in Chicago. He'll remain a player fantasy managers will want to monitor heading into minicamp and training camp.

news.head: Zay Flowers (hamstring) considered day-to-day
news.body: Ravens coach Jesse Minter said WR Zay Flowers is considered day-to-day with a hamstring injury.
news.impact: It is a good sign after Flowers left Sunday's game early after a very strong first half. His status for Week 2 still remains uncertain.

news.head: Zay Flowers (hamstring) ruled out Sunday
news.body: Zay Flowers (hamstring) has been ruled out for the remainder of the Week 1 contest between the Baltimore Ravens and Indianapolis Colts according to Mike Garafolo.
news.impact: Flowers had been sidelined since the second quarter while attempting to work through the hamstring injury an return for head coach Jesse Minter, hauling in five of his six targets for 150 receiving yards and one touchdown on the day.

news.head: Zay Flowers (hamstring) questionable to return Sunday
news.body: Zay Flowers (hamstring) is questionable to return for the Baltimore Ravens against the Indianapolis Colts Sunday the organization announced.
news.impact: Flowers was off to a dynamic start before leaving in the second quarter for head coach Jesse Minter, hauling in five of his six targets for 150 receiving yards and one touchdown prior to exiting. Rashod Bateman and Ja’Kobi Lane would see increased targets if the superstar wideout remains sidelined in the second half for the Ravens.

news.head: Zay Flowers (hamstring) off injury report Sunday
news.body: Zay Flowers is off the injury report for Sunday's game against the Colts.
news.impact: Flowers missed some practice time in the past couple of weeks with a hamstring injury. He'll be a full-go heading into the season off a new contract.

news.head: Jaxon Smith-Njigba electric in win Wednesday
news.body: Jaxon Smith-Njigba caught 8-of-11 targets for 122 yards and a touchdown in Wednesday night's 13-10 win over the New England Patriots.
news.impact: On Wednesday, Smith-Njigba picked up right where he left off last season, exploding for 122 yards and a touchdown in a big win over the Patriots. He did that with Drew Lock throwing him passes after starter Sam Darnold went down with a hip injury earlier in the game. Fantasy managers should be happy with his performance in this matchup but should keep a close eye on the health of Darnold, as the young wideout's week-to-week ceiling will certainly take a hit if their starting QB misses significant time.

news.head: Jaxon Smith-Njigba signs historic four-year extension with Seahawks
news.body: The Seahawks signed WR Jaxon Smith-Njigba to a four-year, $168.6 million contract extension.
news.impact: Smith-Njigba signs the richest contract extension for a receiver in NFL history with the deal including $120 million in guaranteed money. The 2025 NFL Offensive Player of the Year and Super Bowl Champion went for 1,793 yards and 10 touchdowns on 119 receptions last season. He will remain under contract with the Seahawks through the 2031 season.

news.head: Jaxon Smith-Njigba has fifth-year team option exercised by Seahawks
news.body: The Seahawks exercised WR Jaxon Smith-Njigba’s fifth-year team option for 2027.
news.impact: Henderson added that Smith-Njigba’s 2027 salary is fully guaranteed and should make him roughly $23.85 million. This is expected to be a step towards the two sides agreeing to a long-term extension.

news.head: Jaxon Smith-Njigba off injury report for Super Bowl
news.body: Jaxon Smith-Njigba is off the injury report for the Super Bowl against the Patriots.
news.impact: Smith-Njigba closed the week with a full practice on Friday. He is officially a full-go heading into the big game on Sunday.

news.head: Jahmyr Gibbs leads backfield attack in Week 1 win over Saints
news.body: Jahmyr Gibbs carried the ball 29 times for 156 yards and two touchdowns while also hauling in all five of his targets for 30 yards in the Lions' 31-30 Week 1 win over the New Orleans Saints.
news.impact: Gibbs was dynamic out of the backfield for head coach Dan Campbell, averaging 5.4 yards per carry in the win. The running back remains an explosive RB1 option in all formats, with a Week 2 road matchup against the Buffalo Bills up next.

news.head: Jahmyr Gibbs agrees to 3-year, $67.5 million deal with Lions
news.body: Jahmyr Gibbs has agreed to 3-year, $67.5 million deal with Lions that could be worth up to $75.75 million. Gibbs is now the NFL’s highest paid running back.
news.impact: Gibbs has done everything he needs to to earn this money. He’s a premier running back in the NFL, in the argument for the best. Now with David Montgomery gone, we will see how well he can shoulder a workhorse role, and fantasy managers are rightly expecting big things.

news.head: Jahmyr Gibbs does not practice Wednesday amid contract talks with Lions
news.body: Jahmyr Gibbs did not practice on Wednesday amid contract talks with the Lions.
news.impact: Gibbs has two years left on his rookie deal but is currently eligible for an extension. Gibbs could earn more than $20 million per year based on previous reports. This will remain a situation to monitor as Gibbs holds in to begin training camp.

news.head: Jahmyr Gibbs in position to 'reset running back market'
news.body: Jeremy Fowler reports that Jahmyr Gibbs is positioned to reset the running back market in a big way.
news.impact: Fowler expects Gibbs to earn at least $20 million per year when he lands a new deal. He had his fifth-year option exercised back in April.

news.head: Matthew Golden totals 95 yards Sunday
news.body: Matthew Golden caught 6-of-12 targets for 95 yards in the Packers 39-22 loss against the Vikings.
news.impact: After a lost rookie season, Golden opened this year leading Green Bay receivers in targets on Sunday. He is in the WR3/WR4 mix heading into Week 2 for fantasy managers.

news.head: Matthew Golden (toe) returns to practice Tuesday
news.body: Matthew Golden was back at practice at Packers training camp on Tuesday.
news.impact: Golden makes his way back after missing a few days of practice. He was spotted running with the Green Bay first team offense on Tuesday.

news.head: Matthew Golden (toe) not expected to practice Monday
news.body: Packers coach Matt LaFleur said he does not expect WR Matthew Golden to practice on Monday.
news.impact: Golden also missed practice on Sunday. He remains day-to-day. It is unknown how serious his injury is.

news.head: Matthew Golden (toe) not practicing Sunday
news.body: Matthew Golden did not practice on Sunday due to a toe injury.
news.impact: It is unclear how serious the injury is for Golden. He is day-to-day going into the week. There should be an update provided by coach Matt LaFleur when available.

news.head: Terry McLaurin quiet in Week 1 loss to Eagles
news.body: Terry McLaurin caught two of his four targets for 14 yards in the Commanders’ 24-22 Week 1 loss to the Philadelphia Eagles.
news.impact: McLaurin was one of the more underwhelming options as part of a disappointing Washington aerial attack in the season opener, averaging 7.0 yards per reception in the loss. The wideout will look to get back on track in Week 2 against a Dallas Cowboys that struggled to slow down the New York Giants in Week 1.

news.head: Terry McLaurin expected to play against Lions
news.body: Commanders WR Terry McLaurin is set to start against the Lions on Saturday.
news.impact: McLaurin enters the fantasy football season as a top-50 selection. He and Jayden Daniels will have an opportunity to build momentum ahead of the regular season.

news.head: Terry McLaurin catches four passes in season finale
news.body: Terry McLaurin caught all four of his targets for 57 yards in a 24-17 win over the Eagles in Week 18.
news.impact: McLaurin finished as the Commanders' receiving leader in the season-ender. The veteran did not live up to expectations in 2025, appearing in just 10 games due to injury. He wound up with just 38 catches for 582 yards and three touchdowns along the way. McLaurin is a candidate to post a bounce-back season for Washington in 2026.

news.head: Terry McLaurin hauls in five receptions in Week 17 loss to Cowboys
news.body: Terry McLaurin hauled in five of his seven targets for 63 yards in the Commanders' 30-23 Week 17 loss to the Cowboys.
news.impact: McLaurin has made an impact in the Washington passing attack when called upon, logging six or more targets in three of his last five games. The wideout will look to finish an injury-riddled season on a positive note in Week 18 against the Philadelphia Eagles.

news.head: Tee Higgins totals 59 yards Sunday
news.body: Tee Higgins caught 3-of-6 targets for 59 yards in the Bengals 33-27 win over the Buccaneers.
news.impact: It could have been worse. You could have Ja'Marr Chase catching two passes for 12 yards. It wasn't the most inspiring start to the season for Higgins, but he still had a couple of big catches. He'll remain an upside WR2 heading into Week 2 against the Texans.

news.head: Tee Higgins (foot) cleared for Week 1
news.body: Tee Higgins (foot) is cleared to play in Week 1 for the Cincinnati Bengals against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers according to Kelsey Conway.

news.head: Tee Higgins (foot) practices in full again Thursday
news.body: Tee Higgins (foot) practiced in a full capacity again on Thursday.
news.impact: The Bengals will likely have Higgins for their season opener on Sunday, as he has been a full participant at two-straight practices to start the week. Fantasy managers should feel confident starting him if he's fully cleared to play prior to kickoff against the Buccaneers.

news.head: Tee Higgins (foot) fully participates in practice Wednesday
news.body: Tee Higgins (foot) fully participated in Cincinnati's practice on Wednesday.
news.impact: Higgins is still listed on Cincinnati's injury report due to a nagging foot injury, but it's not a serious issue at this point and he was able to log a full practice session on Wednesday. He should be good to go for Week 1 and projects to be a good fantasy option against the Buccaneers.

news.head: Jaylen Waddle disappoints in Broncos debut Monday
news.body: Jaylen Waddle caught 1-of-3 targets for just two yards in Monday night's 31-10 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs.
news.impact: There has been a lot of hype for the veteran wideout after the Broncos traded for him this offseason, but he got off to a poor start with his new team on Monday night. He caught one pass for just two yards over the course of the game, which burned any fantasy manager who risked starting him in this matchup. Denver's offense as a whole struggled heavily against Kansas City's defense, however, so there's a good chance that he and the rest of the offense bounce back and return to solid fantasy production in easier matchups moving forward.

news.head: Jaylen Waddle (leg) in full pads at practice Tuesday
news.body: Jaylen Waddle is in full pads at practice on Tuesday.
news.impact: It is another positive sign for Waddle following his return to practice on Monday. He remains on track to be good to go for the start of the regular season.

news.head: Jaylen Waddle (leg) returns to practice Monday
news.body: Jaylen Waddle returned to practice on Monday after dealing with a leg muscle strain.
news.impact: Waddle missed practice all of last week, but has now returned to action at the start of this week. The wideout should still be monitored throughout the week to see if an injury pops back up.

news.head: Jaylen Waddle (muscle strain) not practicing Wednesday
news.body: Jaylen Waddle remained absent from practice on Wednesday.
news.impact: Waddle is likely to miss practice all week. He is sidelined with a muscle strain.

news.head: Hunter Henry hauls in three passes Wednesday
news.body: Hunter Henry caught three passes for 26 yards in Wednesday's 13-10 loss to the Seattle Seahawks.
news.impact: New England's offense wasn't very effective on Wednesday night, and Henry was no exception to that. He totaled just 26 scoreless yards against the Seahawks, which left him with a poor fantasy total. His value as a streaming option may be diminished this year with Eli Raridon seemingly primed to be more involved at the tight end position for the Patriots.

news.head: Hunter Henry agrees to two year extension with Patriots
news.body: Hunter Henry has agreed to a two year extension with the New England Patriots. He had one year left remaining on his contract, but is now locked in till the end of 2028.
news.impact: It’s great news for Henry managers, but bad news for Eli Raridon truthers. The rookie and promising young tight end could still break out as Henry ages out, but this certainly puts a damper on his prospects in the short term. But getting back to Henry, he should be a solid target later in fantasy drafts this year.

news.head: Hunter Henry (rest) listed as questionable for Super Bowl
news.body: Hunter Henry is listed as questionable for the Super Bowl next Sunday against the Seahawks.
news.impact: Henry closed the week with a full practice on Friday. He should be good to go heading into next week.

news.head: Hunter Henry (rest) limited in practice Thursday
news.body: Hunter Henry was limited in practice on Thursday.
news.impact: Henry is continuing to be managed in practice. He'll be a full-go heading into the Super Bowl next week.

news.head: Joe Burrow not at best Sunday
news.body: Joe Burrow completed 25-of-35 passes for 254 yards with one touchdown and one interception in the Bengals 33-27 win over the Buccaneers on Sunday.
news.impact: While Cincinnati won the game, Burrow did not have the most inspiring of performances for fantasy managers. That included a pick-six. He will face the Texans defense in Week 2.

news.head: Joe Burrow, Bengals starters will not play in preseason finale
news.body: The Bengals starters will not play in Friday’s preseason finale against the Eagles.
news.impact: We will see Joe Burrow and the starters for Cincinnati back on the field in Week 1 against the Bucs.

news.head: Joe Burrow, Bengals starters set to be sidelined Saturday
news.body: Joe Burrow and Cincinnati's starters are set to be sidelined for Saturday's preseason game against the Chicago Bears.
news.impact: Burrow and many of Cincinnati's starters played in the team's first preseason game last week, but they are going to be sidelined for this week's game against the Bears. It remains to be seen if their starters will take the field for the team's third and final preseason game on August 28.

news.head: Joe Burrow, Bengals starters to play in preseason opener
news.body: The Bengals starters will play in their preseason opener against the Lions.
news.impact: It likely won't be more than one or two series for the starters, but we'll at least get a glimpse at seeing them play.

news.head: Kenny Gainwell uninvolved Sunday
news.body: Kenny Gainwell ran for 15 yards on five carries in the Buccaneers 33-27 loss against the Bengals on Sunday. He also caught his line target for three yards receiving.
news.impact: This felt like the perfect time for Gainwell to make an impact with Tampa Bay falling behind 21-3 early, but it was Bucky Irving in the passing game out of the backfield who caught seven passes. Gainwell is a risky flex play for now in PPR leagues until we see him more involved.

news.head: Kenny Gainwell (personal) not practicing Friday, expected back Sunday
news.body: Kenny Gainwell is not practicing on Friday due to personal reasons.
news.impact: It is an excused absence for Gainwell, who is expected to be back on Sunday. He is competing for a complimentary role alongside Bucky Irving.

news.head: Kenneth Gainwell referred to as '1B running back' by HC Todd Bowles
news.body: Buccaneers coach Todd Bowles referred to Kenneth Gainwell as the team’s 1B running back.
news.impact: The hype on Gainwell has continued since early in the Bucs offseason program. He was also only more noticeable early on with Bucky Irving recovering from an offseason procedure. This will remain a situation to monitor heading into training camp.

news.head: Kenneth Gainwell signs two-year deal with Bucs
news.body: Former Pittsburgh Steelers running back Kenneth Gainwell signed a two-year deal with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers worth $14 million.
news.impact: With Rachaad White's time in Tampa, Fla., likely over, the Buccaneers added another pass-catching back to play behind Bucky Irving. Gainwell had career-high marks in nearly every stat last season, with 1,023 yards and eight touchdowns from scrimmage. He should serve as a strong complement to the Buccaneers' offense.

news.head: DeVonta Smith catches three passes in Week 1 win
news.body: DeVonta Smith caught three of his six targets for 53 yards in the Eagles’ 24-22 Week 1 win over the Washington Commanders.
news.impact: The wideout was mostly held in check despite leading the team in targets, finishing behind tight end Dallas Goedert and No. 2 wideout Dontayvion Wicks in receiving yards on the win. The wideout remains one of the more explosive options in the Philadelphia passing attack, with an opportunity to get back on track against the Tennessee Titans in Week 2 up next.

news.head: DeVonta Smith practicing fully on Monday
news.body: Devonta Smith (hamstring) is practicing fully on Monday for the first time in three weeks. He returned in a limited fashion recently, but he is back to fully participating.
news.impact: It’s great news for Smith as he works his way back from a hamstring injury. This should be the all the confidence boost fantasy managers needed to continue targeting him highly in drafts.

news.head: DeVonta Smith (hamstring) officially limited Thursday
news.body: DeVonta Smith (hamstring) was officially a limited participant at practice on Thursday.
news.impact: Smith is still in the process of recovering from a hamstring injury, but he was able to take part in Thursday's joint practice with New England in a limited capacity. It seems like his recover is going well, and unless there's a setback of some kind, it looks like he will be fully healthy in time for the season opener.

news.head: DeVonta Smith (hamstring) returns to practice Monday
news.body: DeVonta Smith returned to practice on Monday as he continues to deal with a hamstring injury.
news.impact: This is an encouraging sign for Smith, who has missed the last two weeks of camp with a hamstring injury. While he will likely return in a limited capacity early this week, he should be monitored to see how his hamstring responds to being back at practice.

news.head: Drake London held to two catches in Week 1 loss
news.body: Drake London caught two of his four targets for 29 yards in a 20-13 loss to the Steelers in Week 1. He also gained six yards on his lone carry in the game.
news.impact: London was quiet in the close loss, although his 29 receiving yards were good enough for him to finish second on the Falcons in that category. The Falcons were forced to play Cooper Rush, their third-string QB, thanks to injuries, so London should bounce back once either Tua Tagovailoa or Michael Penix is ready to return to the field. London sets up as a low-end WR1 heading into Week 2 against Carolina.

news.head: Drake London: Extension is 'on top of mind' per GM Ian Cunningham
news.body: Falcons GM Ian Cunningham said an extension for Drake London is “on top of mind.”
news.impact: It appears an extension could be agreed to after the NFL Draft. London is entering the final year of his rookie contract. There should be a new deal agreed to at some point later in the offseason.

news.head: Drake London finds the end zone in Week 18
news.body: Drake London caught 4-of-8 targets for 78 yards and a touchdown in the Falcons 19-17 win over the Saints.
news.impact: Despite struggling with Kirk Cousins to end the season, London closed the year on a high note with a touchdown. He missed the 1,000 yard mark after missing five games. He is set to head into the final year of his rookie deal where he should remain a WR1 for fantasy managers.

news.head: Drake London (knee) officially active for Week 18
news.body: Falcons WR Drake London (knee) is officially active for Week 18.
news.impact: London was listed as questionable after being limited in practice this week. He will remain the top pass catcher for Kirk Cousins and the Falcons against the Saints.

news.head: Bucky Irving active in passing game Sunday
news.body: Bucky Irving ran for 45 yards and a touchdown on eight carries in the Buccaneers 33-27 loss against the Bengals on Sunday. He also caught 7-of-7 targets for 48 yards receiving.
news.impact: Irving took advantage of the gamescript in the passing game with Tampa Bay falling behind 21-3 early. He also lost a fumble, but otherwise performed well. He will be an RB2 play next week against the Browns.

news.head: Bucky Irving will be full-go to begin training camp
news.body: Buccaneers coach Todd Bowles said Bucky Irving is “full-go” to begin training camp.
news.impact: Bowles said Irving looked good in practice on Wednesday. He is not being eased into anything. The question going into training camp will be what the split will be between him and Kenneth Gainwell.

news.head: Bucky Irving could see reduced workload to be more effective
news.body: Buccaneers beat reporter Scott Reynolds suggested the team may want to reduce Bucky Irving's workload to allow him to be more effective this season.
news.impact: Reynolds notes that there's a reason why Bucs head coach Todd Bowles has called Irving and Kenneth Gainwell 1A and 1B. The Bucs gave Gainwell a two-year, $14 million deal in free agency and he has reportedly impressed new offensive coordinator Zac Robinson. Gainwell emerged in a big way with the Steelers last season and it appears he could be in line for another similar role in the backfield for Tampa Bay. Irving is expected to be good to go in training camp, but he missed time earlier in the teams offseason program recovering from a shoulder injury.

news.head: Bucky Irving (shoulder) says he will be good to go for training camp
news.body: Bucky Irving said he expects to be "good to go" for training camp.
news.impact: Irving made the statement at his annual youth football camp. He has been limited to start the offseason program working his way back from offseason shoulder surgery after he played through a shoulder injury last season. The Bucs backfield will be a situation to monitor in training camp following their free agency addition of Kenneth Gainwell.

news.head: Breece Hall finds the end zone in Week 1 win
news.body: Breece Hall carried the ball 22 times for 102 yards and a touchdown while catching both of his targets for 16 yards in a 23-10 win over the Titans in Week 1.
news.impact: Hall dealt with a groin issue during camp, but he appeared to be at full health in the Week 1 win. The veteran running back handled the majority of the backfield carries, with Braelon Allen mixing in for 10 totes. Hall found the end zone for the first time of the season on a four-yard rush in the third quarter. He will slot in as a solid RB1 in fantasy heading into a Week 2 home matchup against the Packers.

news.head: Breece Hall (groin) off injury report for Sunday
news.body: Breece Hall (groin) is off of the injury report for Sunday's game against the Tennessee Titans.
news.impact: Hall is heading into the weekend entirely free of any injury designation ahead of the team's season opener against the Titans on Sunday. He shouldn't have any substantial limitations to his workload in this matchup, and he projects to be a high-quality fantasy asset in this game and beyond if he can stay healthy.

news.head: Breece Hall (groin) logs full practice Thursday
news.body: Breece Hall (groin) logged another full practice session on Thursday.
news.impact: Hall has been a full participant in two-straight practices to start the week. He told reporters earlier that will be good to go for Week 1, so fantasy managers shouldn't have any real hesitations with starting him ahead of the first game of the season.

news.head: Breece Hall (groin) says he is good to go Week 1
news.body: Breece Hall told reporters he’s good to go and can handle a full workload if necessary.
news.impact: Hall recently missed a couple of weeks with a strained groin. He added he feels fresh from the time off. He'll be an RB2 for fantasy managers heading into the season.

news.head: Chargers D/ST doesn't accomplish much in Week 1 loss
news.body: The Chargers allowed 26 points on 393 yards of total offense in Sunday's 26-14 loss to the Cardinals.
news.impact: The Chargers did not force a turnover and came up with just one sack in Sunday's season-opening letdown. The L.A. defense did at least provide some friction in the red zone, limiting the Cardinals to two touchdowns in five trips, but this was still a mediocre effort overall. Arizona QB Jacoby Brissett largely picked the Chargers apart with accurate passing from a clean pocket while the Cardinals' running game churned out 116 yards and a touchdown. The Chargers will look to shore things up for a Week 2 matchup with the Raiders.

news.head: Mike McDaniel expected to be named Chargers OC
news.body: The Chargers are expected to name Mike McDaniel their next offensive coordinator.
news.impact: McDaniel had drawn interest from other teams in both a head coach and offensive coordinator role. It was announced earlier on Tuesday that he had taken his name out of the race to be the Cleveland Browns next head coach. He will likely bring a faster-paced offense to the Chargers led by Justin Herbert through the air and Omarion Hampton on the ground. This should lead to more upside for the Chargers offense as a whole heading into next season.

news.head: Chargers D/ST logs four sacks Sunday
news.body: The Chargers' D/ST logged four sacks and allowed 13 points in Sunday's loss to the Denver Broncos.
news.impact: Los Angeles' defense had a sneaky good game on Sunday, allowing Denver's starters to score just 13 points over the course of the game. This unit is on something of a hot streak, as they have only allowed their opponent to score more than 20 points just once in the last ten weeks. They could give the Patriots a run for their money in the Wild Card round if they can keep that momentum up.

news.head: Los Angeles Chargers D/ST picks off Houston twice in loss
news.body: The Los Angeles Chargers D/ST picked off Houston QB CJ Stroud twice but failed to register a sack in the Chargers' 20-16 loss to the Texans.
news.impact: The Chargers' defense was fine against the Texans, but a sack or two would have been nice for fantasy managers. They've been a great unit for much of the last month, but will face a tough test against Denver next Sunday.

news.head: Michael Wilson comes up with five catches in Week 1
news.body: Michael Wilson secured 5-of-7 targets for 56 yards in Sunday's 26-14 win over the Chargers.
news.impact: With his next lucrative contract extension in hand, Wilson turned in a decent performance during Sunday's win. The fourth-year receiver finished third on the team in receptions, targets, and receiving yards, maintaining a solid rapport with QB Jacoby Brissett.

news.head: Michael Wilson agrees to three year, $75 million deal with Cardinals
news.body: Michael Wilson has agreed to a three year, $75 million deal with the Arizona Cardinals.
news.impact: Wilson was about to be playing on the final year of his rookie contract, but will now see himself attached to the team for the long haul. It will be interesting to see how his role changes, if at all, under a new coaching stafff and with Marvin Harrison Jr. back in the fold.

news.head: Michael Wilson expected to play role as Z-receiver
news.body: Cardinals coach Mike LaFleur said Michael Wilson will play the Puka Nacua role, “closer to the core,” as the Z-receiver.
news.impact: LaFleur has spent the past three years as the Rams offensive coordinator and figures to bring a lot of what he learned under Sean McVay to the Cardinals offense. Wilson is expected to line up off the line of scrimmage which will allow him to move more freely. Wilson exploded last season when Marvin Harrison Jr. missed time. The question remains what his production will be heading into a full season with Harrison healthy, but he should be put in a more favorable situation.

news.head: Michael Wilson hit pay dirt in Week 18 loss
news.body: Michael Wilson caught 5-of-8 targets for 99 yards and a touchdown in the Cardinals 37-20 loss to the Rams.
news.impact: Wilson broke free on a 43-yard touchdown reception in the third quarter. Wilson will end the season on a high note, tallying a touchdown in each of the last five games.

news.head: DK Metcalf leads Steelers with 10 targets in Week 1
news.body: DK Metcalf caught four of his 10 targets for 40 yards in a 20-13 win over the Falcons in Week 1.
news.impact: Metcalf didn't do much damage but his usage was encouraging as he easily led the Steelers in targets while newcomer Michael Pittman Jr. saw just three looks from Aaron Rodgers. Metcalf will be a high-end WR3 in fantasy heading into Week 2 against the Patriots.

news.head: DK Metcalf off injury report for Week 1
news.body: DK Metcalf is off of the injury report for Week 1's matchup against the Atlanta Falcons.
news.impact: Metcalf was dealing with an undisclosed injury earlier, but it's not an issue for him anymore and he is off of the injury report entirely ahead of Week 1. He goes into the season as the projected top target for the Steelers this season.

news.head: DK Metcalf practices Monday
news.body: DK Metcalf practiced on Monday.
news.impact: Metcalf missed time during training camp with an undisclosed injury. He remains on track to be good to go for Sunday's season opener against the Falcons.

news.head: DK Metcalf will be available Week 1
news.body: Steelers GM Omar Khan announced WR DK Metcalf will be available for Week 1.
news.impact: Metcalf has been dealing with an undisclosed injury, but appears to be good to go. He is a strong flex play against the Falcons in Week 1.

news.head: Bo Nix struggles in loss Monday
news.body: Bo Nix completed 17-of-28 passing attempts for 131 yards, one touchdown, and one interception in Monday night's 31-10 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs.
news.impact: Nix had a poor performance on Monday night. He was held to just 131 passing yards on the night and wasn't able to get Denver's offense going, leading them to score just ten points en route to a blowout loss at the hands of their divisional rivals. He should improve and play better in more favorable matchups moving forward, but they will continue to have a tough schedule for the foreseeable future, so fantasy managers might be better off looking for another option for the time being.

news.head: Bo Nix will not play in preseason opener
news.body: Bo Nix will not play in the Broncos preseason opener against the Falcons.
news.impact: Nix is expected to play in the second and third preseason games. Jarrett Stidham and Sam Ehlinger will both play a half.

news.head: Bo Nix (ankle) practices without limitations Wednesday
news.body: Bo Nix practiced on Wednesday at Broncos training camp without any limitations.
news.impact: Nix was able to get 7-on-7 work in during OTAs. He appears to be well on track to be good to go for the start of the season.

news.head: Bo Nix (ankle) participates in 7-on-7 drills Wednesday
news.body: Broncos QB Bo Nix participated in the 7-on-7 periods during the team’s second minicamp practice Wednesday.
news.impact: Per Kosmider, Nix hit RJ Harvey for a touchdown during a red-zone drill. He remains on track to be a full-go for training camp.

news.head: De'Von Achane sees 15 touches in Week 1 loss to Raiders
news.body: De'Von Achane carried the ball 11 times for 36 yards while also hauling in four of his five targets for 30 yards in the Dolphins' 27-13 Week 1 loss to the Las Vegas Raiders.
news.impact: Achane was unable to find much running room out of the backfield in the season opener, with the Las Vegas defense challenging new starting quarterback Malik Willis to beat it through the air. The running back remains a dynamic option in PPR formats, but fantasy managers may need to temper expectations in the short term, with a Week 2 matchup against the San Francisco 49ers up next.

news.head: De'Von Achane (shoulder) cleared to practice
news.body: Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley said De'Von Achane is ready to go after offseason shoulder surgery.
news.impact: Achane didn't participate in team drills this spring as he rehabbed, but he's good to go now that training camp's here. He'll be in line for his workhorse role as the focal point of the Dolphins offense.

news.head: De'Von Achane (shoulder) sees uptick in reps in minicamp Tuesday
news.body: Dolphins RB De'Von Achane reportedly saw an uptick in practice activity at Tuesday’s minicamp session.
news.impact: Achane is continuing to work his way back from an offseason procedure on his shoulder. He is expected to be good to go for training camp.

news.head: De'Von Achane (shoulder) hopeful to be ready for training camp
news.body: De'Von Achane told reporters he hopes to return to full action by training camp.
news.impact: Achane, who is fresh off a contract extension, underwent a clean-up procedure on his shoulder during the offseason. He hasn't been fully cleared yet, but he is hopeful to be good to go by training camp. He has still been practicing in limited fashion.

news.head: Kyle Pitts Sr. held without a catch in Week 1
news.body: Kyle Pitts Sr. failed to catch his lone target in a 20-13 loss to the Steelers in Week 1.
news.impact: It was a rough day for the Atlanta passing attack as third-string QB Cooper Rush only passed for 143 yards. Pitts will hope to bounce back in Week 2 against the Panthers, although he will be tough to trust in fantasy as long as Rush is under center.

news.head: Kyle Pitts Sr. agrees to 3-year, $54 million extension with Falcons
news.body: Kyle Pitts Sr. has agreed to a 3-year, $54 million extension with the Atlanta Falcons.
news.impact: After coming off arguably his best season as a pro, Pitts gets the bag. He will operate as the teams second target behind Drake London and TE1 in a tight end friendly Stefanski system. It’s wheels up for the still young Pitts.

news.head: Kyle Pitts Sr. could be moved if Falcons find trade partner
news.body: Adam Schefter said “he would watch to see if [the Falcons] could find a trade partner for Kyle Pitts, who they’re open to dealing.”
news.impact: Pitts had found himself in the midst of trade rumors earlier in the offseason, but they have quieted down since. He signed his franchise tender earlier in April. It still seems like Pitts will likely remain in Atlanta, but it is at least worth monitoring.

news.head: Kyle Pitts Sr. showing up for Falcons voluntary offseason workouts
news.body: Kyle Pitts Sr. is signing his franchise tag and showing up for the Falcons voluntary workouts to begin their offseason program.
news.impact: The two sides can still negotiate a long-term deal. The tag is $15.045 million fully guaranteed. Pitts took a step forward in his career last season, most notably when Drake London missed time.

news.head: Kyren Williams punches in score in loss to Niners
news.body: Kyren Williams ran 11 times for 41 yards and the Rams' only touchdown. He also caught all three of his targets for 24 receiving yards.
news.impact: Williams' day was saved by the touchdown; otherwise it was fairly miserable. Blake Corum showed out in his opportunities, but he was limited to ground work only. Kyren appears to be in a committee now, but he at least has the edge in passing situations, giving him more appeal.

news.head: Kyren Williams sees 15 touches in Week 18 win
news.body: Kyren Williams rushed for 60 yards on 12 carries in the Rams 37-20 win over the Cardinals. He caught 3-of-5 targets for 21 yards.
news.impact: Williams and Blake Corum continued to split time in the backfield to close out the regular season. Both running backs have been effective in that role this season, so the Rams will likely continue that throughout their playoff run.

news.head: Kyren Williams (ankle) officially active for Week 18
news.body: Rams RB Kyren Williams (ankle) is officially active for Week 18.
news.impact: Williams was limited in practice this week, but is healthy enough to suit up against the Cardinals. Despite having a playoff spot locked up, the Rams are playing their starters in the final regular season game.

news.head: Kyren Williams (ankle) listed questionable for Week 18
news.body: Kyren Williams is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Cardinals.
news.impact: Williams was limited in practice throughout the week. Rams coach Sean McVay has said starters will play regardless of the Seahawks/49ers result on Saturday.

news.head: Brock Bowers (knee) considered day-to-day
news.body: Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak said Brock Bowers is day-to-day.
news.impact: Bowers did not play in Sunday’s season opener after undergoing a meniscus trim. His status remains uncertain for Week 2.

news.head: Brock Bowers (knee) to miss 'a game or two'
news.body: Brock Bowers underwent a minor meniscus trim operation on Tuesday and is set to be sidelined for 'a game or two' as a result.
news.impact: Bowers reportedly got 'banged up' during training camp last week, and the team made the decision to have him undergo a minor procedure to trim his meniscus. This is especially concerning considering that he missed much of last year due to a nagging knee injury, and the team already expects him to be sidelined for at least a game or two while he recovers from this one. This is an alarming situation that fantasy managers should keep close tabs on, as this injury could linger if there are any setbacks in his recovery. Michael Mayer will step in as the team's top tight end in his absence, with Tre Tucker and Jalen Nailor both also likely to see an increase in opportunities in the star tight end's absence.

news.head: Brock Bowers: Raiders 'concocting multiple ways' to get TE involved
news.body: The Raiders are reportedly "concocting multiple ways" to get Brock Bowers involved in the offense
news.impact: Per Edwards, the Raiders believe Bowers' versatility is his "greatest weapon." He will remain one of the top tight ends in fantasy football alongside Trey McBride.

news.head: Brock Bowers says he 'feels great' in OTAs
news.body: Brock Bowers told reporters he "feels great" being back on the field.
news.impact: Bowers missed time last season with a knee injury he suffered in Week 1. He is entering camp fully healthy as one of the top tight ends in the NFL.

news.head: Tyjae Spears finishes with 24 all-purpose yards in Week 1
news.body: Tyjae Spears carried the ball three times for 12 yards and caught two of his four targets for 12 yards in a 23-10 loss to the Jets in Week 1.
news.impact: Spears operated behind Tony Pollard, who had eight touches. It was not a great day for the Tennessee run game, as the Titans were playing from behind for the entire game. Spears at least drew an encouraging number of targets in the passing attack. He will be a low-end flex option heading into Week 2 against the Eagles.

news.head: Tyjae Spears racks up seven receptions in loss
news.body: Tyjae Spears ran three times for 18 yards and caught all seven of his targets for nine yards in the Titans' 41-7 loss to the Jaguars.
news.impact: Spears made his fantasy day with his receiving in PPR leagues, but the yards certainly didn't come with it. His nine yards were the fewest yards on seven catches since at least 2010. Spears has some PPR appeal, but in a split backfield, it's tough to see him as much more than a flex play in 2026.

news.head: Tyjae Spears does nothing with seven touches Sunday
news.body: Tyjae Spears gained only two yards on six carries and negative yardage on one catch in Sunday's loss to the Saints.
news.impact: After putting up his best game of the season in Week 16, Spears let down any fantasy managers who took a shot on him in Week 17. He is a real long shot to do much of anything against the Jaguars' tenacious run defense in Week 18.

news.head: Tyjae Spears finds the end zone Sunday
news.body: Tyjae Spears ran for 52 yards and a touchdown on 13 carries in the Titans 26-9 win over the Chiefs. He also caught 5-of-5 targets for 53 yards receiving.
news.impact: Spears totaled over 100 yards from scrimmage with a score. He had a long catch and run of 34 yards. He'll be on the low-end flex radar next week against the Saints.

news.head: Jonathan Brooks sees five touches in Week 1 loss
news.body: Jonathan Brooks rushed four times for 14 yards while also catching one of his two targets for 48 yards in the Panthers' 59-37 loss to the Chicago Bears in Week 1.
news.impact: Brooks made the most of an otherwise underwhelming performance, with a 48-yard reception in the Week 1 loss. The running back will look to offer fantasy managers more impactful touches in a Week 2 divisional matchup against the Atlanta Falcons.

news.head: Jonathon Brooks (groin) not expected to face snap count Sunday
news.body: The Panthers say RB Jonathon Brooks will not face a snap count on Sunday against the Bears.
news.impact: Brooks was able to practice three straight days this week. It remains unclear what the split between him and Chuba Hubbard will look like heading into the season.

news.head: Jonathon Brooks (groin) practicing for third straight day
news.body: Jonathon Brooks (groin) is in practice uniform today. This will mark his third consecutive day of practice.
news.impact: Brooks has steadily improved since suffering the groin injury and looks like he is on his way to playing in Week 1. His workload might be lessened, as the team is looking to keep him healthy for the long term. However, while he might be tough to start, he’s an interesting name to watch on opening week.

news.head: Jonathon Brooks (groin) limited again Thursday
news.body: Jonathon Brooks (groin) was limited at practice again on Thursday.
news.impact: A groin injury left Brooks sidelined for a second-straight practice on Thursday. He said on Wednesday that he plans to play in Week 1, however, so it appears he is still trending towards suiting up against the Bears. The team could limit his workload if he's still managing an injury, though, so he may be a riskier start for the first game of the season.

news.head: Carnell Tate catches four passes in Week 1
news.body: Carnell Tate caught four of his six targets for 38 yards in a 23-10 loss to the Jets in Week 1.
news.impact: Tate tied for the team lead in targets and receiving yards while finishing second in receptions in his NFL debut. The rookie receiver will surely have bigger games going forward, as the entire Tennessee offense struggled in the season opener. Tate will be a low-end WR3 heading into a Week 2 matchup against the Eagles.

news.head: Carnell Tate (stiffness) good to go for Sunday
news.body: Carnell Tate (stiffness) is off of the injury report and good to go for Week 1's matchup against the New York Jets.
news.impact: The rookie is no longer on Tennessee's injury report and is set to make his NFL debut on Sunday. Fantasy managers should pay close attention to his debut game to see if he has the talent and situation of a breakout fantasy player for this season.

news.head: Carnell Tate returns to practice Friday
news.body: Titans rookie WR Carnell Tate returned to practice on Friday.
news.impact: Tate missed practice time earlier this week due to "stiffness." The rookie could see some more reps in Sunday's preseason game against the Seahawks.

news.head: Carnell Tate misses practice due to stiffness
news.body: Carnell Tate did not practice on Wednesday due to stiffness.
news.impact: It doesn't about to be a serious concern. Tate is day-to-day heading into Thursday.

news.head: Trey McBride starts season with strong performance
news.body: Trey McBride hauled in 9-of-13 targets for 95 yards and one touchdown in Sunday's 26-14 win over the Chargers.
news.impact: McBride is arguably the league's top fantasy asset at tight end, and he certainly looked the part in Week 1. Coming off back-to-back seasons with more than 100 receptions and 1,100 yards, McBride was QB Jacoby Brissett's favorite target on Sunday, getting five more looks than the next-closest Arizona pass catcher.

news.head: Trey McBride hauls in seven passes in Week 18 win
news.body: Trey McBride caught 7-of-8 targets for 65 yards in the Cardinals 37-20 loss to the Rams.
news.impact: McBride was tied for the team lead in targets and led the team in receptions Sunday. Despite a shaky quarterback situation, McBride will be one of the top tight ends drafted by fantasy managers in 2026.

news.head: Trey McBride hauls in 10 passes Sunday
news.body: Trey McBride caught 10-of-13 targets for 76 yards and a touchdown in the Cardinals 37-14 loss against the Bengals.
news.impact: McBride hauled in a garbage time touchdown from Jacoby Brissett in the final minutes with Arizona down 37-7. It was a huge bounce back week for him. He should be in line for another big game in Week 18 against the Rams.

news.head: Trey McBride quiet in loss Sunday
news.body: Trey McBride hauled in 4-of-8 targets for just 27 yards in Sunday's 26-19 loss to the Atlanta Falcons.
news.impact: McBride has been dominant this season, but he had probably his worst game of the season on Sunday. He was held to just 27 yards against the Falcons and finished with his lowest reception total out of any game this season with just four catches. He should bounce back in the near future, but this performance was untimely for any fantasy managers who were relying on him in their playoffs.

news.head: Ashton Jeanty leads offense in Week 1 win over Dolphins
news.body: Ashton Jeanty carried the ball 23 times for 102 yards while also hauling in all six of his targets for a team-leading 45 yards and two touchdowns in the Raiders' 27-13 Week 1 win over the Miami Dolphins.
news.impact: Jeanty was dynamic out of the backfield in the season opener, leading the team in rushing and receiving yards in the win. the running back remains an elite RB1 option with PPR upside for fantasy managers ahead of a Week 2 matchup against the Los Angeles Chargers ahead.

news.head: Ashton Jeanty (ankle) off injury report Sunday
news.body: Ashton Jeanty is off the injury report for Sunday's game against the Dolphins.
news.impact: Jeanty practiced in full all week. He should be good to go in his lead role to open the season.

news.head: Ashton Jeanty (ankle) expected to play Sunday
news.body: ESPN’s Adam Schefter said Raiders RB Ashton Jeanty is going to play in Week 1 against the Dolphins.
news.impact: Jeanty opened the week practicing in full on Wednesday as he works his way back from an ankle sprain. He remains a strong RB1 for fantasy managers going into the season.

news.head: Ashton Jeanty (ankle) practices in full Wednesday
news.body: Ashton Jeanty (ankle) practiced in a full capacity on Wednesday.
news.impact: It looks like Jeanty is strongly trending towards playing in Week 1, as he was able to put up a full session in Las Vegas' first practice of the week on Wednesday. If he is active, he will likely see enough work to be a great fantasy option in a positive matchup against the Dolphins.

news.head: Jeremiyah Love finds the end zone in debut
news.body: Jeremiyah Love picked up 41 yards and a touchdown on 11 carries in Sunday's 26-14 win over the Chargers.
news.impact: Love added a pair of grabs for nine yards to his NFL debut, and despite still being somewhat limited by the ankle sprain he sustained a month ago, the rookie certainly showed promise of things to come. Tyler Allgeier did get six more carries than Love, but that load share should begin to swing the other way as the season moves forward. The Cardinals have a tough matchup with the Seahawks on tap for Week 2.

news.head: Jeremiyah Love (ankle) active for Week 1
news.body: Jeremiyah Love (ankle) is active for Week 1 for the Arizona Cardinals against the Los Angeles Chargers.
news.impact: Love is good to go after clearing through pregame activities without any setbacks from the injured ankle, with the rookie running back set to share the backfield with free agent Tyler Allgeier against the Chargers.

news.head: Jeremiyah Love (ankle) expected to play on Sunday against Chargers
news.body: Jeremiyah Love (ankle) is expected to play against the Chargers on Sunday.
news.impact: Love is currently listed as questionable, but barring a setback, looks like he will be good to go against the Chargers. While his talent is among the best in the league, his role might be limited as he continues to work his way back from injury. Expect closer to RB3 numbers with upside for much more.

news.head: Jeremiyah Love (ankle) officially questionable for Sunday
news.body: Jeremiyah Love (ankle) is officially questionable for Sunday's game against the Los Angeles Chargers.
news.impact: The rookie is officially being listed as questionable to play in Sunday's season opener. There have been a lot of optimistic reports surrounding his availability, so it looks more likely than not that he will suit up against the Chargers, although that decision won't be made until closer to game time. If he is ruled out, Tyler Allgeier will be primed for a massive workload in Week 1 in Love's absence.

news.head: Harrison Mevis kicks single PAT in loss to Niners
news.body: Harrison Mevis made his only PAT attempt in the Rams' 27-7 tough loss to the 49ers.
news.impact: Mevis wasn't called upon much, the Rams offense was just never in scoring position for most of the game. He could have come in in the second half, but the Rams elected to go for it on 4th and goal at the 1 yard line, which was the correct choice, but their failure to convert meant Mevis was going to have an even bigger stinker. Brighter days are ahead for the Rams kicker.

news.head: Harrison Mevis returns to Rams after being tendered Monday
news.body: Harrison Mevis has been tendered by the Rams and will return to Los Angeles for the 2026 season.
news.impact: Undrafted out of Missouri in 2024, Mevis was a revelation for both the Rams and for fantasy owners last season. He replaced Joshua Karty as Los Angeles' kicker midway through they year and went 12-for-13 on field goal tries and a perfect 39-of-39 on extra point attempts in nine regular season games. He was also perfect in three postseason contests, going 6-for-6 on field goals and 9-for-9 on PATs. Mevis will open 2026 as the Rams' primary kicker and, given the potency of Los Angeles' offense, should be in line for a big year.

news.head: Harrison Mevis perfect in Week 18
news.body: Harrison Mevis connected on 3-of-3 field goals and 4-of-4 extra points in the Rams 37-20 win over the Cardinals.
news.impact: Mevis connected on field goals from 34, 40, and 42 yards out in the win. Mevis will end his first season with the Rams 12-of-13 on field goal attempts and 39-of-39 on extra point attempts.

news.head: Harrison Mevis goes for 5 points on Monday night
news.body: Harrison Mevis hit all three of his PATs and his only field goal in the Rams’ 27-24 loss to the Falcons on Monday night.
news.impact: Mevis didn’t have the greatest day for fantasy, the offense was shut out in the first half and struggled to do much until the final quarter. He’s been a solid kicker for the Rams this season and should be a fine fantasy asset if he returns in 2026.

news.head: Bijan Robinson hauls in touchdown catch in Week 1
news.body: Bijan Robinson carried the ball 21 times for 83 yards and caught eight of his 10 targets for 90 yards and a touchdown in a 20-13 loss to the Steelers in Week 1.
news.impact: Robinson was basically the entire offense for the Falcons in the close loss to Pittsburgh. He scored the team's only touchdown on a 23-yard catch at the end of the first quarter. It was an excellent start to the season for the star running back, who will slot in as a high-end RB1 in fantasy heading into a Week 2 matchup against the Panthers.

news.head: Bijan Robinson agrees to three-year extension with Falcons
news.body: Bijan Robinson has agreed to a three-year, $75 million contract extension with the Atlanta Falcons according to Adam Schefter.
news.impact: The deal includes $51 million in guaranteed money while also making Robinson the highest-paid running back in the league. The third-year back finished with 2,298 total offensive yards and 11 total touchdowns in 2025 and remains in the argument as the 1.01 pick in upcoming fantasy drafts with offensive minded Kevin Stefanski being named the new head coach this offseason for the Falcons.

news.head: Bijan Robinson does not practice Wednesday amid contract talks with Falcons
news.body: Bijan Robinson did not practice on Wednesday amid contract talks with the Falcons.
news.impact: Jahmyr Gibbs did not practice either on Wednesday for the same reason. Both players are under contract for two more seasons and are looking for new contracts. They'll both be among the league's highest paid running backs with new deals and deservingly so. This will remain a situation to monitor, but it's too early in training camp to have any major concerns.

news.head: Bijan Robinson could land extension with Falcons this offseason
news.body: The Falcons are expected to prioritize Bijan Robinson for an extension this summer.
news.impact: This news comes after Atlanta extended Drake London on Tuesday. It is possible we see Bijan and Jahmyr Gibbs both break the running back market this offseason.

news.head: Justin Herbert starts new season with mediocre performance
news.body: Justin Herbert connected on 17-of-27 passes for 209 yards with one touchdown and one interception, adding 29 yards on five carries in Sunday's 26-14 loss to the Cardinals.
news.impact: Herbert and the Chargers' offense definitely disappointed under new OC Mike McDaniel on Sunday. This was expected by many to be an opening act for a dynamic offense against a sub-par defensive unit. It turned out to be anything but that. Herbert was sacked three times and picked off once while just clearing 200 yards on 27 throws. He did find top receiver Ladd McConkey for an eight-yard TD toss in the third quarter, but that was it as far as putting points on the board through the air. Herbert should still be viewed as a solid QB 1 going into a matchup with the Raiders, but if he disappoints again, the seventh-year pro will drop like a rock.

news.head: Justin Herbert, starters will play Thursday
news.body: Justin Herbert and most of Los Angeles' starters will play in Thursday's preseason finale against the Los Angeles Rams.
news.impact: HC Jim Harbaugh told reporters that Herbert and most of the team's starters are going to play in their final preseason game on Thursday night, with the exception of a few veterans. It remains unlikely that the starting unit will see more than a quarter or two of action, however.

news.head: Justin Herbert, Chargers starters to play one series Thursday
news.body: Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh said the starters will play one series on Thursday against the 49ers.
news.impact: We will get our first look at the Chargers offense under new OC Mike McDaniel.
