news.head: Justin Herbert focusing on footwork and anticipatory throwing
news.body: Chargers OC Mike McDaniel has Justin Herbert focusing on footwork and anticipatory throwing.
news.impact: McDaniel is continuing to try to help Herbert improve and focus on certain areas of his game this offseason. The hype will remain high on the Chargers offense heading into this season.

news.head: Travis Etienne Jr. sees 16 touches in Week 1 loss to Lions
news.body: Travis Etienne Jr. rushed nine times for a team-high 46 yards while also hauling in seven of his nine targets for 32 yards in the Saints' 31-30 Week 1 loss to the Detroit Lions.
news.impact: Etienne Jr. made the most of his carries out of the backfield for a New Orleans offense that had trailed 21-0 at one point, averaging 5.1 yards per carry in the loss. The running back offers fantasy managers more potential in PPR formats, with a Week 2 contest against the Baltimore Ravens up next.

news.head: Travis Etienne Jr. splits first-team reps with Alvin Kamara Wednesday
news.body: Travis Etienne Jr. split first-team reps with Alvin Kamara in practice on Wednesday.
news.impact: Etienne is likely to be the 1A in the Saints backfield with the contract he got in free agency. This will be a situation to monitor throughout training camp.

news.head: Travis Etienne Jr. signing with Saints
news.body: The Saints are signing RB Travis Etienne Jr. to a four-year, $52 million deal.
news.impact: The future of Alvin Kamara in the Saints backfield is uncertain as Etienne joins the group. The status of Kamara will need to be monitored the rest of the offseason. Either way, Etienne should be stepping into the lead role. He'll be on the low-end RB1/high-end RB2 radar for fantasy managers.

news.head: Travis Etienne Jr. gets 15 touches in win
news.body: Travis Etienne Jr. ran 14 times for 32 yards and caught a single pass for six yards in the Jaguars' 41-7 win over the Titans.
news.impact: Etienne had a bit of a quiet day despite the offensive onslaught by the Jaguars. He should be a favorite candidate to be the Jaguars' RB1 in 2026 after a bounce-back season.

news.head: Justin Jefferson scores two touchdowns Sunday
news.body: Justin Jefferson caught 8-of-9 targets for 92 yards and two touchdowns in the Vikings 39-22 win over the Packers.
news.impact: Despite Kyler Murray leaving in the first quarter with a concussion, Jefferson was still able to produce in a big way with Carson Wentz. He remains a locked and loaded high-end WR1.

news.head: Justin Jefferson restructures contract with Vikings
news.body: The Vikings restructured the contract of Justin Jefferson.
news.impact: Minnesota is making moves to clear salary cap space. Pelissero notes they still have work to do to get under the cap by Wednesday.

news.head: Justin Jefferson goes over 100 receiving yards in Week 18
news.body: Justin Jefferson ended the 2025 season on a high note, catching eight passes for 101 yards in the Vikings' 16-3 win over the Packers on Sunday.
news.impact: With the 101 yards, Jefferson joined Mike Evans and Randy Moss as the only players in NFL history to record at least 1,000 receiving yards in each of his first six seasons. It was, however, a bit of a down year for Jefferson, who finished with a career-low 1,048 yards and just two touchdowns. The 100-yard effort on Sunday was just his third of the season and his first since October 5. Jefferson was hurt by inconsistent quarterback play this season, but he still remains one of the best receivers in the NFL and should be a favorite to rebound in 2026.

news.head: Justin Jefferson hauls in four receptions in Week 17 win over Lions
news.body: Justin Jefferson hauled in four of his team-high five targets for 30 yards in the Vikings' 23-10 Week 17 win over the Lions.
news.impact: Jefferson has made the most of increased involvement in the Minnesota offense, recording four or more receptions in each of his last two games. The dynamic wideout will look to finish a frustrating season on a positive note in a Week 18 matchup against the Green Bay Packers.

news.head: Tucker Kraft totals 65 yards Sunday
news.body: Tucker Kraft caught 3-of-6 targets for 65 yards in the Packers 39-22 loss against the Vikings.
news.impact: Kraft was playing in his first game back from his torn ACL. He was on a snap count in his first game back. He remains a TE1 heading into next week against the Jets.

news.head: Tucker Kraft signs four year, $75 million deal with Packers
news.body: Tucker Kraft has agreed to a four-year, $75 million deal with the Green Bay Packers. The deal is worth up to $92 million.
news.impact: Kraft was on his way to a massive season in 2025 before going down with a torn ACL. He gets his payday as the Packers lock in their emergeing star for the long haul.

news.head: Tucker Kraft (knee) off injury report for Week 1
news.body: Tucker Kraft (knee) is off of the injury report for Week 1's game against the Minnesota Vikings.
news.impact: Kraft has been rehabbing from a major knee injury all offseason, but it appears that he is finally close to full health again, as he carries no injury designation prior to the team's season opener on Sunday. He could be limited for his first few weeks back, but the team hasn't indicated that, meaning that he could be seeing a full workload in the very near future.

news.head: Tucker Kraft (knee) to participate in 11-on-11 drills in joint practice
news.body: Tucker Kraft will participate in 11-on-11 drills in the Packers joint practice with Cardinals.
news.impact: Kraft returned to team drills earlier in August. He remains on track to be good to go for Week 1 in September.

news.head: Jonathan Taylor rushes for two touchdowns in Week 1 loss
news.body: Jonathan Taylor carried the ball 19 times for 98 yards and two touchdowns while also catching three of his four targets for 23 yards in the Colts' 41-23 loss to the Baltimore Ravens in Week 1.
news.impact: Taylor was the lone bright spot in an underwhelming Colts offense to begin the season, averaging 5.2 yards per carry in the loss. The superstar running back will look to remain an impactful backfield option in Week 2 against the Kansas City Chiefs.

news.head: Jonathan Taylor agrees to two-year, $44 million extension with Colts
news.body: Jonathan Taylor has agreed to a two-year, $44 million deal with the Indianapolis Colts that could be worth up to $47 million.
news.impact: The 27 year old is coming off of back-to-back 1,400 yard rushing seasons with at least 11 rushing touchdowns in each, including a ridiculous 18 rushing touchdowns in 2025. Taylor should be viewed as a top tier running back in 2026, and his deal secures his dynasty value for the next several seasons.

news.head: Jonathan Taylor struggles in Week 18
news.body: Jonathan Taylor ran for 26 yards on 14 carries in the Colts 38-30 loss against the Texans. He also caught 2-of-2 targets for 13 yards receiving.
news.impact: Taylor struggled to get anything going on the ground to close the season. It was a struggle over the second half of the year for him after he was the favorite to win Offensive Player of the Year during the first half of the season. He should remain a high-end RB1 heading into next season.

news.head: Jonathan Taylor finds the end zone Sunday
news.body: Jonathan Taylor ran for 70 yards and a touchdown on 21 carries in the Colts 23-17 loss against the Jaguars. He also caught 3-of-6 targets for 14 yards receiving.
news.impact: Taylor was able to salvage his day with a score on the ground. He also had another touchdown called back due to a penalty. It is unclear if he will see his usual role in Week 18 against the Texans.

news.head: Wan'Dale Robninson goes for 38 yards in Week 1
news.body: Wan'Dale Robinson caught five of his six targets for 38 yards in a 23-10 loss to the Jets in Week 1.
news.impact: Robinson tied for the team lead in targets and receiving yards while leading the way with his five catches. The entire Tennessee offense struggled to move the ball in Week 1, which cut into Robinson's final stats. He will look to bounce back as a decent flex option in PPR leagues heading into a Week 2 matchup against the Eagles.

news.head: Wan'Dale Robinson (head) off injury report for Week 1
news.body: Wan'Dale Robinson (head) is off of the injury report ahead of Week 1's matchup against the New York Jets.
news.impact: As expected, Robinson's head injury is no longer an issue and he carries no injury designation heading into Week 1. He should be a full go against the Jets and projects to be a worthwhile streaming option in PPR formats.

news.head: Wan'Dale Robinson expected to play on outside and in slot with Titans
news.body: Wan'Dale Robinson told reporters he expects to play on the outside as well as in the slot with the Titans.
news.impact: Robinson branched out from being a slot-only wide receiver last season. It resulted in him reaching 1,000 yards for the first time in his career. He should step in as the top target for Cam Ward and the Titans.

news.head: Wan’Dale Robinson agrees to deal with Titans
news.body: Wan’Dale Robinson has agreed four year, $78 million deal with the Tennessee Titans.
news.impact: Robinson was long rumored to go to the Titans, and those rumors have come true. He will rejoin former Giants HC Brian Daboll in Tennessee and operate as a primary target for Cam Ward in 2026. It’s wheels up for Wan’Dale, who has 140 targets and at least 92 receptions each of the past two years.

news.head: Jayden Daniels tosses two touchdowns in Week 1 loss to Eagles
news.body: Jayden Daniels completed 18-of-34 pass attempts for 164 yards and two touchdowns while also rushing five times for 31 yards on the Commanders’ 24-22 Week 1 loss to the Philadelphia Eagles.
news.impact: Daniels was unable to find much success against a stout Philadelphia defense in the season opener, completing 53% of his pass attempts in the loss. The quarterback will look to offer more impactful results against a Dallas Cowboys defense that struggled in Week 1 against the New York Giants.

news.head: Jayden Daniels expected to play against Lions
news.body: Commanders QB Jayden Daniels is set to start against the Lions on Saturday.
news.impact: Daniels had a very underwhelming sophomore campaign, largely due to injury. He and the starters will have an opportunity to build chemistry and momentum ahead of the regular season.

news.head: Jayden Daniels: OC David Blough expected to run QB friendly offense
news.body: Commanders GM Adam Peters said he believes the David Blough offense will be more QB friendly for Jayden Daniels.
news.impact: Peters added he believes Daniels will have more options in the new offense under Blough. He'll be looking to bounce back after he was limited to just seven games due to injuries last season.

news.head: Jayden Daniels (elbow) to miss final three games
news.body: Commanders QB Jayden Daniels will be shut down for the remainder of the season.
news.impact: With Daniels sidelined, Marcus Mariota is expected to start the final three games. Mariota has 11 total touchdowns across seven starts this season and has been a serviceable fantasy option. Daniels will now turn his focus toward a full recovery and preparing for the 2026 season.

news.head: Chris Godwin Jr. hauls in four passes Sunday
news.body: Chris Godwin Jr. caught 4-of-4 targets for 40 yards in the Buccaneers 33-27 loss against the Bengals on Sunday.
news.impact: Godwin totaled 30 of his 40 yards on one reception. The Bucs offense was unable to get in sync with four lost fumbles. He'll remain a WR3 heading into Week 2 against the Browns.

news.head: Chris Godwin Jr. (soreness) does not practice Tuesday
news.body: Chris Godwin Jr. did not practice on Tuesday to manage injuries and soreness.
news.impact: Godwin, Jalen McMillan and Emeka Egbuka all sat out on Tuesday. It doesn't appear to be anything serious with any of them.

news.head: Chris Godwin Jr. quiet in Week 18
news.body: Chris Godwin Jr. caught his lone target for eight yards in the Bucs 16-14 win over the Panthers.
news.impact: It was a quiet day for the entire Bucs wide receiver room. Godwin showed flashes after working his way back to full health, but he struggled to finish the season. He'll be a bounce back candidate next year.

news.head: Chris Godwin (illness) questionable, will play Saturday
news.body: Chris Godwin (illness) will be available for Saturday's game.
news.impact: Godwin was a late addition to the injury report due to being under the weather. However, the veteran receiver will be active for the all-important divisional matchup with the Panthers.

news.head: Luther Burden III sees six touches in Week 1
news.body: Luther Burden III hauled in all five of his targets for 63 yards while also rushing once for two yards in the Bears' 59-37 Week 1 win over the Carolina Panthers.
news.impact: Burden III saw steady involvement in the Chicago passing attack, finishing second on the team in targets, receptions, and receiving yards in the win. The wideout offers head coach Ben Johnson another dynamic pass-catcher as part of an explosive Chicago offense ahead of a Week 2 divisional matchup with the Minnesota Vikings.

news.head: Luther Burden III (groin) good to go for Week 1
news.body: Luther Burden III (groin) is off of the injury report and good to go for Week 1's matchup against the Carolina Panthers.
news.impact: Burden was dealing with a groin injury earlier in the offseason, but he is fully healthy now and carries no injury designation ahead of Sunday's season opener. He should play without any restrictions and will be primed for a huge Week 1 if the Bears are without Rome Odunze (calf) for their matchup against the Panthers.

news.head: Luther Burden III (groin) practices Tuesday
news.body: Luther Burden III was practicing on Tuesday.
news.impact: Burden had returned to practice last week. He is on track to be good to go for the start of the season next week.

news.head: Luther Burden III (groin) back at practice Wednesday
news.body: Luther Burden III returned to practicing on Wednesday.
news.impact: Burden was back on the field for the first time since injuring his groin on August 8. He went through individual drills and went inside when 7 on 7 started. This should put him on track to be good to go for Week 1.

news.head: Stefon Diggs finds end zone in Week 1 loss to Eagles
news.body: Stefon Diggs hauled in four of his nine targets for 55 yards and one touchdown in the Commanders’ 24-22 Week 1 loss to the Philadelphia Eagles.
news.impact: Diggs saw plenty of volume as part of a Washington passing attack held in check, leading the team in targets in a losing effort. The veteran wideout offers fantasy managers a stable WR2/3 option while the Commanders offense looks to get back on track in a Week 2 matchup against the Dallas Cowboys.

news.head: Stefon Diggs expected to play against Lions
news.body: Stefon Diggs is set to make his Commanders debut in the preseason on Saturday.
news.impact: Diggs will see his first action as a member of the Commanders. It will be worth tuning in to see what his exact role looks like.

news.head: Stefon Diggs signs with Commanders
news.body: The Washington Commanders have signed WR Stefon Diggs
news.impact: Diggs had been closely linked to Washington for a while. He should step into the immediate No. 2 wide receiver role behind Terry McLaurin. He is coming off a 1,000 yard season with the Patriots. This likely means they won't be signing Brandon Aiyuk.

news.head: Stefon Diggs linked to Commanders
news.body: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports Stefon Diggs is "intrigued" by the Commanders.
news.impact: Diggs is drawing interest from at least four other teams. He would step into the immediate WR2 role in Washington alongside Terry McLaurin. He totaled just over 1,000 yards with the Patriots last season coming off a torn ACL. He is now almost two years removed from the injury. He'll likely want to sign with a team soon with training camp starting up.

news.head: Chuba Hubbard scores two touchdowns in Week 1 loss to Bears
news.body: Chuba Hubbard carried the ball 10 times for 49 yards and one touchdown while also catching all three of his targets for 38 yards and one touchdown in the Panthers' 59-37 Week 1 loss to the Chicago Bears.
news.impact: Hubbard took advantage of a primary ball-carrying option before the game script changed, leading the team in rushing yards in the loss. The running back remains a solid option out of the backfield for head coach Dave Canales, with a Week 2 matchup against the Atlanta Falcons up next.

news.head: Chuba Hubbard (hamstring) off injury report for Week 1
news.body: Chuba Hubbard (hamstring) is off of the injury report ahead of Week 1's matchup against the Chicago Bears.
news.impact: Hubbard was battling a hamstring injury earlier this offseason, but it's no longer an issue for him and he carries no injury designation ahead of Week 1. He will likely split work with Jonathan Brooks (groin) in the season opener, which hurts the fantasy outlook for both of them.

news.head: Chuba Hubbard (hamstring) week-to-week with hamstring injury
news.body: Chuba Hubbard (hamstring) is week-to-week with a hamstring injury per HC Dave Canales. He is expected to play in Week 1.
news.impact: While it sounds like Hubbard should be good to go for the season opener, he could still be limited following a multi-week absence. With that said, it’s now wheels up for Jonathon Brooks, who’s now going to see his ADP rise yet again.

news.head: Chuba Hubbard to play in preseason game Saturday
news.body: Chuba Hubbard will play in the Panthers preseason game on Saturday against the Bills.
news.impact: Hubbard is unlikely to see many snaps. The Panthers are also expected to play Jonathon Brooks.

news.head: Puka Nacua goes for 74 yards in loss
news.body: Puka Nacua caught five of nine targets for 74 yards in the Rams' 27-7 loss to the Niners on Thursday.
news.impact: Puka was the only Ram who had more than 26 receiving yards, and most of those yards came on a nice catch and run early on in the game. His final total was respectable, but fantasy managers will hope for more next time he's out on the field.

news.head: Puka Nacua not listed on Rams first injury report
news.body: Puka Nacua is not listed on the Rams initial injury report for Week 1.
news.impact: Puka has been dealing with a psoas injury for a little over a week, but his absence on the injury report is a big indication that barring a setback, he will play on Thursday. The star receiver should be a full go and lock into fantasy lineups.

news.head: Puka Nacua (psoas) expected to play in Week 1
news.body: Los Angeles Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua is expected to play in Week 1 against the San Francisco 49ers as the team travels to Australia, says head coach Sean McVay.
news.impact: Nacua has been dealing with a psoas injury but returned to practice about a week ago. With the opening game in Melbourne, the Rams are being smart with their players given the toll of travel. However, their WR1 should be good to go. Nacua also still faces a potential suspension "under the NFL’s personal conduct policy," says Adkins.

news.head: Puka Nacua (psoas) returns to practice
news.body: Puka Nacua returned to practice Sunday.
news.impact: Nacua had missed practice for much of the past couple of weeks with psoas soreness. The injury appears to be behind him and he is expected to avoid the commissioner’s exempt list, meaning he should be good to go for Week 1.

news.head: Tetairoa McMillan hauls in five receptions in Week 1 loss
news.body: Tetairoa McMillan hauled in five of his eight targets for 75 yards in the Panthers' 59-37 Week 1 loss to the Chicago Bears.
news.impact: McMillan made the most of his sizeable volume in the Carolina passing attack, finishing second in targets, receptions, and receiving yards in the loss. The wideout remains one of the more dynamic pass-catching options in the Carolina offense moving forward, with a Week 2 contest against the Atlanta Falcons up next.

news.head: Tetairoa McMillan (foot) practices Thursday
news.body: Tetairoa McMillan was at practice on Thursday.
news.impact: The Panthers and Cardinals are the first teams to have veterans report to training camp. McMillan had missed most of the spring due to a foot injury.

news.head: Tetairoa McMillan expected to see more slot usage this season
news.body: Cameron Wolfe reports that Tetairoa McMillan is expected to see more usage in the slot this season.
news.impact: McMillan started to see more snaps in the slot during the second half of his rookie season last year. Wolfe notes that the Panthers believe Chris Brazzell II will be able to play on the outside that will allow McMillan the opportunity to play more in the slot. He should be able to take advantage of mismatches in the slot as he looks to take a step forward heading into his second season in the NFL.

news.head: Tetairoa McMillan (ankle) hopeful to be ready for training camp
news.body: Tetairoa McMillan told reporters he is hopeful to be ready for the start of training camp.
news.impact: McMillan has been limited to individual drills early on in OTAs. He said he is "feeling better" now.

news.head: Aaron Jones Sr. finds the end zone Sunday
news.body: Aaron Jones Sr. ran for 40 yards and a touchdown on 12 carries in the Vikings 39-22 win over the Packers. He did not catch his lone target.
news.impact: Jones was the 1B in the Vikings backfield behind Jordan Mason to open the season. He'll be a touchdown dependent RB2/flex play most weeks.

news.head: Aaron Jones Sr. joins Vikings on re-worked deal
news.body: Aaron Jones Sr. is returning to the Vikings on a one-year deal that lowered his base salary to $5.5 million.
news.impact: Jones’ return to Minnesota likely puts a damper on any potential flashy signing or draft pick the Vikings may have done otherwise. He should be a decent RB2 for the team, likely retaining the same role he has had the past two seasons.

news.head: Aaron Jones Sr. will be released or traded at start of league year
news.body: The Vikings have informed RB Aaron Jones Sr. that, barring a trade, he will be released at the start of the league year this month.
news.impact: The move will save the Vikings $7.75 million against the cap. That would leave Jordan Mason at the top of the depth chart in Minnesota for now, though they'll likely address the position in the NFL Draft.

news.head: Aaron Jones Sr. (hip) ruled out for Week 18
news.body: Aaron Jones Sr. has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Packers.
news.impact: The season will be over for Jones. He totaled 548 yards and two touchdowns to go along with another 199 yards and a score through the air as a receiver.

news.head: Dallas Goedert hauls in two touchdowns in Week 1 win over Commanders
news.body: Dallas Goedert hauled in four of his five targets for 77 yards and two touchdowns in the Eagles’ 24-22 Week 1 win over the Washington Commanders.
news.impact: Goedert made the most of his involvement in the Philadelphia passing attack in the season opener, leading the team in receiving yards in the win. The tight end offers fantasy managers a steady TE1 option entering a favorable Week 2 contest against the Tennessee Titans.

news.head: Dallas Goedert returning to Eagles on one-year deal
news.body: Dallas Goedert and the Eagles have agreed on a one-year deal to keep the star tight end in Philadelphia for another season.
news.impact: Goedert played 15 games last year and caught a career-high 60 passes for 591 yards and a career-best 11 touchdowns. The 31-year-old has spent his entire eight-year career with Philadelphia and has totaled 409 catches for 4,676 yards and 35 touchdowns in 108 games. His status has been in limbo during the offseason and, with the Eagles signing Grant Calcaterra and Johnny Mundt, it appeared that Goedert's days in Philadelphia were coming to an end. That, however, is not the case as Goedert will take his rightful place as the starting tight end with the Eagles for a ninth season. He should be one of the first tight ends drafted in fantasy leagues in 2026.

news.head: Dallas Goedert not a free agent just yet
news.body: Dallas Goedert was reportedly not listed as a free agent by the league.
news.impact: Goedert's void date has been pushed back to Friday. It is still possible the two sides can work out a contract extension as a result.

news.head: Dallas Goedert 'moving on' from Philly
news.body: TE Dallas Goedert is likely to part ways with the Eagles this offseason.
news.impact: Goedert is coming off career highs in both receptions and touchdowns. Depending on his landing spot, he could be a mid-to-low-end TE1 in 2026.

news.head: Tony Pollard held to 35 rushing yards in Week 1
news.body: Tony Pollard carried the ball seven times for 35 yards and lost one yard on his lone catch in a 23-10 loss to the Jets in Week 1.
news.impact: Pollard was quiet with the Titans playing from behind for most of the game. On the bright side, the veteran running back led the backfield with Tyjae Spears getting just three carries. Pollard will look to bounce back as a high-end RB3 in Week 2 against the Eagles.

news.head: Tony Pollard (foot) returns to practice Wednesday
news.body: Tony Pollard returned to practice on Wednesday.
news.impact: Pollard missed two practices with a foot issue. He saw four carries in the Titans preseason opener.

news.head: Tony Pollard (foot) not seen practicing Monday
news.body: Tony Pollard did not practice on Monday.
news.impact: Pollard previously also missed practice on Saturday. He saw four carries for 22 yards and a touchdown in the team’s preseason opener.

news.head: Tony Pollard gets 17 touches in loss
news.body: Tony Pollard ran 14 times for 42 yards and caught all three of his targets for 17 yards in the Titans' 41-7 loss to the Jaguars.
news.impact: Pollard capped off a tumultuous year in Tennessee with nearly 1,300 scrimmage yards and five touchdowns. He's under contract for one more year, but it's fair to wonder whether they will trade him this offseason as they look to rebuild the roster.

news.head: Jacksonville Jaguars D/ST shut down hapless Browns
news.body: The Jacksonville Jaguars D/ST shut down the Browns' offense on Sunday in the team's dominant 34-10 win. They ended the day with five sacks, a pick, and a fumble recovery.
news.impact: It was a great day for the Jags' defense in what was expected to be an easy matchup. They're worth streaming when the matchup is right, but they could be in for tough sledding against Denver next week.

news.head: Jacksonville Jaguars D/ST shut down Titans in dominant win
news.body: The Jacksonville Jaguars D/ST got a sack and a pick-six in the Jaguars' 41-7 win over the Titans.
news.impact: The Jaguars didn't have multiple takeaways or many sacks, but they simply sucked the life out of the Titans' offense. That's not to say they didn't make great plays; they certainly did, and they counted for fantasy big time. They are coming into the playoffs on a hot streak.

news.head: Jaguars D/ST records two interceptions Sunday
news.body: The Jaguars D/ST allowed 17 points on 204 yards with two interceptions and two sacks on Sunday against the Colts.
news.impact: The second interception on the day came on a Hail Mary thrown by Riley Leonard on the final play of the game. They should be worth starting again in Week 18 against the Titans.

news.head: Jaguars D/ST allows 20 points Sunday
news.body: The Jaguars' D/ST logged one sack, one interception, and one fumble recovery while allowing 20 points in Sunday's win over the Denver Broncos.
news.impact: Jacksonville's defense had a pretty good game against the Broncos on Sunday. They allowed just 20 points and were able to log a couple of key takeaways to help secure the win on the road. This unit had a good schedule to close out the season, with matchups against the Colts and Titans coming up over the next couple of weeks.

news.head: Los Angeles Rams D/ST run over by 49ers
news.body: The Los Angeles Rams' D/ST was completely destroyed by the 49ers' offense, and it didn't help that the Rams' offense was equally outmatched, making the final result all the more stark.
news.impact: The Rams still have plenty of star talent on this side of the ball, so don't overreact to one week of football. They should be just fine as the season rolls along once they find their footing.

news.head: Rams D/ST allows 20 points in Week 18 win
news.body: The Rams D/ST allowed 238 passing yards, 79 rushing yards, and 20 points in a 37-20 win over the Cardinals.
news.impact: The Rams' defense tallied one interception, one fumble, and six sacks in the win. The Rams will head on the road to take on the NFC South champion Carolina Panthers in the first round of the playoffs.

news.head: Los Angeles Rams D/ST has huge touchdown in loss
news.body: The Los Angeles Rams D/ST allowed 27 points with no sacks or turnovers in the Rams 27-24 loss to the Falcons. They did however score a touchdown.
news.impact: The special teams unit came up big late in the loss to the Falcons thanks to a blocked field goal turned touchdown, getting the team back on the board and swinging momentum their way. But it wasn’t enough, as the offense still continued to have its struggles despite some success, and the defense struggled to stop Bijan Robinson all night. It’s a tough loss, but they will look to rebound next week and into the NFL playoffs.

news.head: Rams D/ST records four sacks and forces three turnovers Thursday
news.body: Despite dropping a heartbreaking 38-37 overtime loss in Seattle on Thursday night, the Rams D/ST sacked QB Sam Darnold four times and forced three Seahawks' turnovers in the high-scoring contest.
news.impact: Los Angeles picked off Darnold twice and forced a fumble from former teammate, Cooper Kupp, late in the first half. The Rams also registered four sacks and broke up four passes on the night. Next up is a Monday Night matchup in Atlanta against the Falcons.

news.head: Nico Collins turns in strong season debut
news.body: Nico Collins grabbed 7-of-10 targets for 75 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 36-31 loss to the Bills.
news.impact: Nico Collins played his typical go-to role for QB C.J. Stroud on Sunday. Collins led the team in receptions, targets, and yards. He also found the end zone for the first time this season, hitting paydirt on a 12-yard play just before halftime. Collins is a WR1 for fantasy purposes.

news.head: Nico Collins sits out 11-on-11 drills in practice Thursday
news.body: Nico Collins did not participate in 11-on-11 drills at Texans practice on Thursday.
news.impact: It is too early to be concerned for Collins, but it's something to monitor nonetheless heading into minicamp.

news.head: Nico Collins agrees to a two-year adjusted contract with Texans
news.body: Nico Collins has agreed to a two-year adjustment to his contract with the Texans, getting more guaranteed money over the next two seasons. He is scheduled to be a free agent in 2028.
news.impact: The contract gives Collins a raise as well, not a bad deal at all. He should be in line for plenty of targets as the top wideout for QB CJ Stroud over the next two seasons, and don’t be surprised if the Texans try to extend him when the time comes.

news.head: Nico Collins, teams have called Texans to check on WR
news.body: Jordan Schultz reports that teams have called the Texans to check on WR Nico Collins.
news.impact: Collins is due for another contract as he is set to make $20.6 million this season when the wide receiver market is double that. It still seems highly unlikely he is traded, but it's a situation to monitor nonetheless.

news.head: Brock Purdy dismantles Rams defense in statement win
news.body: Brock Purdy completed 25-of-34 passes for 205 yards, three touchdowns, and a pick in the 49ers' 27-7 win over the Rams on Thursday. He also ran five times for 29 yards.
news.impact: Purdy was great in this game aside from a couple of hiccups, namely the interception. However, he did what he needed to and got the Niners into scoring position and helped them take advantage of the several short fields they inherited. Purdy should be a solid asset moving forward for fantasy.

news.head: Brock Purdy shut down by Seattle defense Saturday
news.body: Brock Purdy completed 19-of-27 passes for just 127 yards and one interception in the 49ers 13-3 loss to the Seahawks.
news.impact: Purdy was held to a season-low 127 yards and failed to reach 200 yards through the air in a game for just the third time in his nine starts. It was also his only start of the year without throwing a touchdown pass. He carried the ball twice for 21 yards and had San Francisco's longest run of the night (11 yards).

news.head: Brock Purdy accounts for five touchdowns in Week 17 win over Bears
news.body: Brock Purdy completed 24-of-33 pass attempts for 303 yards, three touchdowns, and one interception while also rushing six times for 28 yards and two touchdowns in the 49ers' 42-38 Week 17 win over the Bears.
news.impact: Purdy continues an impactful stretch behind center, recording two or more touchdowns in each of his last four games (12 passing, three rushing) for the 49ers. The signal-caller remains a dynamic QB1 option despite a difficult Week 18 matchup against the Seattle Seahawks.

news.head: Brock Purdy lights it up on Monday Night Football
news.body: Brock Purdy completed 25 of 34 passes for 295 yards with five touchdowns and one interception, adding 11 yards on two carries in Monday's 48-27 win over the Colts.
news.impact: Purdy set a new career high in TD passes for a single game on Monday, as he has now posted an 8-1 TD/INT ratio over the last two weeks. He has also completed exactly 75% of his passes while throwing for 295 yards in each of those two contests. Purdy missed several games due to injury earlier this season, but he is completely locked in at the right time for the 49ers.

news.head: Jaylen Warren leads Pittsburgh backfield in Week 1
news.body: Jaylen Warren carried the ball 10 times for 46 yards while catching five of his six targets for 27 yards and losing a fumble in a 20-13 win over the Falcons in Week 1.
news.impact: Warren and Rico Dowdle split first-team reps in the preseason, but it was Warren who emerged with the better game in Week 1, out-touching Dowdle 15 to 10 and out-gaining him 73 to 21. Warren will be a flex option for fantasy purposes heading into Week 2 against the Patriots.

news.head: Jaylen Warren, Rico Dowdle both see first-team reps Thursday
news.body: Jaylen Warren and Rico Dowdle split the first-team reps in practice on Thursday.
news.impact: Warren and Dowdle continue to rotate who sees the first reps with the first-team. They are likely to both be involved in a committee in the Steelers backfield this season.

news.head: Jaylen Warren runs for 66 yards in Week 18
news.body: Jaylen Warren carried the ball 14 times for 66 yards and caught all five of his targets for 33 yards in a 26-24 win over the Ravens in Week 18.
news.impact: Warren was productive in the win, although he was outproduced by Kenneth Gainwell. The two have formed a solid pair in the backfield for Pittsburgh this season. Warren will now prepare to face off against the Texans next week in the Wild-Card round of the playoffs.

news.head: Jaylen Warren logs 12 touches in Week 17 loss
news.body: Jaylen Warren rushed for 64 yards on 12 carries in the Steelers 13-6 loss to the Browns.
news.impact: Warren was not a factor in the passing game, but did see the bulk of the touches in the running game. Unfortunately for fantasy managers, this was far from the wonderful performance he turned in last week. Warren and the Steelers will take on the Ravens in Week 18.

news.head: Christian Watson scores two touchdowns in big day Sunday
news.body: Christian Watson caught 6-of-8 targets for 147 yards and two touchdowns in the Packers 39-22 loss against the Vikings on Sunday.
news.impact: Watson exploded for an 81-yard catch and run score early. He was later found in the end zone again by Jordan Love. He will be an upside WR2 next week against the Jets.

news.head: Christian Watson agrees to four-year, $110 million extension with Packers
news.body: Christian Watson has agreed to a four-year, $110 million extension with the Green Bay Packers. He is the second Green Bay receiver to sign an extension this offseason following Jayden Reed.
news.impact: Watson put together his best season on a per game basis in 2025 after coming back from an injury that forced him to miss the first seven weeks of the season. It’s quite a lot of money for a receiver who has been plagued with health issues and never had more than 620 receiving yards in a year. But to be fair to him, he averaged 13.2 PPR PPG in 2025 and he’s seen by many as a sleeper in 2026. This could certainly be the year he comes alive for the Packers offense.

news.head: Christian Watson does not see the field in Week 18
news.body: Christian Watson was dressed but did not see the field on Sunday during the Packers' 16-3 loss to Minnesota in the final week of the regular season.
news.impact: Watson, along with most of Green Bay's regular starters, did not play on Sunday. He finishes the regular season with 35 catches for 611 yards and six touchdowns in 10 games. He will be back in the starting lineup next weekend for the Wild Card round of the postseason.

news.head: Christian Watson goes for 113 yards in loss
news.body: Christian Watson caught five of six targets for 113 yards and a score in the Packers' 41-24 loss to the Ravens on Saturday.
news.impact: Watson led all Packers pass catchers in receptions, yards, and targets. It's his best game of the season to date and a nice bounce back after two down games. Overall, it looks like he's finally become the Packers' WR1, but we all know that can change quickly.

news.head: Trevor Lawrence flawless in big win over Browns
news.body: Trevor Lawrence completed 18-of-23 passes for 245 yards and four touchdowns in the Jaguars' 34-10 win over the Browns. He also ran twice for three yards.
news.impact: Lawrence played on easy mode against a Browns defense that just couldn't create stops. He had only five incompletions to four touchdowns on the day, a great ratio to have. With their win over the Browns, the Jags are the only AFC South team to clinch a win on Sunday. He faces a much tougher test against the Broncos next week.

news.head: Trevor Lawrence: Jaguars starters 'trending' towards playing Friday
news.body: Jaguars head coach Liam Coen said he is “trending toward” playing the starters in Friday’s preseason game against the Panthers.
news.impact: The Jaguars starters did not see the field in last week's preseason opener. If they do play, it'll likely be in limited fashion.

news.head: Trevor Lawrence tosses three touchdowns in win
news.body: Trevor Lawrence completed 22-of-30 passes for 255 yards and three touchdowns in the Jaguars 41-7 win over the Titans. He also ran twice for 11 yards.
news.impact: Lawrence capped off a great season with a dominant performance against the lowly Titans. It wasn't always pretty, and there were plenty of struggles early on this season, but HC Liam Coen and Lawrence were able to get things rolling. The team is looking like they could be a tough out in the postseason, but time will tell.

news.head: Trevor Lawrence rushes for two touchdowns Sunday
news.body: Trevor Lawrence completed 23-of-37 passes for 263 yards with one interception in the Jaguars 23-17 win over the Colts.
news.impact: The big part of Lawrences day was the two touchdowns he scored on the ground as a rusher. He continued his strong finish to the fantasy season during the playoffs the past few weeks. Lawrence should play in Week 18 with the Jaguars needing a win.

news.head: Ravens D/ST stifles Colts in Week 1 win
news.body: The Ravens D/ST recorded two sacks, one fumble recovery, and one interception in a Week 1 win over the Indianapolis Colts.
news.impact: The defense stood tall in the season opener for first-year head coach Jesse Minter, allowing less than 275 offensive yards in the win. The unit will look to take advantage of a favorable Week 2 contest against the New Orleans Saints.

news.head: Baltimore Ravens hire Jesse Minter as Head Coach
news.body: The Baltimore Ravens are hiring former Los Angeles Chargers DC Jesse Minter as their new head coach.
news.impact: It was reported Minter turned down the Browns second interview as he saw better opportunity elsewhere, and this certainly fits the bill. He’ll look to take over the mantle of John Harbaugh and get the Ravens back into the playoff race in 2026 with Lamar Jackson at the helm of the offense and a talented defense to boot.

news.head: Baltimore Ravens parting ways with John Harbaugh
news.body: The Baltimore Ravens are reportedly parting ways with head coach John Harbaugh after 18 seasons. He was the second-longest-tenured head coach in the NFL.
news.impact: Harbaugh and the Ravens missed the playoffs this year, and there seemed to be some tension that was not present in recent seasons. Now, the Ravens are resetting with the coach in charge, a massive change for an organization that was 180-113 with Harbaugh at the helm. Harbaugh is a Super Bowl champion and should immediately be one of the top candidates for current vacancies.

news.head: Ravens D/ST allows 26 points in Week 18
news.body: The Ravens D/ST allowed 26 points while notching two sacks in a 26-24 loss to the Steelers in Week 18.
news.impact: Baltimore allowed the Steelers to gain 390 yards of total offense in the loss, which caused the Ravens to miss the playoffs. The Ravens struggled on defense in 2025 and will look to address that unit this offseason.

news.head: Javonte Williams scores twice in loss Sunday
news.body: Javonte Williams rushed the ball 12 times for 41 yards and a touchdown and caught five passes for 31 yards and another touchdown in Sunday night's 28-20 loss to the New York Giants.
news.impact: Williams was arguably Dallas' most impactful offensive player on Sunday night. He scored two touchdowns and totaled 72 yards on a night where the entire offense struggled, leaving him with a surprisingly good fantasy total on the week. He is clearly the team's bellcow running back at this point and should be viewed as a high quality fantasy option for the foreseeable future.

news.head: Javonte Williams remains Cowboys lead back in 2026
news.body: Javonte Williams remains as Dallas’ lead back by a comfortable margin headed into 2026 following a breakout campaign that ended with him signing a three year extension with the team.
news.impact: Williams has the bell-cow, or at least the lead role, on lockdown. However, what’s primarily in question is who will be backing him up, as Jaydon Blue, Malik Davis, and Phil Mafah are all vying for the role. It appears Dallas, while comfortable with Williams, doesn’t want to put the same sort of workload on him again this season as he had in 2025. That could hurt his upside unless he becomes more proficient in the passing game, but on volume alone he should maintain RB2 status.

news.head: Javonte Williams lands three year deal with Dallas
news.body: Javonte Williams has landed a three year deal with the Dallas Cowboys, with $16 million guaranteed.
news.impact: The former Bronco cashes in after a big season in Dallas. Expectations were fairly low for the veteran back, who was coming off of multiple injuries and disappointing seasons, but he crushed expectations to the tune of 1,200 rushing yards and 11 rushing touchdowns. He is a strong RB2 heading into 2026 with RB1 upside.

news.head: Javonte Williams (shoulder/neck) placed on IR
news.body: Javonte Williams (shoulder/neck) has been placed on Injured Reserve with shoulder and neck injuries.
news.impact: Williams was ruled out for Week 18, with Jaydon Blue expected to take on the workload in his absence. It’s a sad end to an otherwise great season for Williams, who will likely see a lot of interest from teams in free agency, but don’t be surprised if he comes back to Dallas.

news.head: Christian McCaffrey racks up 88 scrimmage yards in win
news.body: Christian McCaffrey ran 10 times for 68 yards and caught five of eight targets for 20 yards in the 49ers' 27-7 win over the Rams on Thursday.
news.impact: McCaffrey surprisingly had a split backfield with Kaelon Black, at least much more than expected. The veteran tied Black in touches, 15 to 15, but had the edge in opportunities, 18 to 15, thanks to receiving. It will be interesting to see if this is a Week 1 fluke or a recurring theme, as Black was involved throughout the game, not just when the game was well in hand. Still, CMC is a top-tier asset, and while today was fine, bigger days are ahead.

news.head: Christian McCaffrey would have practiced if it wasn't joint practice
news.body: 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan said RB Christian McCaffrey would have practiced on Tuesday if it wasn't a joint practice.
news.impact: Shanahan refuted the idea that McCaffrey isn't practicing because of a contract-related issue. McCaffrey remains day-to-day.

news.head: Christian McCaffrey remains absent from practice Sunday
news.body: Christian McCaffrey is still not practicing on Sunday.
news.impact: McCaffrey has been absent from practice this week due to tightness. It remains unclear how serious of an injury he is dealing with. His status will need to continue to be monitored in practice this week.

news.head: Christian McCaffrey still not practicing Tuesday due to tightness
news.body: Christian McCaffrey remains absent from practice on Tuesday due to tightness.
news.impact: It appears to be precautionary for McCaffrey. He remains day-to-day.

news.head: Amon-Ra St. Brown hauls in 10 receptions in Week 1 win over Saints
news.body: Amon-Ra St. Brown hauled in 10 of his team-leading 14 targets for 67 yards and two touchdowns in the Lions' 31-30 Week 1 win over the New Orleans Saints.
news.impact: St. Brown was dynamic in the season-opening contest for head coach Dan Campbell, hauling in both of quarterback Jared Goff's touchdown passes in the win. The wideout remains an elite WR1 option in all formats ahead of a Week 2 road matchup against the Buffalo Bills.

news.head: Amon-Ra St. Brown has contract restructured by Lions
news.body: The Lions restructured the contract of WR Amon-Ra St. Brown.
news.impact: LT Penei Sewell also had his contract restructured. The Lions created $35.68 million in cap space.

news.head: Amon-Ra St. Brown catches 11 passes in Week 18
news.body: Amon-Ra St. Brown caught 11-of-15 targets for a game-high 139 yards in Detroit's Week 18 victory over the Bears.
news.impact: St. Brown closed out the year on a high note by registering his fifth 100-yard receiving effort of the season. It was also the second time this year that he caught more than 10 passes in a game. St. Brown remains one of the top receivers in the game and he closes out the year with 117 catches for 1,401 yards and 11 scores.

news.head: Amon-Ra St. Brown (knee) active for Week 18
news.body: Amon-Ra St. Brown (knee) is active for Week 18 for the Detroit Lions against the Chicago Bears.
news.impact: St. Brown is good to go after passing through pregame tests on the injured knee without any issues, offering quarterback Jared Goff is most reliable pass-catching option against a tough Chicago defense in the season finale Sunday. The wideout remains a WR1 option in all formats.

news.head: Drake Maye throws three interceptions in loss Wednesday
news.body: Drake Maye completed 23-of-33 passing attempts for 178 yards, one touchdown, and three interceptions while adding 47 yards on the ground in Wednesday night's 13-10 loss to the Seattle Seahawks.
news.impact: Maye started the season on the wrong foot on Wednesday night. He threw for under 200 yards and three interceptions against a tough Seattle defense, including one that cost the Patriots the game. He still showed lots of ability on the ground, however, and he's likely to return to being a good fantasy option against easier defenses. The loss of A.J. Brown (ankle) for at least a few games will severely hamper his short-term upside, however.

news.head: Drake Maye (shoulder) off injury report for Super Bowl
news.body: Drake Maye is not on the injury report for the Super Bowl against the Seahawks.
news.impact: Maye was able to practice fully all week. He is officially good to go for the biggest game of the season on Sunday.

news.head: Drake Maye (shoulder) logs full practice Thursday
news.body: Drake Maye was a full participant in practice on Thursday.
news.impact: Maye has logged two straight full practices to begin the week. He remains on track to be a full-go on Sunday in the Super Bowl.

news.head: Drake Maye (shoulder) logs full practice Wednesday
news.body: Drake Maye was a full participant in practice on Wednesday.
news.impact: Maye was a full participant as he had told reporters. He remains on track to be a full-go on Sunday.

news.head: Courtland Sutton uninvolved in loss Monday
news.body: Courtland Sutton caught 2-of-5 targets for just 11 yards in Monday night's 31-10 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs.
news.impact: Denver's offense as a whole struggled heavily on Monday night, and Sutton was no exception to that. He caught just two of his five targets over the course of the game and was only able to turn that into a measly 11 yards. He remains off of the fantasy radar for the foreseeable future, even in more favorable matchups.

news.head: Courtland Sutton in full pads at practice Friday
news.body: Courtland Sutton was seen in full pads to begin practice on Friday.
news.impact: It is a positive sign after Sutton missed practice on Tuesday and Wednesday before he was limited in his return on Thursday. It appears he should be able to do more in practice on Friday.

news.head: Courtland Sutton being limited early in training camp
news.body: Broncos WR Courtland Sutton is “being limited as part of the team’s ‘protocols’ for the veteran wide receiver.”
news.impact: It explains why Sutton was not seen practicing on Tuesday or Wednesday. He returned to practice on Thursday, but he was still held out of team drills. He should continue to be ramped up as we get closer to the season.

news.head: Courtland Sutton to return to practice Thursday
news.body: Broncos coach Sean Payton said WR Courtland Sutton will return to practice on Thursday.
news.impact: Sutton did not practice on Tuesday or Wednesday which raised some concern. Payton listed it as "intentional load management" for Sutton.

news.head: Cam Skattebo leads team in rushing Sunday
news.body: Cam Skattebo rushed the ball 18 times for 81 yards and a touchdown in Sunday night's 28-20 win over the Dallas Cowboys.
news.impact: Skattebo looked pretty solid in his first game back from an injury that ended his 2025 season early. He led the team in rushing yards and scored a touchdown against the Cowboys, and he was clearly the team's top RB in terms of carries, outnumbering the next closest back three to one in that area. He didn't see a single target or catch over the course of the night, however. If Devin Singletary and Tyrone Tracy Jr. continue to serve as the team's primary receiving backs, Skattebo's fantasy ceiling could be capped by that on a week-to-week basis.

news.head: Cam Skattebo practices Saturday
news.body: Cam Skattebo participated in Saturday’s practice.
news.impact: Raanan noted that Skattebo was limited, but seemed fine. He left practice early on Friday following a collision, but it had appeared to be precautionary.

news.head: Cam Skattebo suffers apparent injury during practice Friday
news.body: Cam Skattebo left practice early on Friday.
news.impact: Skattebo went down after a collision with LB Arvell Reese. He remained on the sideline, but didn't return to practice. The Giants will be cautious with him.

news.head: Cam Skattebo (leg) "good to go" for first day of training camp
news.body: Giants general manager Joe Schoen said Cam Skattebo is "good to go" for the first day of training camp on Wednesday.
news.impact: This was expected, but it is a good sign to see Skattebo seemingly fully healthy heading into the beginning of training camp. The 24-year-old rushed for 410 yards and five touchdowns in eight games last season and should be the undisputed lead running back for the Giants heading into this year.

news.head: Broncos D/ST dismal in loss Monday
news.body: The Broncos' D/ST logged two sacks and one interception while allowing 31 points in Monday night's blowout loss to the Kansas City Chiefs.
news.impact: Denver's defense is supposed to be among the best in the entire NFL, but they didn't look the part on Monday night. They allowed Patrick Mahomes II to lead Kansas City to 31 points on the night, despite the fact that this was his first game back from a major injury and was missing one of his starting tackles. This unit should return to elite form at some point this season, but they have a rocky schedule coming up for the next 4-6 weeks and should not be considered an elite fantasy option at the position for that stretch of games.

news.head: Broncos D/ST scores touchdown in Week 18 win
news.body: The Broncos' D/ST logged four sacks, one interception, one fumble recovery, and a touchdown while allowing just three points in Sunday's win over the Los Angeles Chargers.
news.impact: Denver's defense has been among the best in the league all season long, and they had a suitable performance to end the regular season on Sunday. They logged four sacks and two turnovers against the Chargers, one of which they were able to take to the house for a touchdown. This unit will make life hard for any team they end up playing in the postseason.

news.head: Denver defense dominates on Christmas Day
news.body: The Broncos defense surrendered 13 points on only 139 yards of total offense, registering one sack in Thursday's win over the Chiefs.
news.impact: This Christmas, the Broncos defense was given the gift of a struggling Chiefs offense led by a third-string QB making his first career start. The Denver unit took full advantage, shutting down the Chiefs on the ground and through the air. The Broncos feature a strong defense, but the task will be more difficult against the Chargers in Week 18.

news.head: Broncos D/ST struggles in loss Sunday
news.body: The Broncos' D/ST logged five sacks and allowed 34 points in Sunday's loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars.
news.impact: Denver's defense had a bad game on Sunday. Jacksonville put up the most points on them out of any team this season with 34, and the Broncos weren't able to log any big turnovers to help turn the tide of the game. This unit should bounce back and have a good game against the Chiefs on Christmas Day, however.

news.head: Dalton Kincaid has breakout game against Texans
news.body: Dalton Kincaid caught five of six targets for 130 yards in the Bills’ 36-31 win over the Texans on Sunday.
news.impact: Kincaid had arguably his best game as a pro, acheiving a career-high 130 receiving yards in what should have been tough sledding against Houston. He tied with Khalil Shakir for second in targets on the Bills, but vastly outproduced Shakir in yards. His downfield usage was encouraging, and it’s a promising start to his fourth season. Now to see if it keeps up.

news.head: Dalton Kincaid gets fifth-year option picked up
news.body: The Buffalo Bills have exercised the fifth-year option on TE Dalton Kincaid.
news.impact: Kincaid, a former first-round pick, is coming off his most efficient NFL season. The 26-year-old tight end hauled in 39 receptions for 571 receiving yards and 5 touchdowns. His contract is now guaranteed through 2027 as he continues to operate as one of Josh Allen’s top pass-catching options.

news.head: Dalton Kincaid (knee) not expected to require offseason surgery
news.body: Dalton Kincaid said “does not anticipate” undergoing surgery this offseason.
news.impact: It came out after the season that Kincaid played the 2025 season with a torn PCL. As of now, he should be healthy heading into the Bills offseason program.

news.head: Dalton Kincaid believed to have played entire 2025 season with torn PCL
news.body: Dawson Knox said on on Monday Mornings with Mitch that Dalton Kincaid played the entire 2025 season with a torn PCL.
news.impact: It was also confirmed by Bills beat writer Ryan Talbot who noted that “a source close to Kincaid confirmed what Knox said” on the podcast. Kincaid was consistently on the injury report most of the season with a knee injury, but it was never reported to be as bad as a torn PCL. He will likely require surgery this offseason.

news.head: Rome Odunze quiet in Week 1
news.body: Rome Odunze caught two of his three targets for 52 yards in the Bears' 59-37 Week 1 win over the Carolina Panthers
news.impact: Odunze made the most of minimal usage in the Chicago passing attack in the season opener, averaging 26.0 yards per reception in the win. the wideout provides head coach Ben Johnson with one of many dynamic pass-catching options ahead of a Week 2 matchup against the Minnesota Vikings.

news.head: Rome Odunze (calf) active for Week 1
news.body: Rome Odunze (calf) is officially active for Week 1 for the Chicago Bears against the Carolina Panthers.
news.impact: Odunze is good to go after passing through pregame testing without any setbacks from the calf injury, offering head coach Ben Johnson another dynamic pass-catching option for quarterback Caleb Williams against the Panthers Sunday.

news.head: Rome Odunze (calf) expected to play against Carolina
news.body: Rome Odunze (calf) is expected to play against the Carolina Panthers on Sunday.
news.impact: The Bears made several receiver moves on Saturday, bringing doubt to Odunze's status. However, it does look like the young receiver will play. He's worth starting, but temper expectations a little.

news.head: Rome Odunze (calf) questionable to play Sunday
news.body: Rome Odunze (calf) is questionable to play in Sunday's game against the Carolina Panthers.
news.impact: Odunze has been limited at practice all week due to a calf injury, and now it is threatening to leave him sidelined for the team's season opener on Sunday. He is officially considered questionable to play, and the team will make a final determination about his availability closer to game time. Luther Burden III will be a great fantasy option if Odunze is ruled out, with Zavion Thomas also likely to step up and see more work.

news.head: David Montgomery has big debut for Texans
news.body: David Montgomery rushed for 60 yards and two scores on 20 carries, adding three receptions for 19 yards and another touchdown in Sunday's 36-31 loss to the Bills.
news.impact: Montgomery was given 23 touches in his debut with the Texans, as the veteran back was a focal point of the offense. Granted, he only averaged 3.0 yards per carry, but he found the end zone three times while being involved both on the ground and through the air.

news.head: David Montgomery traded to Houston Texans
news.body: David Montgomery has been traded to the Houston Texans. Houston is sending a fourth rounder, OL Juice Scruggs, and a seventh back to Detroit.
news.impact: Montgomery had made it known he wanted a new opportunity given his lack of usage last year, and the Texans came calling. Monty offers a big upgrade over Nick Chubb as the primary thumper, and his ability in the passing game could easily endanger Woody Marks value as well. For dynasty, it’s great for Montgomery and Jahmyr Gibbs managers, while Marks managers will have to deal with a much bigger threat to any potential volume. This also likely means Joe Mixon, who missed all of last season, is done in Houston.

news.head: David Montgomery gets eight carries in Week 18
news.body: David Montgomery carried the ball eight times for 42 yards and added one catch for 13 yards in Detroit's win over Chicago on Sunday.
news.impact: Montgomery has seen his production drop over the last couple of seasons as Jahmyr Gibbs has emerged as the lead back for the Lions. The seventh-year running back still had a solid campaign with 158 carries for 716 yards and eight scores. However, the carries and the rushing yards were new career-lows for Montgomery.

news.head: David Montgomery quiet in Week 17 loss
news.body: David Montgomery rushed 10 times for 25 yards while also catching both of his targets for 15 yards in the Lions' 23-10 loss to the Vikings in Week 17.
news.impact: Montgomery has struggled to make an impact out of the Detroit backfield of late, finishing with 40 or less offensive yards in each of his last three games. The running back remains a difficult option for fantasy managers to trust in any format ahead of a Week 18 matchup against the Chicago Bears.

news.head: Jalen Coker (ankle) in walking boot, not expected to miss time this week
news.body: Jalen Coker was in a walking boot on Monday, but he is not expected to miss time this week.
news.impact: Coker rolled his left ankle in the first quarter on Sunday. He still went on to have a career day. His status will have to be monitored this week, but he is currently expected to be good to go for Week 2.

news.head: Jalen Coker leads pass-catchers in Week 1 loss to Bears
news.body: Jalen Coker hauled in eight of his team-leading nine targets for 138 yards and two touchdowns in the Panthers' 59-37 Week 1 loss to the Chicago Bears.
news.impact: Coker capitalized on sizeable involvement in the Carolina passing attack, averaging 17.3 yards per reception while leading the team in receiving yards in the loss. The wideout forms a dynamic duo with Tetairoa McMillan for head coach Dave Canales, with a Week 2 contest against the Atlanta Falcons up next.

news.head: Jalen Coker agrees to 3-year, $35 million extension with Panthers
news.body: Jalen Coker has come to an agreement with the Carolina Panthers on a contract extension of 3-years, $35 million with incentives that could drive it up to $41 million.
news.impact: The former UDFA has shown some promising moments in his tenure with the Panthers, notably having a 100 yard game in their playoff showdown against the Rams last season and has brought home quite the bag. He should find himself as the presumed WR2 for the offense.

news.head: Jalen Coker signs exclusive rights tender with Panthers
news.body: Jalen Coker inked his exclusive rights free agent tender on Monday to remain in Carolina for the 2026 season.
news.impact: Coker was tendered by Carolina in early March and made his return to the team official on Monday. The wideout, who will enter his third NFL season in 2026, caught 33 passes for 394 and three touchdowns in 11 games last season - very similar to the 32-478-2 line he posted as a rookie in 2024, also in 11 games. However, in last year's Wild Card round loss to the Rams, Coker hauled in nine passes for 134 yards and a score, which could signal another step forward in 2026 as he and quarterback Bryce Young continue to grow and get on the same page together.

news.head: Jordan Mason being evaluated for sore thumb
news.body: Vikings head coach O'Connell said RB Jordan Mason is being evaluated for a sore thumb.
news.impact: Mason came into the building on Monday with the injury. He is day-to-day for now after leading the backfield on Sunday.

news.head: Jordan Mason sees 15 carries Sunday
news.body: Jordan Mason ran for 59 yards and a touchdown on 15 carries in the Vikings 39-22 win over the Packers.
news.impact: Mason led the way in the Vikings backfield as both he and Aaron Jones saw double-digit carries. He will be in the low-end RB2 conversation next week against the Bears.

news.head: Jordan Mason rushes for game-high 94 yards Sunday
news.body: Jordan Mason carried the ball 14 times for 94 yards as the Vikings defeated the Packers, 16-3, in the regular season finale.
news.impact: Mason finished his first season in Minnesota as the team's leading rusher with 758 yards despite only starting five games for the Vikings. His 94 yards on the ground on Sunday was his second-highest total of the season. With both Mason and Aaron Jones on affordable contracts for next season, the duo figure to form a similar backfield timeshare in 2026.

news.head: Jordan Mason (ankle) removed from injury report for Week 18
news.body: Jordan Mason has been removed from the injury report for Sunday's game against the Packers.
news.impact: Aaron Jones was ruled out. Mason should lead the backfield in the season finale as a result.

news.head: Mark Andrews sees six targets in Week 1 win
news.body: Mark Andrews hauled in four of his six targets for 49 yards in the Ravens' 41-23 Week 1 win over the Indianapolis Colts.
news.impact: Andrews received sizeable volume in the Baltimore passing attack, finishing tied for first in targets in the win. The veteran tight end remains a reliable option ahead of a Week 2 matchup against the New Orleans Saints.

news.head: Mark Andrews catches two passes in Week 18
news.body: Mark Andrews caught two of his three targets for 14 yards in a 26-24 loss to the Steelers in Week 18.
news.impact: Andrews was quiet as the Ravens lost the AFC North and will miss the playoffs. The veteran tight end wraps up his 2025 season with 48 catches for 422 yards and five touchdowns while appearing in all 17 of the Ravens' games. Andrews' days as an elite tight end appear to be over as the team did not prioritize getting him the ball in 2025.

news.head: Mark Andrews snags four passes in win
news.body: Mark Andrews caught all four of his targets for 28 yards in the Ravens' 41-24 win over the Packers.
news.impact: You would think Andrews would have a better game given the number of points the Ravens put up, but it was almost all done on the ground. He's tough to trust for fantasy at this point.

news.head: Mark Andrews quiet in loss Sunday
news.body: Mark Andrews caught 2-of-3 targets for 21 yards in Sunday's 28-24 loss to the New England Patriots.
news.impact: Andrews didn't have a productive game on Sunday. He caught just two passes against the Patriots and nearly had a costly fumble close to halftime, although it didn't hold up. He isn't expected to be fantasy relevant for the last couple games of the season.

news.head: Isaiah Likely hauls in two touchdowns in win Sunday
news.body: Isaiah Likely caught eight passes for 78 yards and two touchdowns in Sunday night's 28-20 win over the Dallas Cowboys.
news.impact: Likely exceeded expectations in his first game as a Giant on Sunday. He led the team in receptions, receiving yards, and touchdowns on the night, scoring twice in what turned out to be a huge win over the Cowboys. His involvement on this offense looks great right now and he will likely be one of the hot waiver additions this week in any league he's not already rostered in.

news.head: Isaiah Likely signs three-year deal with Giants
news.body: The Giants are signing Isaiah Likely to a three-year, $40 million contract.
news.impact: The deal is worth to $47.5 million as Likely reunites with John Harbaugh. He should take on a bigger role with the Giants than what he had in Baltimore. He will be on the TE1 radar for fantasy managers.

news.head: Isaiah Likely to draw interest from Giants
news.body: The Giants are expected to show interest in free agent TE Isaiah Likely.
news.impact: Likely has history with new Giants head coach John Harbaugh. New York will be looking to bring in more offensive weapons to help the development of Jaxson Dart as they're likely losing Wan'Dale Robinson in free agency. Likely is one of the top tight ends available in free agency.

news.head: Isaiah Likely catches two passes in Week 18
news.body: Isaiah Likely caught both of his targets for 32 yards in a 26-24 loss to the Steelers in Week 18.
news.impact: Likely was the Ravens' third-leading receiver in the costly loss which caused Baltimore to miss the playoffs. The veteran tight end finishes 2025 with 27 catches for 307 yards and one touchdown in 14 games. An unrestricted free agent this offseason, Likely's production could explode if he lands with a team that makes him their starter. His landing spot will be an interesting story to monitor this offseason.

news.head: Jakobi Meyers snags touchdown in win
news.body: Jakobi Meyers caught both of his targets for 40 yards and a touchdown in the Jaguars' 34-10 win over the Browns. He also ran once for two yards.
news.impact: Meyers didn't see a lot of targets, just two to be exact, but he made them count. Trevor Lawrence only threw the ball 21 times today, not counting throwaways, and ten different players received a target, so there wasn't much to go around. Hopefully Meyers will see more targets next week against Denver in what should be a more competitive game script.

news.head: Jakobi Meyers (thumb) good to go for Sunday
news.body: Jakobi Meyers (thumb) is good to go for Sunday's game against the Cleveland Browns.
news.impact: As expected, Meyers carries no injury designation ahead of Sunday's season opener and will be available to play against the Browns. His presence is further competition for Parker Washington and Brian Thomas Jr. in a crowded Jacksonville WR room.

news.head: Jakobi Meyers (thumb) limited again Thursday
news.body: Jakobi Meyers (thumb) was limited at practice again on Thursday.
news.impact: The veteran wideout was again limited on Thursday as he continues to recover from a thumb injury of some kind. He is already expected to play this weekend, although he may still be left with an injury designation heading into the weekend if he doesn't practice in full on Friday.

news.head: Jakobi Meyers (thumb) in non-contact jersey in practice
news.body: Jakobi Meyers was in a non-contact jersey during practice on Thursday.
news.impact: Meyers remains up in the air for Sunday's season opener. His status will need to be monitored in practice on Friday.

news.head: Josh Downs catches two passes in Week 1
news.body: Josh Downs caught two of his four targets for 37 yards in the Colts' 41-23 loss to the Baltimore Ravens in Week 1.
news.impact: Downs saw modest involvement in an underperforming Indianapolis passing attack, finishing third on the team in targets in the loss. The wideout remains one of the more risky pass-catchers entering a difficult Week 2 contest against the Kansas City Chiefs.

news.head: Josh Downs (calf) without injury designation for Sunday
news.body: Josh Downs (calf) is without an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Baltimore Ravens.
news.impact: Downs is not listed on Indianapolis' injury report heading into Week 1, meaning that his calf injury is no longer an issue and that he should be at full health at this point. Indianapolis' distribution of targets should be something fantasy managers keep a close eye on this weekend, but the 25-year old isn't projected to be a strong fantasy asset on his own to start the season.

news.head: Josh Downs (calf) practices Tuesday
news.body: Josh Downs practiced on Tuesday.
news.impact: Downs missed time last week with a calf issue. He is on track to be good to go for the season opener next week.

news.head: Josh Downs (calf) not practicing Wednesday
news.body: Josh Downs did not practice on Wednesday.
news.impact: Downs missed practice for undisclosed reasons on Tuesday and it is now said to be a calf injury. He remains day-to-day.

news.head: Romeo Doubs fails to log catch Wednesday
news.body: Romeo Doubs didn't haul in any of his three targets in Wednesday night's 10-13 loss to the Seattle Seahawks.
news.impact: Doubs did not get off to a good start with his new team on Wednesday night. He failed to haul in even a single catch against a tough Seattle defense, and he had a costly drop on a very important play late in the game. He should bounce back in the near future and may be a worthwhile fantasy option short-term with A.J. Brown (ankle) expected to miss a bit of time due to injury.

news.head: Romeo Doubs (undisclosed) does not practice Thursday
news.body: Patriots WR Romeo Doubs did not practice on Thursday.
news.impact: It is unclear what Doubs is dealing with as he did not practice on Wednesday either. It should not be a concern this early in training camp.

news.head: Romeo Doubs signs with Patriots
news.body: The Patriots have signed WR Romeo Doubs.
news.impact: The Patriots had a huge hole at wide receiver, especially after releasing Stefon Diggs. They have been in trade talks for AJ Brown, but now land Doubs in free agency. He'll have a chance to potentially step into the No. 1 wide receiver role for Drake Maye and New England. He'll hold more upside for fantasy managers than what he had in a crowded Packers offense.

news.head: Romeo Doubs drawing interest from Broncos
news.body: The Broncos have reportedly shown interest in free agent WR Romeo Doubs.
news.impact: Doubs was expected to go off the board early on Monday, but he is still available. Denver had shown interest in Kendrick Bourne, who landed in Arizona with the Cardinals.

news.head: Jordan Addison fails to catch pass Sunday
news.body: Jordan Addison did not catch either of his two targets in the Vikings 39-22 win over the Packers.
news.impact: Justin Jefferson dominated the targets after Carson Wentz took over behind center. Addison will be in the WR3/WR4 mix heading into Week 2 against a vulnerable Bears defense.

news.head: Jordan Addison (thumb) to miss day or two of practice
news.body: Vikings coach Kevin O'Connell said WR Jordan Addison will miss a day or two after jamming his thumb.
news.impact: Addison underwent tests that showed the injury will be short-term. He could return to practice by this weekend.

news.head: Jordan Addison officially has fifth-year option picked up by Vikings
news.body: The Vikings have officially exercised Jordan Addison's fifth-year option.
news.impact: It was reported over a month ago and it is now official. Addison has shown flashes of his potential across his first three seasons, while also being suspended three games for violating the league’s substance abuse policy. He was also arrested for misdemeanor trespassing charges earlier this offseason.

news.head: Jordan Addison gets fifth-year option picked up
news.body: The Minnesota Vikings have exercised the fifth-year option on WR Jordan Addison.
news.impact: Addison’s contract is now guaranteed through 2027. He projects as a mid-to-low-end WR3 heading into fantasy draft season.

news.head: Jake Ferguson quiet in loss Sunday
news.body: Jake Ferguson caught just two passes for six yards in Sunday night's 28-20 loss to the New York Giants.
news.impact: The veteran tight end didn't make an impact on Sunday night. He was held to just two catches and six total yards against the Giants, which was a symptom of Dallas' offensive struggles against their divisional rivals. Ferguson isn't expected to be fantasy relevant anytime in the foreseeable future.

news.head: Jake Ferguson restructures contract with Cowboys
news.body: The Cowboys restructured TE Jake Ferguson’s contract.
news.impact: Ferguson’s $7.25 million base salary was turned into a signing bonus. The Cowboys now have $33.2 million in salary cap space.

news.head: Jake Ferguson (personal) misses practice Saturday
news.body: Jake Ferguson missed practice on Saturday due to personal reasons.
news.impact: Ferguson was away from the team on Saturday.

news.head: Jake Ferguson catches just one pass Sunday
news.body: Jake Ferguson caught 1 of 2 targets for only five yards in Sunday's loss to the Giants.
news.impact: Ferguson did not do much in limited playing time Sunday, but he did reach 600 yards for the season to go with his 82 grabs and eight touchdowns. Mark down another productive campaign for the four-year pro.

news.head: Deebo Samuel Sr. snags touchdown in win
news.body: Deebo Samuel Sr. caught six of seven targets for 48 yards and a touchdown in the 49ers' 27-7 win over the Rams on Thursday. He also carried the ball once for 12 yards.
news.impact: Samuel looks to have come back to his old role on the 49ers, lining up everywhere and getting the ball put in his hands to make plays. He even had over 70 kick return yards. Samuel just might be a draft-day steal if they are going to use him like this throughout the season.

news.head: Deebo Samuel Sr. starting against Chargers
news.body: 49ers WR Deebo Samuel Sr. will play against the Chargers in the preseason
news.impact: Thursday night's contest could offer a closer look at the type of role Samuel will have in the 49ers' offense this season.

news.head: Deebo Samuel Sr. participates in team drills Saturday
news.body: Deebo Samuel Sr. was participating in team drills at practice on Saturday.
news.impact: Samuel returns to the practice field two days after returning to the 49ers on a one-year deal. He will be a player to continue to monitor throughout training camp heading into the season.

news.head: Deebo Samuel Sr. not practicing Friday
news.body: Deebo Samuel Sr. will not practice on Friday.
news.impact: Samuel made his return to the 49ers on a one-year contract late Friday night. He should start practicing with the team soon.

news.head: J.K. Dobbins underwhelming in loss Monday
news.body: J.K. Dobbins rushed the ball eight times for 36 yards in Monday night's 31-10 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs.
news.impact: Dobbins wasn't able to get much going on Monday night, being left with just 36 scoreless yards in a loss to the Chiefs. The game script was entirely unfavorable to his role, however, with Denver quickly abandoning the run after falling behind early in the game. He should be more involved than this in most games moving forward.

news.head: J.K. Dobbins will maintain Denver's RB1 role in 2026
news.body: Running back J.K. Dobbins will "for sure" be the Denver Broncos' lead back this season, with three players set to have roles in the backfield, according to Zac Stevens of DNVR Sports.
news.impact: Dobbins was very successful in 2025 when he was healthy, averaging 5.0 yards per carry and rushing for 772 yards in 10 games. RJ Harvey and rookie Jonah Coleman will have roles, a regular trait for head coach Sean Payton's offenses. Due to injury risk and a congested backfield, Dobbins has a deflated ADP price as the half-PPR RB34, according to FantasyPros.

news.head: J.K. Dobbins (soft tissue) practices again Wednesday
news.body: J.K. Dobbins practiced for a second straight day on Wednesday.
news.impact: Dobbins is continuing to work his way through a soft tissue injury. It is unclear how much he has been doing in practice.

news.head: J.K. Dobbins (soft tissue) participates in individual drills Tuesday
news.body: J.K. Dobbins went through individual drills at practice on Tuesday.
news.impact: Dobbins left practice on Monday with a soft-tissue injury. It appears to have just been precautionary.

news.head: Michael Mayer hauls in six receptions in Week 1 win
news.body: Michael Mayer hauled in six of his seven targets for 32 yards in the Raiders' 27-13 Week 1 win over the Miami Dolphins.
news.impact: Mayer took advantage of the absence of No. 1 tight end Brock Bowers, leading the team in targets in the win. The tight end remains a steady option as long as Bowers remains sidelined for fantasy managers, with a Week 2 matchup against the Los Angeles Chargers ahead.

news.head: Michael Mayer agrees to a three-year, $45 million deal with Raiders
news.body: Michael Mayer has agreed to a three-year, $45 million deal with the Las Vegas Raiders.
news.impact: Mayer is an all around contributor, making it well worth the investment for the Raiders. For fantasy, it means that he is behind Brock Bowers for the long term, but maybe the Raiders will employ more tight end sets so both can eat, as they are likely the two most talented pass catchers on the team at this point in time.
