Time will tell what his fantasy value will become.

news.head: Michael Mayer hauls in three passes in Week 18
news.body: Michael Mayer caught 3-of-5 targets for 47 yards in the Raiders 14-12 win over the Chiefs.
news.impact: Mayer led the team in yards and was tied for the team lead in receptions Sunday. Mayer will end the season with 328 receiving yards and one touchdown on 35 receptions.

news.head: Michael Mayer leads Raiders in receiving Sunday
news.body: Michael Mayer caught 9-of-10 targets for 89 yards in the Raiders 34-10 loss against the Giants.
news.impact: With Brock Bowers (knee) sidelined, Mayer took full advantage of the opportunity. He led the Raiders in targets, receptions and receiving yards. He'll remain a TE1 in Week 18 against the Chiefs.

news.head: Jacory Croskey-Merritt reaches end zone in Week 1 loss
news.body: Jacory Croskey-Merritt carried the ball 16 times for 63 yards and one touchdown while also catching his only target for a loss of seven yards in the Commanders’ 24-22 Week 1 loss to the Philadelphia Eagles.
news.impact: Croskey-Merritt made the most of his opportunities out of the backfield, accounting for 50% of the carries for the Commanders in Week 1. The running back seems poised to receive as much volume as he can handle as the primary option out of the backfield to begin the season for head coach Dan Quinn, with a Week 2 divisional matchup against the Dallas Cowboys up next.

news.head: Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) will play in Week 1
news.body: Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) will play in Week 1 for the Washington Commanders against the Philadelphia Eagles according to Ian Rapoport.

news.head: Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) limited participant Wednesday
news.body: Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) was a limited participant at practice on Wednesday.
news.impact: Croskey-Merritt is managing a groin injury right now and was unable to log a full practice session on Wednesday as a result. There's an off-chance that it will leave him sidelined for Week 1, which would lead to more work for Rachaad White against the Eagles.

news.head: Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) returns to practice
news.body: Jacory Croskey-Merritt returned to practice on Tuesday.
news.impact: Croskey-Merritt was absent from practice for the past week. He should be on track to be good to go for Week 1.

news.head: Jayden Reed quiet Sunday
news.body: Jayden Reed caught 3-of-7 targets for 20 yards in the Packers 39-22 loss against the Vikings.
news.impact: The seven targets were encouraging, but Reed was not anywhere near as productive as Christian Watson and Matthew Golden to open the season. He is a WR4/WR5 heading into Week 2.

news.head: Jayden Reed (ankle) returns to practice Tuesday
news.body: Jayden Reed was back at practice on Tuesday.
news.impact: Reed makes his way back after being sidelined for a few days. He worked his way back from an ankle injury.

news.head: Jayden Reed (ankle) not expected to practice Monday
news.body: Packers coach Matt LaFleur said he does not expect WR Jayden Reed to practice on Monday.
news.impact: Reed also missed practice on Sunday. He remains day-to-day. It is unknown how serious his injury is.

news.head: Jayden Reed (ankle) not practicing Sunday
news.body: Jayden Reed did not practice on Sunday due to an ankle injury.
news.impact: It is unclear how serious the injury is for Reed, who signed a three-year extension with Green Bay this offseason. He is day-to-day going into the week. There should be an update provided by coach Matt LaFleur when available.

news.head: Kyle Monangai reaches 100 yards in Week 1 win
news.body: Kyle Monangai rushed 10 times for 100 yards and one touchdown while also catching both of his targets for 24 yards in a 59-37 win over the Carolina Panthers in Week 1.
news.impact: Monangai made the most of limited touches highlighted by a 61-yard rushing touchdown in the win. The second-year running back will look to take advantage of a risky Minnesota Vikings defense in Week 2 for fantasy managers.

news.head: Kyle Monangai (knee) good to go for Week 1
news.body: Kyle Monangai (knee) is good to go for Week 1's game against the Carolina Panthers.
news.impact: Monangai will be good to go for the season opener on Sunday, despite recently dealing with a knee injury of some kind. He isn't expected to be fantasy relevant with D'Andre Swift set to get the start and the bulk of the work for the Bears.

news.head: Kyle Monangai (knee) at practice Monday
news.body: Kyle Monangai was at practice on Monday.
news.impact: Monangai was considered week-to-week to end training camp. His presence at practice on Monday gives him a chance to be available for Sunday’s season opener.

news.head: Kyle Monangai (knee) remains week-to-week
news.body: The Bears say Kyle Monangai remains week-to-week.
news.impact: Monangai has been considered week-to-week for the past couple of weeks. It appears he won't be ready to go to begin the season, which should lead to a workhorse role for D'Andre Swift to open the year.

news.head: Khalil Shakir goes for 50 yards in win
news.body: Khalil Shakir caught four of six targets for 50 yards in the Bills’ 36-31 win over Houston on Sunday.
news.impact: Shakir operated as Josh Allen’s safety valve underneath with DJ Moore and Dalton Kincaid working over the top. That’s been Shakir’s role in the past, so don’t expect it to stop any time soon. His upside is capped because of it, but he’s a decent flex play in PPR formats if you need a solid floor.

news.head: Khalil Shakir good to go for Sunday
news.body: Khalil Shakir will be good to go for Sunday's game against the Houston Texans.
news.impact: Shakir was a full participant at practice on Wednesday and is expected to be fully good to go for Sunday's season opener against the Houston Texans. He is not worth starting for fantasy purposes at this point, however, especially with DJ Moore now in town for the Bills.

news.head: Khalil Shakir (undisclosed) seen practicing Wednesday
news.body: Khalil Shakir (undisclosed) was seen practicing for the Bills on Wednesday.
news.impact: Shakir's availability for Week 1 is currently up in the air due to an undisclosed injury that he's dealing with. He was spotted at practice on Wednesday, however, which bodes well for his availability for the season opener. It remains unclear if he was a limited or full participant.

news.head: Khalil Shakir (undisclosed) 'optimistic' for Week 1
news.body: There's "currently optimism” from the Bills that Khalil Shakir will play in Week 1 against the Texans.
news.impact: Shakir has been sidelined from practice for the past couple of weeks due to an undisclosed injury. Buffalo is reportedly being cautious with him.

news.head: Dalton Schultz hauls in four passes
news.body: Dalton Schultz secured 4-of-8 targets for 35 yards in Sunday's 36-31 loss to the Bills.
news.impact: Schultz caught a career-high 82 passes last season, and he remains a steady presence in the Texans' offense. The veteran tight end finished second on the team with eight targets, trailing only Nico Collins' 10. Schultz has a limited ceiling, but he's almost always on the TE streaming radar.

news.head: Dalton Schultz signs one-year extension with Texans
news.body: The Texans and TE Dalton Schultz have agreed to terms on a one-year extension worth $12.6 million.
news.impact: Schultz will now earn $17.6 million guaranteed combining the 2026 and 2027 seasons. He was a safety blanket for CJ Stroud for much of last season and that will likely remain the case again this upcoming year.

news.head: Dalton Schultz (calf) ruled out for rest of game Sunday
news.body: Dalton Schultz has been ruled out for the remainder of Sunday's Divisional Round game against the Patriots.
news.impact: It is a tough break for a Texans offense already missing Nico Collins. Christian Kirk and Jayden Higgins will be among the players to step into bigger roles in the passing game for Houston.

news.head: Dalton Schultz (calf) questionable to return Sunday
news.body: Dalton Schultz is questionable to return to Sunday's Divisional Round game against the Patriots with a calf injury.
news.impact: Schultz was seen walking back to the locker room. It is a tough break for a Texans offense already without Nico Collins.

news.head: KC Concepcion snags four passes in loss to Jags
news.body: KC Concepcion caught four of five targets for 43 yards in the Browns' 34-10 loss to the Jaguars. He also ran the ball three times for 15 yards.
news.impact: While it wasn't a massive day, it was encouraging that Concepcion got touches as both a receiver and out of the backfield, showing the team wanted to get the ball in his hands. A loss is a loss, but brighter days should be ahead for Concepcion.

news.head: KC Concepcion (shoulder) returns to practice Tuesday
news.body: KC Concepcion was back at practice on Tuesday at Browns training camp.
news.impact: Concepcion landed hard on his shoulder that forced him out of Monday's practice early. He is back one day later.

news.head: KC Concepcion (shoulder) avoids serious injury
news.body: Browns rookie WR KC Concepcion is believed to have avoided a serious shoulder injury on Monday.
news.impact: Concepcion left practice on Monday with a shoulder injury after a hard fall. The team expects him to be fine.

news.head: KC Concepcion (knee) medically cleared
news.body: Browns coach Todd Monken said KC Concepcion has been cleared medically and is good to go.
news.impact: Concepcion participated in individual and team drills on Friday. He had a knee scope in March, which led to the team monitoring his reps previously.

news.head: Brenton Strange grabs touchdown in win over Browns
news.body: Brenton Strange caught two of three targets for 23 yards and a touchdown in the Jaguars' 34-10 win over the Browns on Sunday.
news.impact: Strange was among ten other targeted receivers who were trying to feast off of an extremely small pie of 21 total targets. And he was one of the lucky ones with a touchdown. He should continue to see work as the top tight end for the offense, but things are so spread out that it might be hard to rely on him on a weekly basis.

news.head: Brenton Strange signs three-year extension with Jaguars
news.body: The Jaguars signed Brenton Strange to a three-year contract extension.
news.impact: The deal is worth “up to” $48 million with $25 million guaranteed. Strange missed five games last season, but emerged as a top threat in the passing game when he was healthy for Trevor Lawrence last season. Strange profiles as a borderline TE1 for fantasy managers with Nate Boerkircher and Tanner Koziol competing for snaps behind him.

news.head: Brenton Strange could be offense’s most important player’ behind Lawrence
news.body: Brenton Strange could the the Jags ‘“most important player” aside from Trevor Lawrence, according to Jags beat John Shipley. Shipley notes than despite missing five games last year, Strange still finished third in routes run.
news.impact: Strange is far and away the Jags TE1, and it doesn’t seem anyone is taking that job away from him. Tanner Koziol is next up as a pass catcher, but the rookie out of Houston is the TE3 at the moment and unlikely to impact Strange’s workload.

news.head: Brenton Strange snags touchdown in win
news.body: Brenton Strange caught all six of his targets for 52 yards and a score in the Jaguars' 41-7 win over the Titans.
news.impact: Strange closed out the season with some nice numbers and was a viable tight end streamer. He had at least five targets in five of the Jaguars' last seven games, with three touchdowns to boot. It will be tough for him to be a high-end fantasy tight end given his target competition, but he should be a decent streamer in the right matchup in 2026.

news.head: Devaughn Vele finds end zone in Week 1 loss to Lions
news.body: Devaughn Vele hauled in seven of his nine targets for 69 yards and one touchdown in the Saints' 31-30 Week 1 loss to the Detroit Lions.
news.impact: Vele capitalized on a sizeable role in the New Orleans passing attack, finishing second in targets, receptions, and receiving yards in a losing effort. The wideout looks poised to offer head coach Kellen Moore another impactful pass-catching option in the New Orleans offense moving forward, with a Week 2 contest against the Baltimore Ravens up next.

news.head: Devaughn Vele (shoulder) placed on IR
news.body: The Saints placed Devaughn Vele on injured reserve.
news.impact: Vele will miss the rest of the season. He finishes the year having caught 25 passes for 293 yards and two touchdowns after being traded to the Saints mid-season.

news.head: Devaughn Vele (shoulder) out on Sunday against Jets
news.body: Devaughn Vele (shoulder) has been ruled out for the Saints game against the Jets on Sunday.
news.impact: Vele was having a bit of a breakout the last few weeks, but that is now on hold. Mason Tipton will likely fill the WR2 role in the offense, but the vacated targets will likely find their way to Chris Olave, Juwan Johnson, and the running backs than Tipton himself seeing a large bump in usage.

news.head: Devaughn Vele (shoulder) considered week-to-week
news.body: The Saints say WR Devaughn Vele is considered week-to-week with a shoulder injury.
news.impact: Vele avoided a major injury to his shoulder. It is unclear if he will return for the final three games this season.

news.head: RJ Harvey totals 41 yards in loss Monday
news.body: RJ Harvey rushed the ball three times for 18 yards and caught four passes for 23 yards in Monday night's 31-10 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs.
news.impact: The young running back was one of Denver's more effective offensive players on Monday night, which isn't saying much considering he finished with just 41 scoreless yards in the team's loss to the Chiefs. It looks like J.K. Dobbins will be the team's top rushing option this season, but it's encouraging to see Harvey's involvement in the passing game in Week 1, which is his path to relevance over the course of the season.

news.head: RJ Harvey (torn labrum) progressing in right direction
news.body: Broncos coach Sean Payton said the team is "pleased with how RJ Harvey is progressing."
news.impact: It was recently revealed that Harvey underwent offseason surgery to repair a torn labrum. He participated in 7-on-7 drills in practice on Wednesday.

news.head: RJ Harvey underwent offseason surgery to repair torn labrum
news.body: RJ Harvey reportedly underwent surgery this offseason to repair a torn labrum he suffered in the AFC Championship Game loss to the Patriots.
news.impact: This had not been previously reported. Harvey was able to do some work during Broncos OTAs. His status will need to continue to be monitored into training camp as he competes for touches with J.K. Dobbins and Jonah Coleman.

news.head: RJ Harvey inefficient in Week 18 win
news.body: RJ Harvey rushed the ball 15 times for 28 yards and caught 1-of-4 targets for five yards in Sunday's 19-3 win over the Los Angeles Chargers.
news.impact: The rookie has been a good fantasy option over the last stretch of the regular season, but he had a bad season finale on Sunday. He was only able to rack up a measly 33 scoreless yards against the Chargers, despite seeing 19 opportunities over the course of the game. Any fantasy managers still playing in Week 18 were let down with his performance in this matchup.

news.head: Caleb Douglas leads pass-catchers in Week 1 loss to Raiders
news.body: Caleb Douglas caught five of his team-high seven targets for 94 yards in the Dolphins' 27-13 loss to the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 1.
news.impact: Douglas was the lone bright spot in an underwhelming Miami passing attack, leading the team in receptions and receiving yards in the loss. The wideout will look to provide quarterback Malik Willis with a reliable pass-catching option moving forward, with a Week 2 contest against the San Francisco 49ers up next.

news.head: Caleb Douglas set to start in Week 1
news.body: Caleb Douglas is set to be a starter for the Dolphins in their Week 1 matchup against the Las Vegas Raiders.
news.impact: The Dolphins selected Douglas in the third round of this year's draft, but he had an impressive offseason for them and is set to be a starter for the team in their season opener. That's a great sign for his season outlook, as it means he will have ample opportunities to prove himself and break out from the very start of the season.

news.head: Caleb Douglas selected No. 75 by Miami Dolphins
news.body: The Miami Dolphins have selected WR Caleb Douglas with the No. 75 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft.
news.impact: Douglas heads to the Dolphins with the 75th overall pick after a productive career at Texas Tech. Douglas was a Second Team All-Big 12 selection last season after leading the Red Raiders in receiving yards (846). Douglas ran well at the combine (4.39 40-yard dash), but doesn't always showcase that speed to create separation vertically. He will have every opportunity to contribute immediately as the Dolphins have endured a major overhaul in the wide receiver room entering the 2026 season.

news.head: Tre Tucker catches two passes in Week 1
news.body: Tre Tucker caught two of his four targets for 27 yards in the Raiders' 27-13 win over the Miami Dolphins in Week 1.
news.impact: Tucker was one of six to catch at least one pass from Kirk Cousins in the season opener, averaging a team-high 13.5 yards per reception. The wideout remains one of many pass-catching options as part of a revamped Las Vegas offense, with a Week 2 contest against the Los Angeles Chargers up next.

news.head: Tre Tucker catches two passes in Week 18
news.body: Tre Tucker caught 2-of-6 targets for 30 yards in the Raiders 14-12 win over the Chiefs.
news.impact: Tucker led the team in targets, but was unable to do much with them Sunday. The 24-year-old will end the season with 696 yards and five touchdowns on 57 receptions.

news.head: Tre Tucker hauls in five passes Sunday
news.body: Tre Tucker caught 5-of-6 targets for 49 yards in the Raiders 34-10 loss against the Giants.
news.impact: Tucker was a safety blanket throughout the afternoon for Geno Smith. He'll be a WR4 in Week 18 against the Chiefs.

news.head: Tre Tucker catches four passes Sunday
news.body: Tre Tucker caught 4-of-5 targets for 43 yards in Sunday's 23-21 loss to the Houston Texans.
news.impact: Tucker was a solid contributor for the Raiders on Sunday. He caught four passes for 43 yards against the Texans, which wasn't enough to leave him with a good fantasy total in most league formats. He will likely continue to be the team's WR1 for the remainder of the season, though that's unlikely to lead to much success from a fantasy standpoint.

news.head: Xavier Worthy quiet in win Monday
news.body: Xavier Worthy caught 3-of-6 targets for 18 yards in Monday night's 31-10 win over the Denver Broncos.
news.impact: Worthy was Kansas City's most targeted player on Monday night, but he wasn't able to do much with his opportunities, finishing with just three catches for 18 yards against the Broncos. He isn't expected to be a relevant fantasy option for the foreseeable future.

news.head: Xavier Worthy (shoulder) active for Week 1
news.body: Xavier Worthy (shoulder) is active for Week 1 for the Kansas City Chiefs against the Denver Broncos.
news.impact: Worthy will suit up after being able to practice throughout the week for head coach Andy Reid, joining fellow wideout Rashee Rice (knee) in offering quarterback Patrick Mahomes a full complement of weapons against a strong Denver defense Monday night.

news.head: Xavier Worthy (shoulder) listed as full participant Thursday
news.body: Xavier Worthy (shoulder) was listed as a full participant at practice on Thursday.
news.impact: To no surprise, Worthy seems to be over his shoulder injury and was able to practice in full on Thursday. He should be a full go for Week 1 but doesn't project to be a strong fantasy option in a matchup against the Broncos.

news.head: Xavier Worthy (shoulder) returns to practice Monday
news.body: Xavier Worthy was back practicing at Chiefs training camp on Monday.
news.impact: Worthy missed time during practice last week. The Chiefs had their full wide receiver room on the field on Monday.

news.head: Dontayvion Wicks finds end zone in Week 1 win
news.body: Dontayvion Wicks hauled in two of his four targets for 73 yards and one touchdown in the Eagles’ 24-22 Week 1 win over the Washington Commanders.
news.impact: Wicks made the most of his modest target share in the season opener, averaging 36.5 yards per reception in the win. The wideout offers head coach Nick Sirianni another explosive pass-catching option moving forward, with a favorable Week 2 matchup against the Tennessee Titans up next.

news.head: Dontayvion Wicks on track to be Eagles WR2
news.body: Dontayvion Wicks is trending towards opening the season as the No. 2 wide receiver for the Eagles to open the season.
news.impact: Wicks continues to impress during training camp, while rookie Makai Lemon misses time with a hamstring injury. He was able to show flashes in Green Bay and could see more consistent opportunity with the Eagles. He'll remain a player to monitor for fantasy managers as well as the health of Lemon.

news.head: Dontayvion Wicks not at Eagles OTAs Wednesday
news.body: Dontayvion Wicks was absent Wednesday at Eagles OTAs.
news.impact: Wicks was acquired by the Eagles in a trade this offseason. He will figure to compete for an immediate role in the Eagles wide receiver room.

news.head: Dontayvion Wicks traded to Philadelphia Eagles
news.body: Dontayvion Wicks has been traded to the Philadelphia Eagles for a 2026 fifth round pick and a 2027 sixth. Wicks will sign a $12.5 million extension with the Eagles.
news.impact: $12.5 million is not nothing, and his addition is an interesting transaction given the AJ Brown trade rumors. It doesn’t preclude the Eagles from taking a receiver in the NFL Draft, but his contact seems to signal a decent amount of involvement in the Eagles upcoming plans.

news.head: Denzel Boston snags bomb touchdown in loss
news.body: Denzel Boston caught two of four targets for 59 yards and a touchdown in the Browns' 34-10 loss to the Jaguars on Sunday.
news.impact: Boston had the Browns' only touchdown, though sadly it was in garbage time. His four targets tied with Jerry Jeudy for second on the team, an encouraging sign for his future usage as he gets further acclimated to the NFL game.

news.head: Denzel Boston to practice with first-team offense
news.body: Browns coach Todd Monken said rookie WR Denzel Boston will move into first-team offense.
news.impact: Boston continues to show out early on in training camp. He is slated to compete for an immediate starting role.

news.head: Denzel Boston selected No. 39 by Cleveland Browns
news.body: The Cleveland Browns have selected WR Denzel Boston with the No. 39 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft.
news.impact: Boston becomes the second wide receiver taken by the Browns in the first two rounds of the 2026 Draft as they double up after selecting KC Concepcion in the first round Thursday. Boston is a much larger receiver (6-3, 212) out of Washington and led the Huskies in receiving yards last season. He did not run a 40-yard dash at the combine and doesn't display top speed to create separation. But, he does have excellent hands and he was very tough to bring down at the collegiate level. It's a little surprising that the Browns took another receiver with a need for offensive line help. But, Cleveland is looking for playmakers to improve the offense in 2026 and Boston should help with that as part of the receiver rotation.

news.head: Denzel Boston to visit Panthers Thursday
news.body: The Panthers are hosting Washington WR Denzel Boston for a top-30 visit on Thursday.
news.impact: Carolina holds the No. 19 pick as it looks to potentially add another wide receiver. Boston played for Jedd Fisch for his final two seasons in college, the same system that OROY Tetairoa McMillan played in under Fisch for two seasons at Arizona.

news.head: Blake Corum totals 54 yards in loss
news.body: Blake Corum ran 10 times for 54 yards in the Rams' 27-7 loss to the 49ers on Thursday.
news.impact: Corum was solid on the ground at 5.4 a carry, but that was about all he had going for him. Without a touchdown or receiving work to go along with his yardage, it was a disappointing fantasy performance. However, his usage is encouraging; the Rams at least trust him enough that they will split Kyren Williams' workload with Corum. It makes him a top-tier handcuff RB, and one that should be rostered in case anything happens to Kyren.

news.head: Blake Corum sees 14 touches in Week 18 win
news.body: Blake Corum rushed for 59 yards on 13 carries and caught his lone target for 10 yards in the Rams 37-20 win over the Cardinals.
news.impact: Corum and Kyren Williams continue to split time in the backfield for the Rams. With the Rams success this season in getting both running backs involved, it should be expected that the rotation continues throughout the team's playoff run.

news.head: Blake Corum (ankle) officially active for Week 18
news.body: Blake Corum (ankle) is officially active for Week 18.
news.impact: Corum exited Monday's game with an ankle injury and was considered questionable to play against Arizona. Corum will continue to work in a rotation with Kyren Williams in the final game of the regular season.

news.head: Blake Corum (ankle) listed questionable for Week 18
news.body: Blake Corum is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Cardinals.
news.impact: Corum had missed two straight practices to begin the week after leaving last Monday's game early. It would be a surprise if he plays on Sunday unless he is fully healthy.

news.head: Keenan Allen hauls in six receptions in Week 1 loss
news.body: Keenan Allen hauled in all of his team-high six targets for 32 yards in the Colts' 41-23 loss to the Baltimore Ravens in Week 1.
news.impact: Allen was unable to find much room despite leading the team in receptions, averaging 5.3 yards per reception in the Week 1 loss. The veteran wideout will look to offer head coach Shane Steichem more sizeable impact against a difficult Kansas City Chiefs defense in Week 2.

news.head: Keenan Allen will play in Week 1
news.body: Colts GM Chris Ballard said Keenan Allen will play in Indianapolis’ Week 1 game against the Ravens.
news.impact: Allen was arrested for DWI and DWI endangering a person on Sunday morning. He'll be in the WR4 range for fantasy managers heading into the season.

news.head: Keenan Allen facing two DUI charges after arrest early Sunday morning
news.body: Keenan Allen is facing two DUI charges after being arrested early Sunday morning.
news.impact: The veteran receiver was a badly needed addition to the Colts roster, and now he could find himself suspended for a game or two should the NFL find that action appropriate. It's also possible he will only face fines. Still, it's worth monitoring the vet's situation, as he was an interesting late-round sleeper in drafts.

news.head: Keenan Allen to begin practicing Thursday
news.body: Keenan Allen will begin practicing with the Colts on Thursday.
news.impact: Allen agreed to a contract with the Colts earlier this week. He'll add depth to a depleted Colts wide receiver room.

news.head: Kaelon Black impresses in win over Rams
news.body: Kaelon Black ran 14 times for 65 yards and caught his only target for five yards in the 49ers' 27-7 win over the Rams on Thursday.
news.impact: Black was in a full-on committee with Christian McCaffrey, something few, if any, saw coming. Both were tied at 15 touches apiece, but McCaffrey led in total opportunities thanks to seeing more targets. Black won't have games like this all the time, but he's showing himself to be a valuable handcuff that CMC managers will need to snag when they can.

news.head: Kaelon Black (adductor) in uniform at practice Tuesday
news.body: Kaelon Black is in uniform at practice on Tuesday for the first time since the first week of camp.
news.impact: It is a positive sign for the Black. The rookie will have a chance to be good to go for the regular season opener.

news.head: Kaelon Black (adductor) not practicing Monday
news.body: Kaelon Black missed practice on Monday with an adductor injury.
news.impact: With Jordan James sidelined with a fractured rib, Black was seeing more opportunity to compete for the RB2 role in the 49ers backfield. He is day-to-day for now.

news.head: Kaelon Black selected No. 90 by San Francisco 49ers
news.body: The San Francisco 49ers have selected RB Kaelon Black with the No. 90 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft.
news.impact: Black becomes the latest running back addition in the draft by the 49ers. He showcased his upside in the run by Indiana to winning the national championship this past year. He is a shorter running back who is strong with good vision. He will compete for a depth role in the 49ers backfield.

news.head: Adonai Mitchell goes for 60 yards in Week 1
news.body: Adonai Mitchell caught all three of his targets for 60 yards in a 23-10 win over the Titans in Week 1.
news.impact: Mitchell finished second on the Jets in receiving yards, operating as the team's deep threat. He did most of his damage on a 40-yard pass from Geno Smith. While Mitchell will remain behind Garrett Wilson in the target pecking order, he has some boom/bust potential in a Jets offense that looked much improved from last year. Mitchell settles in as a flex option in Week 2 against Green Bay.

news.head: Adonai Mitchell held without a catch in Week 18
news.body: Adonai Mitchell did not record a reception on three targets in the Jets 35-8 loss to the Bills.
news.impact: Mitchell appeared in seven games with the Jets since being acquired in the trade that sent Sauce Gardner to the Colts. This was the first time the 23-year-old was held without a reception since the trade. Mitchell should factor into the Jets' offensive plans for 2026 and should benefit from the return of Garrett Wilson.

news.head: Adonai Mitchell hauls in three passes in Week 17
news.body: Adonai Mitchell caught 3-of-9 targets for 22 yards in the Jets 42-10 loss to the Patriots.
news.impact: Mitchell led the team in targets, seeing four more than the next option in the passing game. The 23-year-old has registered nine or more targets in three of his last six games as he clearly has worked himself into a prominent role in the Jets' offense. The Jets will take on Buffalo in Week 18.

news.head: Adonai Mitchell catches three passes in Week 16 loss to Patriots
news.body: Adonai Mitchell hauled in three of his six targets for 43 yards in the Jets' 29-6 Week 16 loss to the Saints.
news.impact: Mitchell has struggled despite increased involvement in the New York offense, finishing with less than 60 receiving yards despite six or more targets in five of his last six games. The wideout remains a risky pass-catching option in all formats ahead of a Week 17 contest against the New England Patriots.

news.head: Tyler Allgeier leads Arizona rushing attack in Week 1
news.body: Tyler Allgeier gained 61 yards on 17 carries and nine yards on two receptions in Sunday's 26-14 win over the Chargers.
news.impact: Allgeier shouldered the majority of the backfield load for the Cardinals on Sunday, getting six more carries than Jeremiyah Love. Allgeier was not especially impressive, averaging just 3.6 yards per carry with a long of 11. Allgeier will remain involved, but the share of the carries should tilt more toward Love as the rookie gets further removed from the ankle sprain he sustained a month ago.

news.head: Tyler Allgeier listed as starter on Cardinals depth chart
news.body: Tyler Allgeier was listed as the starting running back on the Cardinals' Week 1 depth chart.
news.impact: Allgeier was listed as the starter ahead of rookie Jeremiyah Love after a training camp battle. Love has also been making his way back from an ankle sprain, which could be why Allgeier sees more carries in the early part of the season. If he does indeed get the start on Sunday, Allgeier could be an RB3 or deeper flex option in fantasy.

news.head: Tyler Allgeier signs two-year deal with Cardinals
news.body: The Cardinals agreed to terms on a two-year, $12.25 million deal with Tyler Allgeier.
news.impact: Allgeier joins James Conner and Trey Benson in the backfield for Arizona. He had potential other landing spots where he could have had more of a feature role if Conner remains in Arizona. This will remain a backfield to monitor the rest of the offseason.

news.head: Tyler Allgeier linked to Seahawks
news.body: The Seahawks are expected to have interest in free agent RB Tyler Allgeier.
news.impact: Allgeier is set to enter free agency next week. He should draw some interest from several teams. The Seahawks are expected to have interest as they're expected to be out of the market to re-sign Kenneth Walker.

news.head: Malik Washington catches three passes in Week 1 loss
news.body: Malik Washington caught three of his eight targets for 53 yards in the Dolphins' 27-13 loss to the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 1.
news.impact: Washington made a modest impact despite leading the team in targets, finishing third on the team in receptions in the loss. The wideout remains another high-risk pass-catching option as part of a Miami offense searching to establish their identity as the season continues, with a Week 2 contest against the San Francisco 49ers up next.

news.head: Malik Washington scores touchdown in loss
news.body: Malik Washington caught three of four targets for six yards and a touchdown while also running twice for 22 yards in the Dolphins’ 38-10 loss to New England on Sunday.
news.impact: Washington failed to get much going as the de facto top target in the Miami offense. He’s did at least score a touchdown, but six yards on three receptions leaves a lot to be desired. He’s a depth option in deep dynasty leagues at best at this point, having failed to take advantage of his opportunities in 2025.

news.head: Malik Washington quiet despite Waddle injury
news.body: Malik Washington was limited to just one reception for four yards on three targets during Sunday's win over the Buccaneers. The wide receiver also added a single carry for one yard but failed to see increased involvement in the passing attack even as Jaylen Waddle missed time with a rib injury.
news.impact: Washington's most notable contribution came on special teams, where he delivered a 47-yard kick return late in the third quarter. He will look to build better chemistry with quarterback Quinn Ewers in the Week 18 regular-season finale against the Patriots.

news.head: Malik Washington finds end zone Sunday
news.body: Malik Washington caught one pass for 23 yards and rushed the ball one time for nine yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 45-21 loss to the Cincinnati Bengals.
news.impact: Washington saw just a couple of touches on Sunday, but he was able to make the most out of them and still finished the 32 total yards and a touchdown. Fantasy managers shouldn't have high expectations for him for the remainder of the season, however.

news.head: T.J. Hockenson hauls in touchdown Sunday
news.body: T.J. Hockenson caught 4-of-5 targets for 36 yards in the Vikings 39-22 win over the Packers.
news.impact: Hockenson caught one of the three touchdowns thrown by Carson Wentz. He could be on the TE1 radar in a favorable matchup next week against the Bears.

news.head: T.J. Hockenson restructures contract with Vikings
news.body: The Vikings restructured the contract of TE T.J. Hockenson.
news.impact: Hockenson is coming off one of the worst seasons of his career. He'll now be two years removed from a knee injury he suffered in 2024. The move saves $5 million against the cap for the Vikings.

news.head: T.J. Hockenson (shoulder) ruled out for Week 18
news.body: T.J. Hockenson has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Packers.
news.impact: The season is officially over for Hockenson. He had a down year this season when he was healthy compared to his standards. It is unclear what his future looks like in Minnesota.

news.head: T.J. Hockenson (shoulder) misses practice Thursday
news.body: T.J. Hockenson did not practice on Thursday.
news.impact: Hockenson appears likely to remain sidelined in Sunday's season finale.

news.head: Rachaad White sees nine touches in Week 1
news.body: Rachaad White rushed seven times for 22 yards while also catching both of his targets for five yards in the Commanders’ 24-22 Week 1 loss to the Philadelphia Eagles.
news.impact: White made the most of modest touches in the season-opening contest, finishing second to Jacory Croskey-Merritt in touches in the loss. The running back offers more value in PPR formats as the No. 2 backfield option for the Commanders, with a Week 2 contest against the Dallas Cowboys up next.

news.head: Rachaad White (hamstring) off injury report for Sunday
news.body: Rachaad White (hamstring) is off of the injury report for Sunday's game against the Philadelphia Eagles.
news.impact: The veteran running back is fully over his hamstring injury at this point and is set to be a full go for Washington's season opener on Sunday. He will be primed for more work if Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) is limited or sidelined for the team's matchup against the Eagles.

news.head: Rachaad White (hamstring) set to practice Wednesday
news.body: Rachaad White (hamstring) is set to take part in Washington's practice on Wednesday.
news.impact: White's status for Week 1 is still unclear right now thanks to a hamstring injury that he's still dealing with. He is taking part in Wednesday's practice, however, which is a step in the right direction for him. Fantasy managers should pay attention to updates about his health throughout the week, as Jacory Croskey-Merritt will be a significantly better fantasy option if the veteran is sidelined this week.

news.head: Rachaad White (hamstring) won't play Saturday
news.body: Rachaad White (hamstring) won't play in Saturday's preseason game against the Detroit Lions.
news.impact: White is not going to be available to play in Saturday's preseason game. He is still dealing with a minor hamstring injury, but HC Dan Quinn told reporters that he is "certainly close" to a return to the field. Jacory Croskey-Merritt stands to benefit if this injury causes the veteran to miss more time beyond this game.

news.head: Makai Lemon quiet in Week 1
news.body: Makai Lemon caught three of his four targets for a loss of five yards on the Eagles’ 24-22 win over the Washington Commanders in Week 1.
news.impact: Lemon struggled to find any success in the season opener, as the pass-catcher was bottled up by the Commanders defense in the win. The wideout will look for more impactful output in a favorable Week 2 matchup against the Tennessee Titans.

news.head: Makai Lemon (hamstring) practicing in full on Monday
news.body: Makai Lemon (hamstring) is back to practicing fully for the first time in weeks. He returned to practice in a limited fashion last week, and is now practicing in full.
news.impact: This is huge for Lemon’s development and integration into the offense. The more reps he gets, especially as a rookie, the better. He’s looking like a potential draft steal if he can continue to stay healthy and improve his game.

news.head: Makai Lemon (hamstring) limited at practice Thursday
news.body: Makai Lemon (hamstring) was limited at Philadelphia's practice on Thursday.
news.impact: The rookie was able to make his return to practice on Thursday. He was sidelined for a little while after suffering a hamstring injury, but it seems that he is progressing well with his recovery, as the team is now letting him practice in a limited capacity. At this rate he will be ready to play in time for the team's season opener, barring any setbacks with his recovery.

news.head: Makai Lemon (hamstring) still not practicing Wednesday
news.body: Makai Lemon remained absent from practice on Wednesday.
news.impact: Lemon has been sidelined for nearly two weeks with the hamstring issue. It remains unclear when he will return to practice.

news.head: Rashid Shaheed quiet in win Wednesday
news.body: Rashid Shaheed caught 1-of-3 targets for just four yards in Wednesday's 13-10 win over the New England Patriots.
news.impact: The speedy wideout wasn't able to do much on Wednesday, catching just one pass for four yards in the team's win over New England. The injury to starter Sam Darnold (hip) may have played a large role in his lack of production, however, so this isn't a good game to look at in order to discern his true involvement in this offense.

news.head: Rashid Shaheed agrees to three-year deal with Seattle
news.body: Rashid Shaheed has agreed to return to the Seahawks on a three-year, $51 million deal.
news.impact: Shaheed wasn’t what fantasy players hoped he would be in Seattle, managing only 15 receptions for 188 yards after being traded to Seattle despite his deep threat skillset and QB Sam Darnold’s deep throwing ability. However, Shaheed proved his worth in the return game, returning both a punt and kickoff for a touchdown for Seattle. Hopefully in 2026 he sees more work in the receiving game, as his price tag would imply. This likely means Tory Horton’s breakout is at best delayed, if not completely out of the cards with Cooper Kupp also still on the roster with Shaheed and Jaxon Smith-Njigba.

news.head: Rashid Shaheed testing free agency
news.body: WR Rashid Shaheed is expected to test free agency after failing to agree on an extension with the Seahawks.
news.impact: Shaheed’s value to the Seahawks largely came from his returning ability. If he signs elsewhere, he could become fantasy-relevant again.

news.head: Rashid Shaheed hopes to return to Seahawks
news.body: Rashid Shaheed, who ended up in Seattle from New Orleans at the trade deadline, hopes to return to the Pacific Northwest for a Super Bowl title defense in 2026.
news.impact: Shaheed was a game-changer for the Seahawks and their Super Bowl title run upon his arrival from New Orleans. Although he only caught 15 passes for 188 yards in nine regular season games with the Seahawks, he averaged 29.9 yards per kickoff return and 16.2 yards per punt return with two return touchdowns. He added three catches for 78 yards in three postseason games but kicked off the Seahawks' postseason run with a 95-yard kickoff return for a score on the first play in Seattle's Divisional Round win over the 49ers. Shaheed is a deep threat and a dynamic special teams player who should be on Seattle's list to attempt to work out a deal this offseason.

news.head: Pat Freiermuth finds the end zone in Week 1 win
news.body: Pat Freiermuth caught all five of his targets for 46 yards and a touchdown in a 20-13 win over the Falcons in Week 1.
news.impact: Freiermuth kicked off the season with a promising outing in the win over Atlanta. He hauled in Aaron Rodgers' lone touchdown pass on a six-yard catch in the second quarter while tying for second on the team in receptions. Freiermuth will settle in as a TE2 in fantasy heading into a Week 2 matchup against the Patriots.

news.head: Pat Freiermuth goes for 51 yards in Week 18
news.body: Pat Freiermuth caught three of his five targets for 51 yards in a 26-24 win over the Ravens in Week 18.
news.impact: Freiermuth finished third on the Steelers in receiving in the win. The veteran tight end wraps the regular season with 41 catches for 486 yards and four touchdowns while appearing in all 17 of the Steelers' games. He will now prepare to take on the Texans at home in the Wild-Card round of the playoffs.

news.head: Pat Freiermuth hauls in three passes in Week 17
news.body: Pat Freiermuth caught 3-of-5 targets for 63 yards in the Steelers 13-6 loss to the Browns.
news.impact: Freiermuth saw an increase in targets after Darnell Washington exited the game with a broken arm. With Washington out next week, Freiermuth and Jonnu Smith should see the bulk of the snaps at tight end against the Ravens in a matchup with the Ravens to decide the AFC North.

news.head: Pat Freiermuth catches four passes Sunday
news.body: Pat Freiermuth caught 4-of-4 targets for 20 yards in the Steelers 29-24 win over the Lions.
news.impact: Freiermuth finished the day tied for second on the team in receptions. He remains off the fantasy radar.

news.head: Jalen Nailor catches three passes in Week 1
news.body: Jalen Nailor caught three of his five targets for 27 yards in the Raiders' 27-13 win over the Miami Dolphins in Week 1.
news.impact: Nailor was one of many that saw involvement in the Las Vegas passing offense, finishing as one of six to catch at least one pass in the win. The wideout will look to offer more impactful potential in a revamped Las Vegas offense as the season moves forward, with a Week 2 contest against the Los Angeles Chargers up next.

news.head: Jalen Nailor signs three-year deal with Raiders
news.body: The Raiders agreed to terms with WR Jalen Nailor on a three-year, $35 million contract.
news.impact: Nailor will receive $23 million in guaranteed money. He is looking to step into a bigger role after playing in a limited role in Minnesota. He will be a late-round flier in drafts for now.

news.head: Jalen Nailor expected to have 'robust market' in free agency
news.body: WR Jalen Nailor is expected to have a "robust market" in free agency.
news.impact: Nailor posted a 26/395/4 receiving line last season in Minnesota. His projected market value is $4.7M per year, and he's in line for a multi-year deal. He'll likely seek a WR3 role with another team.

news.head: Jalen Nailor catches three passes in Week 18
news.body: Jalen Nailor caught all three of his targets for 49 yards in Minnesota's 16-3 victory over Green Bay on Sunday.
news.impact: Nailor finished second on the team in receiving on Sunday and his three catches were his first since catching three passes at Dallas on December 14. Despite having gone catch-less in five games this season, Nailor finished with career-highs in receptions (29) and receiving yards (444) in his fourth season in Minnesota.

news.head: Kayshon Boutte makes only catch in Texans debut
news.body: Kayshon Boutte caught 1-of-2 targets for 21 yards in Sunday's 36-31 loss to the Bills.
news.impact: Boutte was acquired from New England late in the preseason to shore up the Texans' wide receiver corps. His big-play potential is known from the last couple of years with the Patriots, but his targets were predictably limited in an offense that is still relatively new to him. Boutte is a wait-and-see bench stash in standard fantasy leagues.

news.head: Kayshon Boutte will play in Week 1
news.body: Texans head coach DeMeco Ryans said Kayshon Boutte will play in Week 1 against the Bills.
news.impact: Boutte was acquired in a trade with the Patriots back on August 24. Ryans said he has been “picking up the playbook really well.” He'll be a deep threat on the outside for CJ Stroud.

news.head: Kayshon Boutte traded to Texans
news.body: The Patriots are sending WR Kayshon Boutte to the Texans in exchange for safety Jaylen Reed and a 2028 seventh-round pick.
news.impact: Boutte has had his name in trade rumors for most of the offseason following the Patriots offseason additions of AJ Brown and Romeo Doubs. Boutte will get a fresh start in a wide open wide receiver room with Houston. He should compete for a role as a field stretcher for the Texans.

news.head: Kayshon Boutte significantly involved in Tuesday's practice
news.body: Kayshon Boutte was significantly involved in Tuesday's practice.
news.impact: Boutte reported to minicamp despite his name being in the middle of trade rumors. It will continue to be something to monitor heading into training camp.

news.head: Woody Marks gets 10 touches in Week 1
news.body: Woody Marks rushed for 42 yards on nine carries and caught his only target for a two-yard loss in Sunday's 36-31 loss to the Bills.
news.impact: Marks was certainly involved in the offense behind new workhorse back David Montgomery on Sunday. Marks averaged close to 5.0 yards per carry on his nine attempts. He'll remain a useful handcuff to Montgomery for now.

news.head: Woody Marks: Texans HC DeMeco Ryans seeing year two jump
news.body: Texans coach Demeco Ryans said he is seeing a “year two jump” from Woody Marks.
news.impact: Ryans noted specifically that Marks is looking faster and making better decisions compared to his rookie season. The Texans traded for David Montgomery who is expected to lead the backfield, but Marks should play a role behind him.

news.head: Woody Marks (shoulder) questionable to return Sunday
news.body: Woody Marks is questionable to return to Sunday's Divisional Round game on Sunday against the Patriots.
news.impact: The Texans offense is dropping like flies. Nico Collins was ruled out before Sunday's game with Dalton Schultz ruled out during the game. Nick Chubb will be among the players to see more run in the backfield for Houston.

news.head: Woody Marks sees 10 carries in Week 18
news.body: Woody Marks ran for 48 yards on 10 carries in the Texans 38-30 win over the Colts.
news.impact: Marks was pulled with the starters at halftime. He figures to lead the backfield heading into the second half.

news.head: Pat Bryant leads team in receiving Monday
news.body: Pat Bryant caught 4-of-6 targets for 42 yards in Monday night's 31-10 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs.
news.impact: Bryant was one of the few Broncos who had a respectable showing on Monday night. He looked great at the start of the game but tapered off as it went on and as Denver continued to fall further and further behind on the scoreboard. He was the best out of Denver's receivers in this bad matchup, however, so the breakout potential seems to be there for the second-year wideout this season.

news.head: Pat Bryant (concussion) off injury report Sunday
news.body: Pat Bryant is off the injury report for Sunday's AFC Championship game against the Patriots.
news.impact: Bryant closed the week with two straight full practices. He'll be a full-go heading into Sunday.

news.head: Pat Bryant (concussion) limited Wednesday
news.body: Broncos WR Pat Bryant was a limited participant on Wednesday ahead of the AFC Championship.
news.impact: Bryant caught fire early in last week’s Divisional Round, hauling in three receptions in the opening quarter before suffering a concussion. Denver hopes the rookie can clear protocol ahead of Sunday.

news.head: Pat Bryant hauls in four passes Sunday
news.body: Pat Bryant hauled in 4-of-5 targets for 31 yards in Sunday's 19-3 win over the Los Angeles Chargers.
news.impact: Bryant was uncertain to play coming into the week due to a concussion that he was dealing with, but he was able to play through it and ended up racking up 31 total yards against the Chargers. He will continue to play a supporting role for Denver's offense as they head into the postseason.

news.head: Tre' Harris finishes with three receptions in Week 1
news.body: Tre' Harris caught 3-of-6 targets for 20 yards in Sunday's 26-14 loss to the Cardinals.
news.impact: Harris was at least significantly involved in the passing game Sunday, as the second-year wideout tied a career high in targets set in Week 18 of last season. Harris did not do much with those targets, however, totaling only 20 yards with a long of 11. The second-round pick from 2025 is a fringe redraft option at present.

news.head: Tre Harris inefficient in loss Sunday
news.body: Tre Harris caught 2-of-6 targets for 28 yards in Sunday's 19-3 loss to the Denver Broncos.
news.impact: Harris saw plenty of opportunities on Sunday with six targets, but he wasn't able to take advantage of them and ended up with just two catches for 28 yards. He has had a disappointing rookie campaign and will likely remain a non-factor for the Chargers heading into the postseason.

news.head: Tre Harris quiet in loss to Houston
news.body: Tre Harris caught his only target for eight yards in the Chargers' 20-16 loss to the Houston Texans.
news.impact: After back-to-back weeks of at least 49 receiving yards, Harris went back to being the WR4 of the offense and came up with a single reception. In fact, of all the Chargers receivers, only Quentin Johnston had more than a single catch. Harris is off the board for fantasy for now, but is a worthwhile stash in dynasty.

news.head: Tre Harris totals 54 yards Sunday
news.body: Tre Harris caught 4-of-5 targets for 54 yards in the Chargers 34-17 win over the Cowboys.
news.impact: Harris has continued to show flashes throughout his rookie season. He'll be a player to monitor in drafts heading into next year.

news.head: Cooper Kupp totals 35 yards in win Wednesday
news.body: Cooper Kupp caught 2-of-3 targets for 35 yards in Wednesday night's 13-10 win over the New England Patriots.
news.impact: Kupp didn't end up with a strong statline in the box score on Wednesday, but he was an important player for the Seahawks in this matchup. He made multiple key plays for them and had a touchdown that got called back due to penalty. He isn't likely to be fantasy relevant moving forward, however, especially if QB Sam Darnold (hip) misses time.

news.head: Cooper Kupp quiet until final drive Saturday
news.body: Cooper Kupp caught two passes for 29 yards during the Seahawks' 13-3 victory over the 49ers on Saturday night to clinch the NFC West and the top seed in the NFC.
news.impact: Kupp was held without a catch until picking up two big catches for the Seahawks on their final drive of the game. Both of Kupp's catches converted third downs and helped Seattle kill more than eight minutes off the clock to essentially seal the win. While Kupp doesn't put up the numbers he used to, his veteran presence has helped a young Seahawks' receiving corps this season. He did finish second on the team in receiving yards with 593 on 47 receptions.

news.head: Cooper Kupp quiet Sunday
news.body: Cooper Kupp caught 1-of-3 passes for six yards in the Seahawks 27-10 win over the Panthers.
news.impact: Kupp had one drop that nearly led to an interception. He remains off the fantasy radar heading into Week 18 against the 49ers.

news.head: Cooper Kupp converts key two-point try in win
news.body: Facing his former team on Thursday night, Cooper Kupp caught three of his four targets for 39 yards in Seattle's narrow 38-37 overtime victory. Although he lost a fumble concluding a 17-yard reception in the first half, he contributed to the win by securing the first of the Seahawks' three successful two-point conversions.
news.impact: Kupp continues to work as the distant second option behind Jaxon Smith-Njigba, as no other Seahawks wide receiver recorded a catch in the contest. While teammate Rashid Shaheed found the end zone, his production came via a punt return and a rushing attempt rather than through the air. Kupp will look to clean up the ball security issues when he faces the Panthers in Week 17.

news.head: AJ Barner catches two passes Wednesday
news.body: AJ Barner caught two passes for 13 yards in Wednesday's 13-10 win over the New England Patriots.
news.impact: The Seahawks were able to pick up a win over the Patriots on Wednesday, but they didn't need to get Barner very involved in order to do so. He finished the game with just two catches for 13 yards, and there's not much reason to believe that he will bounce back and become a quality week-to-week option anytime soon.

news.head: AJ Barner (oblique) off injury report Wednesday
news.body: AJ Barner is off the injury report for Wednesday’s game against the Patriots.
news.impact: Barner practiced all week in full. He'll be a TE2 for fantasy managers going into the season.

news.head: AJ Barner (oblique) logs full practice Monday
news.body: AJ Barner was a full participant in practice on Monday.
news.impact: Barner remains on track to be a full-go for Wednesday’s season opener against the Patriots.

news.head: AJ Barner (oblique) practices in full Sunday
news.body: AJ Barner was a full participant in practice on Sunday.
news.impact: Barner missed some time early in the offseason program, but he avoided the PUP list during training camp. He heads into the season as a TE2 for fantasy managers.

news.head: Chris Rodriguez Jr. quiet in win over Browns
news.body: Chris Rodriguez Jr. ran six times for 23 yards in the Jaguars' 34-10 Week 1 win over the Browns.
news.impact: Rodriguez wasn't involved much in the blowout win, carrying the ball only six times. It's possible the team wanted to see more of Tuten today than CRod, but that's purely speculation. As for now, it's hard to start Rodriguez until we know more about what his workload could look like on a weekly basis.

news.head: Chris Rodriguez Jr. (foot) off injury report for Week 1
news.body: Chris Rodriguez Jr. (foot) is off of Jacksonville's injury report ahead of the season opener against the Cleveland Browns.
news.impact: Rodriguez is set to be a full go in Week 1 after battling with a foot injury throughout the preseason. He is likely to play a substantial role in Jacksonville's backfield this season, although the exact distribution of work will remain obscure until after the first game or two, which makes him hard to trust as a fantasy option in the season opener.

news.head: Chris Rodriguez Jr. (foot) expects to be back for Week 1
news.body: Chris Rodriguez Jr. told reporters he plans to be back for Week 1.
news.impact: Rodriguez is currently participating in individual drills at training camp after not being on the field earlier in the offseason program. He is continuing to be managed early in camp as he works his way back to full health.

news.head: Chris Rodriguez Jr. (foot) back at practice Wednesday
news.body: Chris Rodriguez Jr. was back on the field in practice to begin training camp.
news.impact: Rodriguez missed time earlier in the Jaguars offseason program with a foot injury. He will be competing for an immediate role alongside Bhayshul Tuten.

news.head: Malachi Fields catches two passes Sunday
news.body: Malachi Fields caught 2-of-4 targets for 25 yards in Sunday night's 28-20 win over the Dallas Cowboys.
news.impact: The rookie saw the field a decent amount on Sunday night. He wasn't able to put up big numbers from a fantasy perspective, however, totaling just 25 yards on two catches against the Cowboys. His debut was a solid performance overall but fantasy managers shouldn't have high hopes for him for the foreseeable future.

news.head: Malachi Fields works with trainer on side field Wednesday
news.body: Malachi Fields went to a side field and worked with a trainer early in Wednesday's practice.
news.impact: Fields had a limited workload on Tuesday. The rookie remains day-to-day.

news.head: Malachi Fields selected No. 74 by New York Giants
news.body: The New York Giants have selected WR Malachi Fields with the No. 74 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft.
news.impact: Fields will add some size to the Giants wide receiver room standing in at 6'5. He'll have the chance to compete for an immediate role, while also adding depth in the Giants wide receiver room.

news.head: Mike Gesicki explodes to open season
news.body: Mike Gesicki caught 5-of-7 targets for 78 yards with a touchdown in the Bengals 33-27 win over the Buccaneers.
news.impact: While Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins were fairly quiet on Sunday, it was Gesicki who led the team in receiving. Despite his big Week 1 performance, he still isn't a reliable weekly start yet.

news.head: Mike Gesicki catches two passes in loss
news.body: Mike Gesicki caught both of his targets for 13 yards in the Bengals' 20-18 loss to the Browns on Sunday.
news.impact: Gesicki failed to get much going in this game with the passing attack of Ja'Marr Chase, Tee Higgins, and Chase Brown taking most of the work. Between the trio of Gesicki, Drew Sample, and Noah Fant, there's just not enough to go around.

news.head: Mike Gesicki totals 47 yards Sunday
news.body: Mike Gesicki caught 2-of-2 targets for 47 yards in the Bengals 37-14 win over the Cardinals.
news.impact: Gesicki had a big catch of 32 yards. He will continue to split snaps with Noah Fant in Week 18 against the Browns.

news.head: Mike Gesicki hauls in touchdown Sunday
news.body: Mike Gesicki hauled in 3-of-4 targets for 35 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 45-21 win over the Miami Dolphins.
news.impact: Gesicki had a pretty solid game against his former team on Sunday. He racked up 35 yards and a touchdown against the Dolphins, and Cincinnati was able to secure a 24-point win over them to put the cherry on top. He won't be fantasy relevant moving forward, however.

news.head: Cade Otton quiet Sunday
news.body: Cade Otton caught 3-for-5 targets for 26 yards in the Buccaneers 33-27 loss against the Bengals on Sunday.
news.impact: Otton was third on the team in targets, but he was unable to turn it into much production. He remains a TE2 for fantasy managers.

news.head: Cade Otton re-signs with Bucs
news.body: The Bucs are re-signing TE Cade Otton.
news.impact: Otton was set to hit free agency, but he will be remaining with Tampa Bay and Baker Mayfield as a safety blanket. He should remain on the TE1/TE2 radar for fantasy managers.

news.head: Cade Otton dominates in Week 18
news.body: Cade Otton caught 7-of-9 targets for 94 yards and a touchdown in the Bucs 16-7 win over the Panthers.
news.impact: Hauling in a touchdown on the opening drive of the game, Otton dominated in the passing game for Tampa Bay. He was the only player to surpass even 35 receiving yards on the day for the Bucs. He is set to enter free agency this offseason.

news.head: Cade Otton hauls in four catches in loss
news.body: Cade Otton caught all four of his targets for 33 yards during Sunday's 20-17 loss to the Dolphins. While this marked his highest yardage output since Week 10, the tight end has yet to find the end zone this season and continues to see limited volume with the receiving corps at full health.
news.impact: Otton will look to improve upon his numbers when the Buccaneers face the Panthers in the Week 18 regular-season finale.

news.head: Keaton Mitchell gets sparse action in Week 1
news.body: Keaton Mitchell gained nine yards on four carries in Sunday's 26-14 loss to the Cardinals.
news.impact: After Sunday's season opener, Mitchell is clearly little more than a handcuff for Chargers lead back Omarion Hamption. Still, it is worth noting that Mitchell had been dealing with a hamstring issue as recently as last week. The fourth-year back has shown plenty of big-play ability over the last three seasons in Baltimore, but it would likely require an injury to Hampton for Mitchell to offer much fantasy value.

news.head: Keaton Mitchell (hamstring) off injury report for Sunday
news.body: Keaton Mitchell (hamstring) is off of the injury report for Sunday's game against the Arizona Cardinals.
news.impact: Mitchell has been dealing with a nagging hamstring injury for a while, but it appears he is finally over it, as he has received full clearance to suit up and play for the Chargers in their season opener. He will remain relegated to a depth role behind Omarion Hampton for the foreseeable future, however.

news.head: Keaton Mitchell (hamstring) limited participant Wednesday
news.body: Keaton Mitchell (hamstring) was a limited participant at practice on Wednesday.
news.impact: Mitchell was sidelined for a while as he dealt with a hamstring injury, but he was able to practice in a limited fashion on Wednesday. He will have a chance to play in Week 1, but even if he's active, he's not expected to play more than a depth role for the Chargers in their matchup against the Cardinals.

news.head: Keaton Mitchell returns to practice Monday
news.body: Keaton Mitchell was back at Chargers practice on Monday.
news.impact: Mitchell had missed the last six practices. His return on Monday is a good sign for his status heading into Sunday's season opener.

news.head: Caleb Williams posts four touchdowns in Week 1 win over Panthers
news.body: Caleb Williams completed 21-of-29 pass attempts for 269 yards and two touchdowns while also rushing 10 times for 65 yards and two touchdowns in a 59-37 Week 1 win over the Carolina Panthers.
news.impact: Williams was electric behind center to begin the season for head coach Ben Johnson, recording multiple touchdowns through the air and on the ground in the win. The dual-threat quarterback will look to offer fantasy manager a dynamic option in a favorable Week 2 contest against the Minnesota Vikings.

news.head: Caleb Williams throws two TD passes in Week 18
news.body: Caleb Williams completed 20-of-33 passes for 212 yards and two scores in Chicago's 19-16 loss to Detroit on Sunday. He was picked off once.
news.impact: Williams had touchdown passes to Colston Loveland and Jahdae Walker in the three-point loss. Williams closes out his sophomore season with 3,942 passing yards and 27 touchdowns to just seven interceptions as he leads the NFC North Champions into Wild Card Weekend against the Packers.

news.head: Caleb Williams surpasses 300 yards in Week 17 loss to 49ers
news.body: Caleb Williams completed 25-of-42 pass attempts for 330 yards and two touchdowns while also rushing five times for 18 yards in the Bears' 42-38 Week 17 loss to the 49ers.
news.impact: Williams continues a productive stretch behind center, throwing two or more touchdowns in five of his last six games. The dynamic signal-caller remains a versatile dual-threat option ahead of a Week 18 matchup against the Detroit Lions.

news.head: Caleb Williams tosses two touchdowns in Week 16 win over Packers
news.body: Caleb Williams completed 19-of-34 pass attempts for 250 yards and two touchdowns while also rushing three times for 30 yards in the Bears' 22-16 Week 16 win over the Packers.
news.impact: Williams turned around an otherwise pedestrian performance with two touchdown passes late in the fourth quarter and in overtime in a comeback victory. The quarterback faces an injury-ravaged San Francisco 49ers defense in Week 17.

news.head: Patrick Mahomes II scores three touchdowns in return game Monday
news.body: Patrick Mahomes II completed 15-of-27 passing attempts for 184 yards, two touchdowns, and one interception while adding 23 yards and a touchdown on the ground in Monday night's 31-10 win over the Denver Broncos.
news.impact: Monday night marked Mahomes' first game back after suffering a serious knee injury that ended his 2025 season prematurely. He looked good in his first game back, totaling over 200 yards and scoring three touchdowns on the night, including one impressive rushing touchdown from over ten yards out. He and Kansas City's offense as a whole are looking promising right now and may be primed for a big season if they can stay healthy this year.

news.head: Patrick Mahomes II (knee) active for Week 1
news.body: Patrick Mahomes II (knee) is active for Week 1 for the Kansas City Chiefs against the Denver Broncos.
news.impact: Mahomes II cleared through every obstacle in his way in recovering from a late-season knee injury in 2025-26, as the dynamic signal-caller looks to lead a revamped Kansas City offense back to the postseason beginning with the Week 1 divisional matchup against a disruptive Denver defense Monday night.

news.head: Patrick Mahomes II (knee) practices in full Thursday
news.body: Patrick Mahomes II (knee) practiced in a full capacity on Thursday.
news.impact: Mahomes was able to take part in Kansas City's first practice of the week on Thursday and wasn't limited in any way. It seems like the team is planning on him starting on Monday night, barring any unforeseen setbacks. His presence would be great news for the fantasy value of players like Rashee Rice and Travis Kelce in a matchup against a tough Denver defense.

news.head: Patrick Mahomes II (knee) to start Week 1 barring setback
news.body: Chiefs coach Andy Reid said Patrick Mahomes is set to start on Monday night barring a setback.
news.impact: Mahomes has officially worked his way back from a torn ACL and LCL suffered in Week 15 last year. He has said he may not run as much coming off the injury, at least early in the season.

news.head: Jordan Love throws for 387 yards Sunday
news.body: Jordan Love completed 21-of-42 passes for 387 yards with two touchdowns and one interception in the Packers 39-22 loss against the Vikings.
news.impact: Love tossed both touchdowns to Christian Watson as those two connected all afternoon. He did lose a fumble as the struggles began in the second half against the Vikings defense. He will face the Jets next week.

news.head: Jordan Love, Packers starters to see some snaps Friday
news.body: Jordan Love and the Packers starters will see some snaps again in Friday's preseason game against the Broncos.
news.impact: They are expected to play at least one drive again after they also played in the preseason opener against the Steelers.

news.head: Jordan Love (concussion) cleared but will not start Week 18
news.body: Jordan Love has cleared concussion protocol but will not start the Packers' Week 18 matchup against the Vikings as announced by head coach Matt LaFleur and reported by Adam Schefter.
news.impact: Love was a full participant at Wednesday's practice and has cleared concussion protocol, but LaFleur announced that he will be starting Clayton Tune on Sunday in the regular-season finale. With the Packers locked into the seventh-seed in the NFC, Love will get another week to recuperate and get himself ready for the Wild Card round. It's probably best to avoid Green Bay's quarterback and wide receiver situation if your fantasy league is still playing this week.

news.head: Jordan Love to practice Wednesday, remains in concussion protocol
news.body: Jordan Love will practice on Wednesday, but remains in concussion protocol.
news.impact: Packers coach Matt LaFluer confirmed that the Packers plan on resting some of their starters in Week 18. It is unclear if they'll try to get Love in for a quarter or so to knock off some rust after he missed last week.

news.head: Baker Mayfield loses three fumbles Sunday
news.body: Baker Mayfield completed 23-of-28 passes for 216 yards in the Buccaneers 33-27 loss against the Bengals on Sunday.
news.impact: Mayfield did not throw a touchdown or interception, but he did lose three fumbles. He was able to run for 30 yards and a touchdown, but struggled through the air and with ball security. He was playing his first game since landing a three-year extension. He'll look to bounce back against the Browns next week.

news.head: Baker Mayfield signs three-year extension with Bucs
news.body: Baker Mayfield and the Buccaneers reached agreement today on a three-year contract extension.
news.impact: This move comes out of no where as reports suggested talks between the two sides on an extension weren't going to continue this season. Mayfield lands his extension right before the start of the season.

news.head: Baker Mayfield: No immediate plans to re-open contract talks
news.body: Buccaneers GM Jason Licht said there are no immediate plans to re-open contract talks with Baker Mayfield.
news.impact: The expectation was that Mayfield would play this upcoming season on the final year of his contract. This will remain a situation to monitor all year.

news.head: Baker Mayfield expected to play Saturday
news.body: Baker Mayfield is expected to play in Saturday's preseason game against the Kansas City Chiefs.
news.impact: Mayfield was held out of Tampa Bay's first preseason game last week, but it looks like he is going to suit up and play in Saturday's preseason matchup against the Chiefs. It remains to be seen how many snaps the team will let him play, but it remains unlikely that he will see the field for much more than a quarter of the game.

news.head: Jared Goff tosses two touchdowns in Week 1 win over Saints
news.body: Jared Goff completed 26-of-39 pass attempts for 206 yards and two touchdowns while also rushing twice for two yards in the Lions' 31-30 win over the New Orleans Saints in Week 1.
news.impact: Goff took what the New Orleans defense allowed, relying on dynamic running back Jahmyr Gibbs to carry a rusty Detroit starting offense in the Week 1 win. The veteran signal-caller remains a stable mid-tier option with QB1 upside ahead of a Week 2 matchup against the Buffalo Bills.

news.head: Jared Goff will not play Saturday
news.body: Jared Goff will not play in the Lions second preseason game on Saturday against the Commanders.
news.impact: Goff could see some reps in the final preseason game. It will be Josh Dobbs starting with Luke Altmyer seeing reps behind him.

news.head: Jared Goff will not play in preseason opener
news.body: Jared Goff won't be playing in the preseason opener against Cincinnati this week.
news.impact: While Goff won't be playing, head coach Dan Campbell said he may play some starters in the second preseason game against the Commanders.

news.head: Jared Goff restructures contract with Lions
news.body: The Lions restructured QB Jared Goff’s contract.
news.impact: The move allows the Lions to get under the salary cap before Wednesday’s deadline. It lowers Goff’s 2026 salary cap hit from $55 million to just $15 million and adds a void year in 2030.

news.head: Eagles D/ST registers one sack in Week 1
news.body: The Eagles D/ST registered one sack while failing to force any turnovers in a 24-22 win over the Washington Commanders in Week 1.
news.impact: The unit left plenty to be desired in the season-opening win, allowing 296 offensive yards and three touchdowns on the day. The defense will look for more disruptive results for fantasy managers against an underwhelming Tennessee Titans offense in Week 2.

news.head: Eagles D/ST forces two turnovers in Week 18
news.body: The Eagles D/ST allowed 24 points while forcing two turnovers in a 24-17 loss to the Commanders in Week 18.
news.impact: Philadelphia's defense struggled to contain Washington's offense in the loss, although they did manage one interception and recovered one fumble. They will now prepare to face the 49ers at home in the Wild-Card round next week.

news.head: Philadelphia Eagles D/ST comes up clutch against Bills Sunday
news.body: The Philadelphia Eagles D/ST used a dominant first-half performance to hang on for a 13-12 road victory over the Buffalo Bills on Sunday.
news.impact: The Bills had a chance to win at the end of the game but a failed two-point conversion allowed the Eagles to escape with the one-point victory. Philadelphia had five sacks of Josh Allen on the day, at least two of which knocked the Bills out of field goal range. One of the sacks was a fumble recovery that led to an Eagles touchdown. Philadelphia closes out the regular season on Sunday at home against Washington.

news.head: Philadelphia Eagles D/ST contain Washington offense in win
news.body: The Philadelphia Eagles managed two sacks and an interception in the Eagles' 29-18 win over the Commanders.
news.impact: The Eagles defense played better than their fantasy counting stats would suggest. They held the Commanders to just 10 points until garbage time, and frankly, dictated the game for the most part. They'll be tough to trust against a healthy and explosive Buffalo offense next week, however.

news.head: San Fransisco 49ers D/ST shuts down Rams in win
news.body: The San Fransisco 49ers D/ST shut down the Rams offense on Thursday, allowing just seven points in their 27-7 rout of the Super Bowl favorites.
news.impact: The Niners defensive totals were modest, with one interception and a fumble recovery, but were held without a sack. They just kept the Rams from moving the ball while not racking up much in the “counting stats” category. It’s a good showing for the team, and a date with the Dolphins is on tap. They are a great DST option this week if available.

news.head: San Francisco 49ers D/ST does nothing of note Saturday
news.body: The San Francisco 49ers D/ST could muster only two sacks and did not force a turnover during their 13-3 loss to Seattle on Saturday night.
news.impact: Yes, the 49ers only gave up 13 points. But, it could have been much worse as Jason Myers missed two field goals and the Seahawks failed to convert on fourth-and-goal on the game's first drive. Seattle had 361 net yards, including 180 on the ground, and did not turn the ball over against the 49ers defense. That's two straight weeks - and three of the last four - that San Francisco has not forced a turnover.

news.head: 49ers D/ST quiet in Week 17
news.body: The 49ers D/ST failed to register a sack or force a turnover in a 42-38 win over the Bears in Week 17.
news.impact: The unit struggled to keep the Bears from moving the ball, allowing multiple touchdowns on the ground as well as through the air in the win. The defense will look to get back on track in a Week 18 contest against the Seattle Seahawks.

news.head: 49ers D/ST forces two turnovers, scores on INT
news.body: The 49ers D/ST allowed 27 points on 312 yards of total offense, recording two sacks and forcing two turnovers in Monday's win over the Colts.
news.impact: With the offense lighting up the scoreboard for 48 points, the 49ers' defense did not have to do too much Monday night. The 49ers did come up with some big plays, however, including an interception that was returned for a TD as well as a fumble recovery on special teams. The 49ers D/ST has a tricky matchup coming against the Bears in Week 17.

news.head: Patriots D/ST allows 13 points in loss Wednesday
news.body: The Patriots' D/ST logged two sacks and allowed 13 points in Wednesday night's loss to the Seattle Seahawks.
news.impact: New England's defense got a lucky break with QB Sam Darnold (hip) leaving early on in the game. He was replaced by Drew Lock, and while the Patriots held Seattle's offense to just 13 points, that wasn't enough to lead them to a win. This unit should be a decent option against the Steelers in Week 2.

news.head: Patriots D/ST plays well in Week 18 win
news.body: The Patriots' D/ST logged four sacks, one interception, and one fumble recovery in Sunday's 38-10 win over the Miami Dolphins.
news.impact: New England's defense played well on Sunday. They held Miami to just ten points and made a few big plays to help out their offense. This unit has been great over the course of the season and will be a key factor in whether or not they will be able to make a deep push in the playoffs.

news.head: New England Patriots D/ST allows 10 points to Jets Sunday
news.body: The New England Patriots D/ST allowed 307 yards of total offense and only 10 points in a lopsided 42-10 win over the New York Jets on Sunday.
news.impact: The Patriots defense took a back seat to Drake Maye and the New England offense on Sunday. New England had just one sack and forced one turnover against the Jets, but the only real hiccup came on a 59-yard touchdown run by Breece Hall with the game already decided in the fourth quarter. New England closes out the regular season next Sunday against the Dolphins.

news.head: Patriots D/ST allows 24 points in win Sunday
news.body: The Patriots' D/ST logged two fumble recoveries and one sack while allowing 24 points in Sunday night's win over the Baltimore Ravens.
news.impact: New England's defense struggled for much of the game on Sunday, but they were able to step up in the fourth quarter, securing a big fumble recovery to seal the win over the Ravens. This unit projects to be very good over the last couple games of the season with matchups coming up against the Brady Cook-led Jets and the Quinn Ewers-led Dolphins.

news.head: Packers D/ST totals three sacks Sunday
